text:
### Review Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app

1. Select the Campaigns app from the homepage.
2. Search or filter and select the insertion order (IO), then select the campaign. This will open the campaign’s details.
3. Locate the **Creatives** section.
4. Click **View Advanced Modelling**. This will redirect you to the Bid Model app.
5. Select the **Creative** tab.
6. Click **Modeled Creatives**.
7. Locate the **Priority**, **Spend Ratio**, **Spend Ratio Method**, and **Bid Modifier** columns to review the campaign’s Bid Model settings.

### Review Bid Model settings from the Activity Log

The Activity Log records when a user adds or edits a dimension rule across any [Bid Model component](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_ecde5ea44f).

Refer to [Activity Log overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7041034-activity-log-overview) for more details on the types of activities recorded in an Activity Log, and [Manage an Activity Log](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10344379-manage-an-activity-log) for instructions on how to monitor or filter one.

### Edit Bid Model settings

You can edit a campaign’s existing Bid Model settings from the following locations:

- From the Bid Model app
- From the Campaigns app

> **Spend Ratio notice:** When you change an existing Spend Ratio, you must define a Spend Ratio exceeding the amount the campaign has already spent on that dimension value. For example, if a campaign has spent 20% of its budget on ZIP Code A, you can change its Spend Ratio to a value of 21% or higher. For **Bundled** dimensions, the **Bundle’s** Spend Ratio must equal or exceed the total amount the campaign has already spent on its dimensions. Refer to in-platform descriptions for further assistance.

text:
### Edit Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app

1. Follow steps 1-6 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app workflow.
2. Edit the campaign’s Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier settings, as desired.
   1. To update one creative’s Bid Model components at a time, update the **Priority**, **Spend Ratio**, and **Bid Modifier** fields directly.
   2. To update more than one creative’s Bid Model components with the same value, select the checkboxes next to those creatives. Open the **Actions** menu and select **Set Priority**, **Set Spend Ratio** or **Set Bid Modifier**, depending on the desired updates.
3. Edit the applicable field(s), and select **Update Changes**.

You can follow these same steps to edit the Bid Model settings of a **Dimension Bundle**–but you’ll apply your desired changes to the **Bundle’s** top-most row rather than individual dimensions values’ rows.

Your **Bundle**-level or dimension-value-level changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

> **Targeting notice:** There may be certain instances when you’d like for a campaign to stop targeting a dimension that you’ve modeled. You’ll need to delete all Bid Model settings from that dimension before you can remove it from your campaign.

text:
### Delete Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app

1. Follow steps 1-6 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Campaigns app workflow.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to the modeled creative(s) for which you’d like to delete all Bid Model settings.
3. Click **Remove modeling**.
4. Select **Update Changes**.

Refer to Remove all Bid Model settings from a Bundle to complete this process for **Bundled** dimension values, if applicable.

Your changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

### Apply performance filters

You can analyze the performance of your campaign’s modeled and unmodeled Creative dimensions by applying performance filters in the Bid Model app.

Follow these steps to add up to two performance filters:

1. Follow steps 1 through 4 of the Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app workflow.
2. Select the **All Creatives** tab, or select the **Modeled Creatives** tab if you’d only like to apply performance filters to modeled dimension values.
3. Locate the desired metric in the Bid Model table.
   1. You may need to scroll across the table to locate the desired metric column.
4. Click the menu icon next to the metric. This will open the **Set Conditions** pop-up window.
5. The **Metric** menu is pre-populated with the metric you chose. Open the menu and select a different metric, if needed.
6. Open the **Select Condition** menu and choose a data validation rule.
7. Enter the desired value into the **Enter Value** field.
   1. The value type will automatically change based on the metric type you selected (e.g., numerical value, percentage value, etc.)
8. If desired, click **+ Add Condition** to apply one additional performance filter.
9. Choose whether you’d like to apply an “OR” or “AND” relationship between these filters.
   1. “AND” will display a dimension value if it meets both of the metric conditions you’ve set. “OR” will display a dimension value if it meets either of the conditions you’ve set.
10. Repeat steps 5 through 7 to enter your desired metric, condition, and value.
11. Select **Save** to apply the performance filter(s).

The Bid Model table will automatically update based on the performance filter(s) you added. Any filtered metrics will show a blue circle near its menu icon to indicate that you’ve set a condition related to that metric. You can Remove performance filters at any time.

text:
### Remove performance filters

You can change or remove performance filters at any time.

Follow these steps to remove them:

1. Locate the desired metric in the Bid Model table.
   1. You may need to scroll across the table to locate the desired metric column.
2. Click the menu icon next to the metric. This will open the **Set Conditions** pop-up window.
3. To remove one condition, select the trashcan icon next to it.
4. To remove all conditions, select **Clear All**.
5. Click **Save** to apply your changes.

text:
## Bid Model overview

A Bid Model is an optimization tool that you can control to adjust bids, allocate budgets, and shift priorities to optimize campaign performance.

Certain factors, such as eligibility requirements, differ based on the individual [Bid Model component](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview#h_ecde5ea44f) that you define for a campaign. Refer to these resources before beginning the process of applying a Bid Model setting to an Inventory dimension:

- [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview)
- [Spend Ratio overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview)
- [Priority overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-dimension-priority-overview)
- [Bid Modifier overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview)

In this article, you’ll learn how to apply a Bid Model setting (Spend Ratio, Priority, Bid Modifier) to an Inventory dimension. You can also add Bid Model settings to Creative, Location, and Device dimensions. Refer to these resources for more details:

- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Creative dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300515-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-creative-dimension-category#h_4d1afe92b4)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Location dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9300472-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-location-dimension)
- [Apply a Bid Model setting to a Device dimension category](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12081845-apply-a-bid-model-setting-to-a-device-dimension-category#h_53d25f0e14)

text:
## Apply Bid Model settings

> **Dimension category notice:** Bid Modeling can be applied to one Inventory dimension at a time. This means that you can apply Bid Model settings to either the Open Exchange, Deal ID, or Publisher Category Inventory dimensions—not a combination of them.

You can add Bid Model settings to one campaign at a time, and in the following ways:

- From the Bid Model app
- From the Campaigns app
- From the Dashboard app

section_path: Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app

text:
### Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app

1. Select the Bid Model app.
2. Choose whether the campaign is **Running**, **Paused**, **Pending**, **Paused**, **Rejected**, or a **Draft** from the status dropdown menu.
3. Search and select the campaign for which you want to apply Bid Model settings.
   1. A campaign or IO is searchable from the **Select Campaign** field when two criteria are met: it is eligible for Bid Modeling, and its status matches the one you chose in step 2.
4. Expand the **Inventory** menu.
5. Choose **Deal ID**, **Open Exchange**, or **Publisher Category** depending on the dimensions for which you want to apply Bid Model settings.
6. In the **All Deal IDs**, **All Open Exchanges**, or **All Publisher Categories** tab, click the checkbox(es) next to the desired dimension(s).
7. Select **+ Add to Modeling**.
8. Select the **Modeled Deal IDs**, **Modeled Open Exchanges**, or **Modeled Publisher Categories** tab, depending on the dimensions you selected.

article_title: Apply a Bid Model setting to an Inventory dimension category
section_path: Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app
context_header: Apply a Bid Model setting to an Inventory dimension category › Apply Bid Model settings › Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app
text:
### Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app

8. Select the **Modeled Deal IDs**, **Modeled Open Exchanges**, or **Modeled Publisher Categories** tab, depending on the dimensions you selected.
9. To apply a Spend Ratio to these Inventory dimensions:
   1. Locate the **Spend Ratio Method** column and choose **Flexible** or **Strict**.
      1. Refer to [Spend Ratio overview - Key terms and concepts](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview#h_bf06d4b3a1) for more information on these options. Note that Priorities are required for any items featuring a **Flexible** Spend Ratio.
   2. Locate the **Spend Ratio** column and enter a percentage from 0% to 100% for each dimension value.
      1. The percentages must equal 100% if the Spend Ratio is **Strict**, and can equal or exceed 100% if it’s **Flexible**.
   3. Select **Update Changes** to apply the settings.
10. To apply a Priority to these Inventory dimensions:
    1. Locate the **Priority** column.
    2. Add a priority ranging from 1 to 10 for each dimension value, with smaller numbers indicating a higher priority, and larger numbers indicating a lower priority.
    3. Refer to steps 9a-9b to apply Spend Ratios to these dimension values. A **Flexible** Spend Ratio is required for any dimension values that are assigned a Priority.
    4. Select **Update Changes**.
11. To apply a Bid Modifier to these Inventory dimension values:
    1. Locate the **Bid Modifier** column.
    2. Enter a **Base Bid Price** for the campaign.
    3. Add a multiplier between 0.1X and 100X for each desired dimension value.
       1. 1X indicates that you want the Inventory dimension to observe the campaign’s Base Bid Price. Numbers below 1X indicate that you want to pay less than the campaign’s Base Bid Price, and numbers above 1X indicate that you want to pay more than the campaign’s Base Bid Price for that dimension value.
    4. Select **Update Changes**.

The Spend Ratios, Priorities, and/or Bid Modifiers will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

> **Bulk operations:** Steps 9, 10, and 11 share how to apply Bid Model settings one by one. To apply the same Bid Model setting to multiple dimension values, use bulk operations instead. Select the checkbox next to those dimension values; open the **Actions** menu; and select **Spend Ratio**, **Priority**, or **Bid Modifier** to enter your preferred settings.

> **More on Bundles:** A **Bundle** is a feature that you’ll use to manage the Bid Model settings of two or more dimension values from the same dimension. Note that all dimension values in a **Bundle** will take on the Bid Model settings that you apply at the **Bundle** level. text:
### Save dimension values to a Bundle

Follow these steps to save one or more dimension values to a new or existing **Bundle**:

1. Select the **All Deal IDs**, **All Open Exchanges**, or **All Publisher Categories** tab; or the **Modeled Deal IDs**, **Modeled Open Exchanges**, or **Modeled Publisher Categories** tab.
2. Click the checkbox(es) next to the desired dimension value(s).
3. Select **Save To Bundle**. This will open the **Bundle Deal IDs**, **Bundle Open Exchanges**, or **Bundle Publisher Categories** pop-up window, depending on the type of dimension value(s) you chose.
4. To add the dimension values to a new bundle:
   1. Click **New Bundle**.
   2. Enter a unique name for the **Bundle** to differentiate it from others that you may create.
5. To add the dimension values to an existing **Bundle**:
   1. Click **Existing Bundle**.
   2. Open the **Bundle Name** menu and select the desired **Bundle**.
6. Select **Save**.

The **Bundle** “shell” will feature a dedicated row in the Bid Model table, with each bundled dimension value nested below it.

1. Follow steps 1-7 of the Review Bid Model settings from the Bid Model app workflow.
2. Edit the campaign’s Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier settings, as desired.
   1. To update one dimension value’s Bid Model components at a time, update the **Priority**, **Spend Ratio**, and **Bid Modifier** fields directly.
   2. To update more than one dimension values’ Bid Model components with the same value, select the checkboxes next to those items. Open the **Actions** menu and select **Set Priority**, **Set Spend Ratio** or **Set Bid Modifier**, depending on the desired updates.
3. Edit the applicable field(s) and select **Update Changes**.

You can follow these same steps to edit the Bid Model settings of a **Dimension Bundle**–but you’ll apply your desired changes to the **Bundle’s** top-most row rather than individual dimension values’ rows.

Your **Bundle**-level or dimension-value-level changes will typically apply to the campaign within the next hour.

text:
### Apply performance filters

You can analyze the performance of your campaign’s modeled and unmodeled Inventory dimension values by applying performance filters in the Bid Model app.

Follow these steps to add up to two performance filters:

1. Follow steps 1 through 5 of the Add a Spend Ratio, Priority, and/or Bid Modifier from the Bid Model app workflow.
2. Select the **All Deal ID, Open Exchange, Publisher Category)** tab, or select the **Modeled (Deal ID, Open Exchange, Publisher Category)** tab if you’d only like to apply performance filters to modeled dimension values.
3. Locate the desired metric in the Bid Model table.
   1. You may need to scroll across the table to locate the desired metric column.
4. Click the menu icon next to the metric. This will open the **Set Conditions** pop-up window.
5. The **Metric** menu is pre-populated with the metric you chose. Open the menu and select a different metric, if needed.
6. Open the **Select Condition** menu and choose a data validation rule.
7. Enter the desired value into the **Enter Value** field.
   1. The value type will automatically change based on the metric type you selected (e.g., numerical value, percentage value, etc.)
8. If desired, click **+ Add Condition** to apply one additional performance filter.
9. Choose whether you’d like to apply an “OR” or “AND” relationship between these filters.
   1. “AND” will display a dimension value if it meets both of the metric conditions you’ve set. “OR” will display a dimension value if it meets either of the conditions you’ve set.
10. Repeat steps 5 through 7 to enter your desired metric, condition, and value.
11. Select **Save** to apply the performance filter(s).

The Bid Model table will automatically update based on the performance filter(s) you added. Any filtered metrics will show a blue circle near its menu icon to indicate that you’ve set a condition related to that metric. You can Remove performance filters at any time.

### Remove performance filters

You can change or remove performance filters at any time.

Follow these steps to remove them:

1. Locate the desired metric in the Bid Model table.
   1. You may need to scroll across the table to locate the desired metric column.
2. Click the menu icon next to the metric. This will open the **Set Conditions** pop-up window.
3. To remove one condition, select the trashcan icon next to it.
4. To remove all conditions, select **Clear All**.
5. Click **Save** to apply your changes.

text:
## PMP inventory deal overview

> **More on PMP inventory targeting:** Consider creating a PMP inventory group if you plan to target or block the same group of PMP deals across multiple campaigns. Refer to [Inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview) for more details, and review [Create or manage an inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9616211-create-or-manage-an-inventory-group) for step-by-step instructions.

Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory deals are used to purchase ad inventory through a private, invitation-only auction. Unlike Open Exchange inventory, PMP deals provide more control and access to more premium inventory.

In this article, you’ll learn how to add your PMP deals to the IQM platform. Refer to [Assign Private Marketplace (PMP) deals or inventory groups to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615727-assign-private-marketplace-pmp-deals-or-inventory-groups-to-a-campaign) when you’re ready to choose which campaigns will target or block those deals.

text:
## Create a PMP inventory deal

You can add a PMP inventory deal to the IQM platform in the following ways:

- From the Inventory app
- From the Campaigns app - Existing campaign
- From the Campaigns app - New campaign

article_title: Create or manage a Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory deal
context_header: Create or manage a Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory deal › Create a PMP inventory deal › Inventory app
text:
### Inventory app

Follow these steps to add a new PMP inventory deal to the Inventory app:

1. Open the Inventory app.
2. Select the **PMP** tab.
3. Click **+ Add Deal**. This will open the **Add Deal** pop-up window.
4. Enter the unique **Deal ID** provided by the supply-side platform (SSP) or publisher partner.
5. Enter a **Deal Name** to help you identify this deal in the IQM platform.
6. Select the one **Exchange** in which the auction for the PMP inventory deal will take place.
7. Choose whether the current **Deal Status** is **Active** or **Inactive**.
   1. Campaigns can target or block only **Active** PMP inventory deals.
8. If desired, complete the optional **Creative Types**, **CPM**, and/or **Description** fields.
   1. **CPM** refers to the CPM information provided by the SSP or publisher, which you can store within this deal for reference. The CPM value you enter won’t be used in auctions.
9. Select **Add** to finish adding the new PMP inventory deal to the Inventory app.

text:
### Campaigns app - Existing campaign

Follow these steps to add a new PMP inventory deal from a campaign that you’ve already created:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Choose an insertion order (IO), then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one for which you want to add the deal.
3. Locate the **Campaign Name** column and click the campaign’s name. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add or update its details and targeting parameters.
4. Expand the **Inventory** section.
5. Select **PMP Deals**.
6. Click **+ Add Deal**. This will open the **Add Deal** pop-up window.
7. Follow steps 4 through 9 of the Inventory app workflow.
   1. The deal(s) will appear in a **PMP Deals** subsection of the campaign.
8. Select **Save** to apply your changes to the existing campaign.

text:
### Campaigns app - New campaign

Follow these steps to add a new PMP inventory deal to a new campaign from the Campaigns app:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Click on the name of the desired insertion order (IO).
3. Select **+ Create Campaign**. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add its details and targeting parameters.
4. Expand the **Inventory** section.
5. Select **PMP Deals**.
6. Click **+ Add Deal**. This will open the **Add Deal** pop-up window.
7. Follow steps 4 through 9 of the Inventory app workflow.
   1. The deal(s) will appear in a **PMP Deals** subsection of the campaign
8. Select **Save as Draft** to apply your changes to the campaign in a draft format or click **Run** to create the campaign if you’ve completed all other required and applicable sections.

### Edit a PMP inventory deal

You can edit one PMP inventory deal at a time. Follow these steps to apply changes to a PMP inventory deal from the Inventory app:

1. Select the **PMP** tab in the Inventory app.
2. Search, filter, or browse the deals to locate the one you want to edit.
3. Select the checkbox next to the deal.
4. Click **Edit**. This will open the **Edit Deal** pop-up window.
5. Apply your desired changes.
   1. In certain cases, the **Deal Status** field may be uneditable. You can change the status of a deal from **Active** to **Inactive** only when the deal isn’t currently assigned to any campaigns. Those campaigns are listed in the table toward the bottom of the **Edit Deal** pop-up window.

context_header: Inventory groups overview › Inventory groups overview
text:
## Inventory groups overview

An inventory group is a collection of inventory sources. The collection is categorized based on specific criteria such as ad format, placement type, or other relevant attributes that each inventory source has in common. You’ll group inventory when you want to target or block the same set of inventory across multiple campaigns to streamline your operations and manage your campaigns effectively.

Create and target custom Open Exchange, CTV, PMP, or Contextual inventory groups; or take advantage of Curated inventory groups.

context_header: Inventory groups overview › Inventory groups overview › Open Exchange inventory groups
text:
### Open Exchange inventory groups

Open Exchange inventory is available to all bidders in a programmatic auction. This “raw” inventory is listed in the Inventory app for targeting individually, or for targeting via groups that you form based on shared characteristics.

When you create an Open Exchange inventory group, you specify criteria such as where you want the ads to be published (countries, device types), which SSPs you’d like to target inventory from, what device types you’d like to serve on, and more. Consolidate the inventory of your choice into a single collection, then target or block the group across multiple campaigns. Refer to [Create or manage an inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9616211-create-or-manage-an-inventory-group) for more details and step-by-step instructions.

context_header: Inventory groups overview › Inventory groups overview › Connected TV (CTV) inventory groups
text:
### Connected TV (CTV) inventory groups

CTV inventory is purchased via the Open Exchange. CTV inventory includes ads served on internet-connected TVs via built-in functions (smart TV) or external hardware (streaming player, step-top box, game console). It may include both OEM surfaces and streaming app environments.

CTV groups consolidate the CTV inventory of your choice into a single collection, which you can easily target or block across multiple campaigns. Refer to [Create or manage an inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9616211-create-or-manage-an-inventory-group) for more details and step-by-step instructions.

context_header: Inventory groups overview › Inventory groups overview
text:
### Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory groups

Private Marketplace (PMP) deals are used to purchase ad inventory through a private, invitation-only auction. Unlike Open Exchange inventory, PMP deals provide more control and premium inventory.

PMP groups consolidate the PMP deals of your choice into a single collection. Target or block this same group of PMP deals across multiple campaigns. Refer to [Create or manage an inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9616211-create-or-manage-an-inventory-group) for more details and step-by-step instructions.

### Contextual inventory groups

> **More on contextual targeting:** Targeting contextual inventory is one way to reach users based on a site’s keywords or URL. Targeting contextual audiences is another way. These audiences are formed by grouping users together based on their online activity. You determine these groups by indicating a list of relevant keywords and/or URLs and a timeframe. We add a user to the contextual audience when they visit sites that feature those keywords or URLs, browse them during the time period you select, and meet any other parameters that you specify during audience setup. Refer to [Contextual audience overview](https://intercom.help/IQM-Corp/en/articles/6972375-contextual-audience-overview) for more information.

Contextual inventory groups rely on contextual signals to target ads based on the content of a webpage or a given URL. Delivering ads alongside relevant content helps ensure alignment with users’ interest and intent, and can lead to higher engagement.

When you create a contextual inventory group, you specify the specific keywords and/or URLs that you’d like to target, then add the group to a campaign. Refer to [Create or manage an inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9616211-create-or-manage-an-inventory-group) for more details and step-by-step instructions.

context_header: Inventory groups overview › Inventory groups overview › Curated inventory groups
text:
### Curated inventory groups

Unlike custom Open Exchange, PMP, and Contextual inventory groups, Curated inventory groups are readily available. They include collections of inventory that are grouped based on device type and content-subject-matter categories.

Refer to [Curated inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8797253-curated-inventory-groups-overview#h_9c1dfdaf7d) for more information, including how to access and target these groups.

text:
## Inventory overview

After you create a Private Marketplace (PMP) deal or inventory group on the IQM platform, you’ll choose which campaigns will target it. This article outlines how to assign an existing deal or group to a campaign, or remove one that you’ve previously assigned.

Review these resources first if you’d like to create a new PMP deal or inventory group:

- [Create or manage a Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory deal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9613510-create-or-manage-a-private-marketplace-pmp-inventory-deal)
- [Create or manage an inventory group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9616211-create-or-manage-an-inventory-group)

Note that PMP deal and inventory group targeting are optional, and that you can also Target exchanges or publisher categories directly from a campaign, if desired.

article_title: Assign Private Marketplace (PMP) deals or inventory groups to a campaign
section_path: Assign an inventory group to a campaign
context_header: Assign Private Marketplace (PMP) deals or inventory groups to a campaign › Assign an inventory group to a campaign
text:
## Assign an inventory group to a campaign

> **More on inventory groups:** In addition to the inventory groups you create yourself, you can take advantage of curated inventory groups and assign them to your campaigns. These groups are segmented by inventory that’s available on specific devices and belonging to particular content categories. Refer to [Curated inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8797253-curated-inventory-groups-overview) for more information on available inventory group types and inventory sources.

You can assign up to 250 custom or curated inventory groups to existing campaigns from the Inventory or Campaigns apps, or to new campaigns from the Campaigns app.

- From the Inventory app - Existing campaign
- From the Inventory app - New campaign
- From the Campaigns app - Existing campaign
- From the Campaigns app - New campaign

Adding an inventory group to a campaign’s Allowlist means that the platform will target only the inventory in the specified group. Adding inventory to a Blocklist, however, means the platform will bid on all other inventory except the inventory included in the group. Refer to [Allowlist and Blocklist overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10472012-allowlist-and-blocklist-overview) for more information on how campaign targeting works.

### Inventory app - Existing campaign

Follow these steps to assign inventory groups to campaigns that you’ve already created:

1. Open the Inventory app.
2. Select the **Groups** tab.
3. Select the checkbox(es) next to the desired inventory group(s).
4. Click **Assign to Campaign**. This will open the **Assign To Campaigns** pop-up window.
5. Open the **Campaigns** menu to search and select the desired campaign(s).
   1. Campaigns featuring a Draft, Pending, Running, or Paused status are eligible.
6. In the **Allowlist/Blocklist** column, choose whether the group you selected should be targeted (Allowlist) or excluded (Blocklist) by a given campaign.
7. Select **Update** to apply your changes.

2. Click **Create Campaign**. This will open the **Create Campaign** pop-up window.
3. Choose an existing insertion order (IO).
4. Enter a name for the new campaign.
5. The **Advanced** campaign type is selected by default for all inventory groups.
   1. Refer to [Advanced versus PG campaigns](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_97e6822e53) for more details.
6. Click **Create**.

You’ll be automatically redirected to the campaign details page for the new campaign, where you can manage its settings.

2. Choose an insertion order (IO), then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one for which you want to target an inventory group.

7. Search or browse and select the desired group(s).
   1. Filter the available groups by group type (Open Exchange, CTV, PMP, Contextual), if desired.

text:
### Campaigns app - New campaign

Follow these steps to assign inventory groups to a new campaign:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Click on the name of the desired insertion order (IO).
3. Select **+ Create Campaign**. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add its details and targeting parameters.
4. Expand the **Inventory** section.
5. Select **Inventory Groups**.

   1. Filter the available groups by group type (Open Exchange, CTV, PMP, Contextual), if desired.
8. Click **Select**. This will add the group(s) to an **Inventory Groups** subsection of the campaign.
9. Save your changes.
   1. Click **Save as Draft** to apply your changes to the campaign in a draft format.
   2. Click **Run** to create the campaign if you’ve completed all other required and applicable sections.

text:
## Inventory group overview

Inventory groups are collections of inventory that you categorize based on a set of criteria such as ad format, placement type, targeting options, or other attributes. In this article, you’ll learn how to create Open Exchange, Connected TV (CTV), Private Marketplace (PMP), or Contextual [inventory groups](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-what-is-an-inventory-group) in the IQM platform. Refer to Assign an inventory group to a campaign when you’re ready to target an existing group.

In addition to the inventory groups you create yourself, you can take advantage of curated inventory groups and assign them to your campaigns. These groups are segmented by inventory that’s available on specific devices and belonging to particular content categories. Review [Curated inventory groups overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8797253-curated-inventory-groups-overview) for more information on available inventory group types and inventory sources.

article_title: Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report overview
context_header: Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report overview › VLD report overview
text:
## VLD report overview

The Voter Level Data (VLD) report surfaces insights about users you targeted in current or prior political campaigns. It includes ad exposure and engagement data, demographic data, and voting-history details, by voter. Generate and apply these insights to improve current and future campaigns, strengthen your brand’s messaging across channels, and create segmented audience strategies, for example.

You can generate a VLD report if your campaigns and account meet certain criteria. Refer to the VLD report eligibility requirements and considerations section for more information.

> **More on voting data and VLD report insights**
> Like your favorite brands tailor their marketing strategies based on their end users’ demographics and interests, political advertisers use voting data to tailor their political campaigns. Voting data is public, and nonprofit companies are exempt, meaning they can use this data without consent from consumers. The insights we generate for and include in VLD reports are non-sensitive.

article_title: Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report overview
context_header: Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report overview › VLD report eligibility requirements
text:
## VLD report eligibility requirements

If you are a political advertiser and have signed IQM’s master service agreement (MSA), you may be eligible to generate a VLD report.

Other VLD report requirements include:

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| **Campaign vertical** | Political* |
| **Campaign status** | Running Expired (within the past two years) Paused |
| **Campaign duration** | 3 or more days |
| **Campaign creation date** | September 16, 2024 or later (or earlier upon request to IQM's support team) |
| **Voter location** | All US states except Oregon** |
| **Audience type***** | [Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651480-selecting-a-matched-audience) created from L2 IDs [Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651480-selecting-a-matched-audience) created from raw data**** |

***Political:** Any campaign created under a political advertiser account is a “Political” campaign.

****Voter location:** Due to privacy laws in the state of Oregon, we are unable to generate the VLD Insights Report on any voters located there. Contact your account representative for more detailed information on the legality of reidentifying voters at the user level.

*****Audience type:** Your campaign must only include the audience types listed in this requirements table. For example, you cannot generate a VLD report for a campaign if it includes a Matched Audience created from L2 IDs and a Retargeted Audience consisting of your website’s past visitors.

******Raw data:** The VLD report supports audiences you create using First Name, Last Name, Address, and Phone Number. IQM anonymizes the data in the matching process, encrypts the files, and stores them behind a firewall to protect them against information leaks.

article_title: Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report overview
context_header: Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report overview › VLD Insights reporting method
text:
## VLD Insights reporting method

We take seven steps to transform your customer data into VLD insights:

1. Your customer data is uploaded to Amazon S3 Storage, IQM’s secure, cloud-based storage solution.
2. IQM’s processing environment ingests and pseudonymizes consumer data before matching it with L2 partner data, which is also also pseudonymized.
   1. When data is pseudonymised, it’s been de-identified, but the process can be reversed. This means the data can be re-identified. When data is anonymized, it’s been charged in such a way that re-identification is impossible.
   2. Because of our direct relationship with L2 Data, the linkage between L2 ID and the customer’s pseudonymized data is maintained. That linked data, along with Target IDs (MAIDs, Cookies, and RampID) forms our proprietary Voter ID Graph.
3. Matched and pseudonymized data is anonymized for targeting.
4. Anonymized data is segmented and ready for activation within your digital campaigns.
5. As the campaign serves impressions, Target IDs are collected and added into IQM’s Voter ID graph.
6. The graph is used to reverse-map matched and pseudonimized data to L2’s Voter ID.
7. IQM generates your VLD Insights report, tying ad exposure and engagement to L2’s Voter ID.

The VLD Insights report may only be utilized with L2 data. You can either bring a list of L2 IDs to target, or submit your CRM data containing First Name, Last Name, Home Address, and Phone Number. We’ll match that data to L2 IDs for targeting.

article_title: Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report overview
context_header: Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report overview › VLD report pricing
text:
## VLD report pricing

There is a cost associated with generating a VLD report. You can reference the VLD report price after you enter key details–like the campaign’s total number of impressions and date range–and before you generate the report. We calculate these impressions on a CPM basis.

Refer to the [Generate or manage a Voter Level Data (VLD)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9827401-generate-or-manage-a-voter-level-data-vld-report) report page for more information on where to reference the report-price preview.

article_title: Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report overview
context_header: Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report overview › VLD report pricing › Report price surcharges
text:
### Report price surcharges

Agencies with workspace permissions can apply a markup to IQM’s VLD rate for individual advertisers. These surcharges can use either a percentage- or rate-based markup.

When you apply a markup, we’ll show advertisers a consolidated “VLD Insights Cost.” Here’s how it’s calculated:

Follow these steps to apply a **VLD Rate Markup** to an advertiser in the **Customers** app:

1. Go to the **Customers** app and select the **Finance** tab.
2. Locate and select the advertiser for which you'd like to apply the surcharge.
3. In the **Voter Level Data Rate** section, choose whether you'd like to add an **Absolute** markup or **Percentage** markup.
   1. An **Absolute** markup is a dollar amount, while the **Percentage** markup is a percentage of the listed IQM VLD rate.
4. Enter your markup value or percentage, and select the checkmark icon to confirm your selection.

article_title: Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report overview
context_header: Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report overview › VLD report pricing
text:
### Price deduction - Sufficient funds

The workflow to generate a VLD report ends with a **Generate** button that you can use to create your report. We will deduct the **VLD Insights Cost** from your account’s available balance immediately after you select this button in the **Generate VLD** widget.

### Price deduction - Insufficient funds

> Organization administrators can add funds to an account. Contact yours to complete this process.

The workflow to generate a VLD report ends with a **Generate** button that you can use to create your report. If your account’s available balance is less than the **VLD Insights Cost**, then this button will prompt you to add funds to your account instead. We will redirect you to enter a fund amount and select a payment method when you click **Add Funds**.

context_header: Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report overview › VLD report pricing › Pricing for VLD reports with overlapping datasets
text:
### Pricing for VLD reports with overlapping datasets

There may be instances when you generate multiple VLD reports with partially overlapping date ranges for the same campaign. This means that the insight data also overlaps. You will pay only once for VLD insights for each date.

**Example:** You generate two reports for the same campaign–one with a date range of August 1st-10th, and another with a date range of August 5th-20th. Since you already paid for the insights from August 1st-10th, we will only change you for a portion of the second report: the new data generated for the August 11th-20th date range. We will still aggregate data from the full August 5th-20th date range in the second report.

article_title: Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report overview
context_header: Voter Level Data (VLD) Insights report overview › VLD report metrics
text:
## VLD report metrics

VLD reports return ad exposure metrics (Impressions, Clicks, Conversions) at a user level. If you used L2 data for audience creation, you can also reference each user’s L2 ID and multiple demographic data points.

| **Metric title** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| **Impressions** | The number of times the user viewed your ad. |
| **Clicks** | The number of times the user clicked on your ad. |
| **Conversions** | The number of a user’s conversions that can be attributed to your ad. |
| **L2 ID** | The user’s L2 ID, which is available when your campaign includes a matched audience that uses L2 IDs. |
| **First Name** | The user's legal first name. |
| **Middle Name** | The user's legal middle name. |
| **Last Name** | The user's legal last name. |
| **Address** | The user’s permanent residence location details. |
| **ZIP Code** | The user’s permanent residence location details. |
| **State** | The user’s permanent residence location details. |
| **Phone 1, Phone 2** | The user’s primary and/or secondary phone number(s). |
| **Registration status** | “Active” or “Not Active” depending on the user’s current voter registration status. |
| **Age** | The user's age. |
| **Gender** | “M” for “Male” or “F” for “Female” based on a user’s legal sex. |
| **Marital Status** | “Single,” “Married,” “Divorced,” or “Widowed” depending on the user’s current legal marital status. |
| **Net Worth** | The total value of the user’s assets once their liabilities and debts are subtracted. |
| **Home Owner** | “Yes” or “No” depending on the user’s home ownership status. |
| **Income** | The money the user earns on an annual basis. |
| **Education** | The extent of formal, certified instruction that the user has completed. |
| **Presidential_primary_2000 (2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020, etc.)** | “Y” or “N” depending on the user’s voting status during this election type and cycle. |
| **General_2023_11_07 (2022_11_08, etc.)** | Y” or “N” depending on the user’s voting status during this election type and cycle. |

## VLD report statuses

You can review a VLD report’s current status on the **Voter Level Data** page.

| **Status** | **Definition** |
| --- | --- |
| **Ready** | Your insights are generated. You can view, download, or email the VLD report. |
| **Processing** | We are working on generating your insights. Check back in about 15 minutes. |
| **Failed*** | You either encountered a technical error during report generation, or the campaign you selected is no longer eligible for VLD insights. Try again in a few minutes to rule out a technical error. |

* If a VLD report features a **Failed** status, we will credit the cost to your account immediately.

text:
### Generate a VLD Insights report from the Insights app

Follow these steps to access the **+ Generate New** workflow:

1. Open the Insights app.
2. Select **Voter Level Data**.
3. Click **+ Generate New**. This will open the **Generate Voter Level Data** pop-up window.
4. Choose whether the campaign is **Running**, **Paused**, or **Expired** from the **Campaign Status** menu.
5. Search and select the campaign for which you want to generate insights.
   1. Search for the campaign’s name or ID, or the Insertion Order’s (IO) name or ID.
   2. If a desired campaign or IO is missing from the list, its status doesn’t match the **Campaign Status** you selected and/or it isn’t eligible for VLD Insights generation.
6. Select a date range from the **Date Range** field.
   1. Date ranges use the same time zone as the location where the campaign was initially created.
7. Click **Next**.
8. Review your campaign selection, and a summary of the report’s chargeable impressions and the associated cost.
   1. We calculate the **VLD Insights Price** based on the number of impressions that your campaign or IO delivered during the specified date range at a CPM rate.
9. Select **Previous** to change the report’s settings, if desired.
10. Click **Generate** to create the VLD Insights report.
    1. The **VLD Insight Price** is deducted from your account’s available balance immediately after you select this button.

VLD reports are typically ready within 15 minutes. Once generated, you can find the VLD insights on the Insights app’s **Voter Level Data** page. Review Manage a VLD report for details on how to review, download, or delete a report.

### Download a VLD Insights report

1. Filter or search the table to locate the desired report.
2. Open the **Download** menu in the **Actions** column.

text:
### Review campaign eligibility criteria

If you are in the **Insights** app, the **Campaign** field in the **Generate Voter Level Data** pop-up window only includes campaigns that are eligible for VLD report creation.

If you are in the **Campaigns** or **Dashboard** app, the option to generate a VLD report is only available for eligible campaigns.

Refer to the [Voter Level Data (VLD) report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9827089-voter-level-data-vld-insights-report-overview) page for more information on the factors that make you or your campaign eligible for VLD insights.

### Check the campaign’s current status

If you are generating a VLD report in the **Insights** app, you are first prompted to select the campaign’s current status from the **Campaign Status** drop-down menu. This selection narrows the available **Campaign** field options to those with that status. For example, if you choose **Expired**, we will only make eligible campaigns with an **Expired** status searchable in the **Campaign** field.

Check the campaign’s current status and update the **Campaign Status** field accordingly, if applicable.

To help reduce user errors next time, consider generating a VLD report from the **Campaigns** or **Dashboard** apps. Unlike VLD report creation via the **Insights** app, these two workflows will pre-populate the **Campaign Status**, **Campaign**, and **Date Range** fields during setup. Refer to the [Generate or manage a Voter Level Data (VLD) report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9827401-generate-or-manage-a-voter-level-data-vld-insights-report) article for more information on how to generate a VLD report from the **Campaigns** or **Dashboard** apps.

text:
## VLD report creation - Cannot generate a report

You may encounter a warning message or another issue that blocks you from generating VLD data from a particular campaign and across a particular date range. We build in certain blocks to help avoid charging you for highly similar datasets more than once, or generating reports inaccurately.

These blocks typically occur for one of the following reasons:

1. You can generate one VLD report at a time for each campaign.
   1. You can generate another VLD report once your in-progress report displays a **Ready** status on the **Voter Level Data** page. Refer to the [Generate or manage a Voter Level Data (VLD) report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9827401-generate-or-manage-a-voter-level-data-vld-insights-report) page to learn how to access this page.
2. You can generate one VLD report total when you choose the same report dates for the same campaign.
   1. The **Generate** option will not be available in the **Generate Voter Level Data** widget. Instead, you can review the VLD report you already generated for this campaign and date range.

There may be certain cases where you’ve previously generated VLD reports, but your access is now revoked. For example, your signed MSA for VLD Insights reporting may have expired. You won’t be able to generate new insights, but you can continue to access reports you’ve already generated for three years after their creation date, in alignment with the IQM platform data-retention policy.

text:
## Pre-bid audience targeting overview

Pre-bid audiences are groups of fraud and invalid traffic (IVT), brand suitability, viewability, and supply refinement pre-bid segments that you select. You can create these audiences and seamlessly integrate them into new or existing campaigns.

The IQM platform supports targeting individual pre-bid segments or Pre-bid audiences. We recommend creating a Pre-bid audience when you plan to target the same set of pre-bid segments across multiple campaigns. You can add the audience to a campaign instead of manually selecting the individual segments each time.

Review [Create or manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience) to learn how to create a Pre-bid audience, then return to this article when you’re ready to add one to a new or existing campaign.

text:
### From the Campaigns app - New campaign

Follow these steps to assign a Pre-bid audience or individual Pre-bid segments to a new campaign from the Campaigns app:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Choose an Insertion Order (IO) to arrive at the **Insertion Order Info** page.
3. Click **+ Create Campaign**. You’ll be redirected to a form for the new campaign, where you can add or update its details and targeting parameters.
4. Locate and expand the **Pre-bid Audience** section.
5. To choose an existing audience, open the **Select Audiences** menu and click the audience’s name.
6. To choose individual segments:
   1. Click **+ Add Pre-bid Segments**.
   2. Search or browse and select the desired segments.
7. Review and manage the segments you added.
   1. Each provider, segment category, CPM price, and individual segment will appear in the table.
   2. If desired, click the trashcan icon next to any segments you’d like to remove from the campaign.
      1. The original Pre-bid audience that includes the segments won’t be impacted. If you’d like to update the Pre-bid audience to ensure that any changes are saved, refer to [Manage a Pre-bid audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8698628-create-or-manage-a-pre-bid-audience#h_a0f76c937c) for step-by-step instructions.
8. If desired, save your campaign’s targeting settings as a new [campaign template](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign#h_49ff912ba6).
9. Save your changes.
   1. Click **Save as Draft** to apply your selections in a draft format.
   2. Click **Run** to apply your selections and create the campaign.

Refer to the [Campaign Targeting Guide](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide) for additional support with completing the campaign’s other required and applicable fields.

article_title: Import an audience from the L2 DataMapping platform
context_header: Import an audience from the L2 DataMapping platform › L2 audience import overview
text:
## L2 audience import overview

IQM partners with data provider “L2” to offer comprehensive voter and constituent targeting solutions. Our direct integrations allow you to export audiences directly from the L2 platform and import them into the IQM platform. You can manage these audiences in the **Audiences** app, or add them directly to your campaigns.

article_title: Import an audience from the L2 DataMapping platform
context_header: Import an audience from the L2 DataMapping platform › Import an L2 audience
text:
### Prepare to import an L2 audience

You’ll need these three items before you can import an L2 audience:

1. An L2 platform account login.
2. Your IQM account ID.
3. The segment name.

Follow these steps to locate your IQM account ID:

1. Select **My Profile** from the IQM homepage.
2. Click **Organizations**.
3. Locate the code listed in the **ID** field.

### Send universe

Follow these steps to send an audience from the L2 platform to your account on the IQM platform:

1. Navigate to the [L2 DataMapping](https://www.l2datamapping.com/account/login?&r0=/) platform (external link) and log into your account.
2. Search for and select the audience you’d like to send to the IQM platform.
3. Locate the **SOURCE** category.
4. Select the **+** icon next to the **Universes** dropdown menu to create a new universe.
5. Enter a name for the universe using the following naming convention: IQM_[IQM account ID]_[Segment name].
   1. Replace the items in brackets with the correct values, and remove the brackets. For example, “IQM_123456_CustomSegment”.
6. Select the universe name you entered to open the **Universe Details** page.
7. Click the house icon.
8. Select **Transmit this Universe to a third-party application**.
9. Choose **IQM** from the list of third-party applications that populate.
10. Click **SEND UNIVERSE** to export the universe to the IQM platform.

article_title: Generate and interpret a Campaign Bidding Insights report
context_header: Generate and interpret a Campaign Bidding Insights report › Campaign Bidding Insights report overview
text:
## Campaign Bidding Insights report overview

The Campaign Bidding Insights report captures each time that a campaign was rejected, then segments those occurrences into specific rejection reasons. You can use this data to assess which targeting parameters are limiting a campaign’s number of bid requests, then apply strategic optimizations to increase scale.

You can generate Campaign Bidding Insights for campaigns that meet certain eligibility criteria. Refer to [Campaign Bidding Insights report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10111445-campaign-bidding-insights-overview) for more information.

article_title: Generate and interpret a Campaign Bidding Insights report
section_path: Generate a Campaign Bidding Insights report
context_header: Generate and interpret a Campaign Bidding Insights report › Generate a Campaign Bidding Insights report
text:
## Generate a Campaign Bidding Insights report

You can generate Campaign Bidding Insights for one campaign at a time, and in the following ways:

- From the Insights app
- From the Campaigns app
- From the Dashboard app

article_title: Generate and interpret a Campaign Bidding Insights report
section_path: Generate a Campaign Bidding Insights report
Generate a report from the Insights app
context_header: Generate and interpret a Campaign Bidding Insights report › Generate a Campaign Bidding Insights report › Generate a report from the Insights app
text:
### Generate a report from the Insights app

Follow these steps to review Campaign Bidding Insights from the Insights app:

1. Open the Insights app.
2. Select **Campaign Bidding Insights.**
3. Choose whether the desired campaign is **Running**, **Paused**, or **Expired** from the **Campaign Status** menu.
4. Search and select the campaign for which you want to generate insights.
   1. Search for the campaign’s name or ID, or the insertion order’s (IO) name or ID.
   2. A campaign or IO is searchable from the **Campaign** field when it’s [eligible for Campaign Bidding Insights report generation](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10111445-campaign-bidding-insights-overview#h_3952d00349), and its status matches the **Campaign Status** you chose in step 3.
5. Select a time frame from the **Calendar** field.
   1. Choose a time frame ranging from the past one hour up to the past two weeks.
   2. The **Calendar** field uses the same time zone as the location where the campaign was created.

Campaign Bidding Insights will generate automatically once you complete the **Campaign Status**, **Campaign**, and **Calendar** fields.
