| [Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights reports (Healthcare)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview) | Compliantly evaluate the effectiveness of your Healthcare campaigns based on pre- and post-campaign prescription (Rx, TRx) volumes and competitors’ prescription patterns. |
| [Provider Level Data (PLD) Insights reports (Healthcare)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10774817-provider-level-data-pld-insights-report-overview) | Compliantly assess and optimize Healthcare campaigns. |
| [Audience Quality Insights reports (Healthcare)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13132023-audience-quality-aq-insights-report-overview) | Evaluate how effectively your Healthcare campaigns reached the intended patient audience. |

Refer to [Generate performance and insights data from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471810-generate-performance-and-insights-data-from-a-dashboard) for more details on how to generate reports and insights from a dashboard table.

context_header: Dashboard overview › Dashboard elements › AI Insights
text:
### AI Insights

AI Insights surface insights related to campaign-level performance.

The "CampaignPulse" AI Insights feature automatically checks critical or high-risk blockers to a campaign’s ability to serve ad impressions. You can also run CampaignPulse on-demand at any time for eligible campaigns. This diagnostic tool lets you know which issues are putting your campaign at the greatest risk, and what actions to take to address them.

Note that CampaignPulse is designed to help you detect and address significant risks to campaign delivery. For other campaign-optimization tools and strategies, refer to [Optimization overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12004298-optimization-overview).

Review [Create or manage a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign) or [Manage a campaign from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard) to get started with CampaignPulse.

context_header: Dashboard overview › Dashboard elements › AI Insights
text:
#### CampaignPulse eligibility requirements

All advertisers are eligible to run CampaignPulse for eligible campaigns. Refer to the table below for campaign-eligibility criteria.

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| Vertical | Specialty Political Healthcare |
| Campaign type | Advanced |
| Campaign status | Running, with a Start Date in the past |

#### CampaignPulse delivery insights

CampaignPulse checks critical blockers to a campaign’s ability to serve ad impressions. These blockers typically relate to possible errors and misses such as ensuring your account’s balance is sufficient, checking that targeted elements such as creatives and audiences feature a Ready status, and making sure your insertion order (IO) End Date is compatible with the End Dates of its campaigns, for example.

Review all CampaignPulse delivery insights closely for instructions on how to address the issues that can put your campaigns at risk.

context_header: Dashboard overview › Key terms and concepts
text:
### Set, Add, Split

**Set**, **Add**, and **Split** are three options that you’ll encounter when you edit a campaign’s total budget from a dashboard. Refer to [Manage a campaign from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard) for more information on how to apply these changes to your campaigns.

### Set

The **New Total Budget** value that you enter is the exact value that’s used for the campaign’s total budget.

Example: A campaign’s current total budget is $200,000. You enter $250,000 in the **New Total Budget** field and select **= Set**. The campaign’s new total budget is $250,000.

context_header: Dashboard overview › Key terms and concepts
text:
### Add

The value you enter in the **New Total Budget** field is the amount that gets added to the campaign’s existing total budget.

Example: A campaign’s current total budget is $200,000. You enter $50,000 in the **New Total Budget** field and select **+ Add**. The campaign’s new total budget is $250,000.

### Split

The value you enter in the **New Total Budget** field is the amount that gets divided evenly across each of the campaigns you selected. Note that you must select more than one campaign for the **Split** open to appear.

Example: A campaign’s current total budget is $200,000. You select four campaigns, enter $250,000 in the **New Total Budget** field, and click **÷ Split**. Each of the four campaigns’ total budgets are $62,5000, which total $250,000 when combined.

context_header: Create or manage a dashboard › Overview
text:
## Overview

> **Partner with Vera:** Vera serves as a versatile partner that simplifies and streamlines complex operations across the campaign lifecycle. This includes creating and managing data dashboards in the Vera app. Refer to ["Vera - IQM's artificial intelligence (AI) agent" collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15493648-vera-iqm-s-artificial-intelligence-ai-agent-collection-overview) to get started.

You’ll use the dashboards you create in the Dashboard app to track your campaigns’ progress and performance. Create and manage customized dashboards that fit your needs and improve your reporting workflow.

You can also save time by adjusting certain campaign elements—like budgets and bid prices—directly from these dashboards. Refer to [Manage a campaign from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard) for more information, and continue reading to learn how to customize your dashboards.

context_header: Create or manage a dashboard › Customize a dashboard
text:
## Customize a dashboard

Start by opening the Dashboard app from the homepage. You can customize a dashboard in the following ways:

- Limit data to a particular time zone or date range
- Customize a dashboard table
  - Add or remove a column
  - Sort by a column
  - Move a column
  - Filter or search
- Compare metrics
- Group by a metric

context_header: Create or manage a dashboard › Customize a dashboard
text:
### Select a time zone and date range

The dashboard aggregates campaigns and related data based on your time zone and date range selections.

Follow these steps to choose the dates and times that you’d like for the dashboard to reflect:

1. Search or browse and select a time zone from the **Time Zone** menu.
2. Open the **Date Range** menu.
3. Either manually select your preferred date range or select a preset timeframe from the available options.
4. Click **Apply**.

### Customize a dashboard table

> **Reach metric notice:** The **Reach** metric is an aggregated value that’s updated daily. The value shown reflects the campaign’s reach through yesterday, and any changes you apply today will reflect on the dashboard tomorrow.

Choose which metrics appear in your dashboard’s table; define the order in which they appear; and sort, filter, or search to surface campaigns by their elements.

context_header: Create or manage a dashboard › Customize a dashboard › Customize a dashboard table
text:
#### Add or remove a column

Follow these steps to choose which columns appear in your dashboard:

1. Open the **Columns** menu.
2. Click a metric to add it to the dashboard table.
3. Click a previously selected metric to remove it from the dashboard table.
4. If desired, use bulk operations to add or remove all columns.

#### Sort by a column

You can sort a dashboard table by any column’s dimensions or metrics.

Click a column’s title once to sort by that dimension or metric in ascending order. Click it again to sort by that dimension or metric in descending order.

#### Move a column

You can drag-and-drop a column to change the order in which your dashboard table’s dimensions and metrics appear.

Click and hold a column’s title. Drag the column’s title and hover it before or after another column’s title. When the vertical blue line appears, release your click to place the column in its new location.

context_header: Create or manage a dashboard › Customize a dashboard › Customize a dashboard table › Filter or search
text:
#### Filter or search

Follow these steps to choose which insertion orders (IO) and campaigns populate in the table:

1. Select your preferred customizations from the row of filters.
   1. Refer to [Dashboard elements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview#h_6d2be3e27f) to learn more about each filter.
2. Use the **Search by** field to enter an IO, name, or status.

context_header: Create or manage a dashboard › Customize a dashboard
text:
### Compare metrics and group by a metric

Use the data comparison panel to review data related to two metrics, and determine top performers by grouping by a particular dimension and metric.

### Compare metrics

1. If needed, select the arrow icon to expand the data comparison panel.
2. Browse and select the two metrics you’d like to compare from the menus.
   1. Note the colored circle next to each metric name to help you differentiate between them as you review the chart.
3. Hover your cursor over the chart area for metric details by date.

### Group by a metric

1. If needed, select the arrow icon to expand the data comparison panel.
2. Browse and select the dimension you’d like to group.
3. Browse and select the metric you’d like to review by the group you chose.
   1. For example, you might group by the **Creative** dimension and **Clicks** metric to uncover which creatives drove the most clicks during the date range you selected.
4. Review the bar graphs for performance details.

Note that the panel displays the top five items based on performance related to the metric you select; however, you can view full performance details in the dashboard table. Follow the steps outlined in Filter or search and Sort by a column to review performance by a particular campaign element and metric.

If no data was captured for this metric across the date range you select, **0** will appear next to each campaign element in the panel.

text:
## Create a new dashboard

> **More on dashboard creation:** The **Dashboard** menu will only appear if you previously created and saved a dashboard. If this is your first dashboard, follow the steps outlined in Save dashboard settings instead.

Follow these steps to keep a record of each dashboard customization you apply:

1. Open the **Dashboard** menu.
2. Select **Create New Dashboard**.
3. Enter a name for the new dashboard.
4. Click **Create New Dashboard**.

context_header: Create or manage a dashboard › Save dashboard settings
text:
## Save dashboard settings

Follow these steps to save changes to an existing dashboard:

1. Select **Save Dashboard**.
   1. If you’re saving changes to an existing dashboard, this will apply those changes.
   2. If you don’t have any saved dashboards, this will open the **Create Dashboard** pop-up window.
2. Enter a name for the new dashboard.
3. Click **Create**

You can return to the Dashboard app and Open a saved dashboard at any time to automatically apply each of your settings and filters.

context_header: Create or manage a dashboard › Open a saved dashboard
text:
## Open a saved dashboard

Open the **Dashboard** menu to browse and select an existing dashboard.

context_header: Create or manage a dashboard › Clear dashboard settings and filters
text:
## Clear dashboard settings and filters

Follow these steps to discard a dashboard’s unsaved changes:

1. Select **Reset**. This will open the **Reset Dashboard** pop-up window.
2. Click **Reset** to confirm your selection.

If no changes were saved prior to resetting the dashboard, selecting **Reset** will restore the dashboard’s default settings and filters. Note that this action is permanent. You’ll need to manually apply each setting and filter if you’d like to create the same dashboard again.

## Run and review AI Insights from a dashboard

> **More on CampaignPulse:** Refer to [Dashboard overview: AI Insights](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview#h_68302a50c0) for more information on CampaignPulse, including which campaigns are eligible and which campaign-performance elements it checks.

AI Insights surface insights related to campaign-level performance.

The “CampaignPulse” AI Insights feature automatically checks critical blockers to a running campaign’s ability to serve ad impressions. You can also run CampaignPulse on-demand at any time for [eligible campaigns](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview#h_08d9acd6e9).

Follow these steps to access CampaignPulse and review its insights from a dashboard:

1. Open the **View by** filter and select **Campaigns**.
2. Locate the **AI Insights** column in the dashboard table.
3. Select **Run Now**.
4. Select the **AI Insights** icon next to the desired campaign. This will open the **AI Insights** panel.
   1. A number indicates that CampaignPulse identified risks to campaign delivery.
   2. An enabled **AI Insights** icon with number indicates that the campaign is currently eligible for CampaignPulse, but no critical underdelivery risks were identified.
   3. A disabled **AI Insights** icon indicates that the campaign is currently ineligible for CampaignPulse.
5. If desired, filter the insights by type.

## Manage a campaign’s budget from a dashboard

You can change your campaigns’ total and daily budgets from a dashboard. Note that budgets are editable for budget-based campaigns, but not for impression-based ones.

article_title: Manage a campaign from a dashboard
section_path: Manage a campaign’s budget from a dashboard
context_header: Manage a campaign from a dashboard › Manage a campaign’s budget from a dashboard › Change a campaign’s total budget
text:
### Change a campaign’s total budget

> **Set**, **Add**, **or Split:** When you change a campaign’s total budget from a dashboard, you’ll choose whether to **Set**, **Add**, or **Split** the new value. Refer to [Key terms and concepts - Set, add, split](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview#h_f2238b5d23) for more information on these options.

You can update total budgets individually or in bulk.

article_title: Manage a campaign from a dashboard
section_path: Manage a campaign’s budget from a dashboard
context_header: Manage a campaign from a dashboard › Manage a campaign’s budget from a dashboard › Change a campaign’s total budget
text:
#### Change total budgets one by one

Follow these steps to update a campaign’s total budget:

1. Double-click the cell in the desired campaign’s **Total Budget** column.
2. Enter the new value.
3. Select the checkmark icon. This will open the **Set Total Budget** pop-up window.
4. Review the most recent total budget and the new total budget you’ve entered.
5. Click **Set** to apply your changes.

#### Change total budgets in bulk

Follow these steps to update the total budgets of multiple campaigns:

1. Select the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s).
2. Click **Total Budget** from the **Set Budget** menu. This will open the **Change Total Budget** pop-up window.
3. Enter the new value in the **New Total Budget** field.
4. Select **= Set**, **+ Add**, or **÷ Split**, depending on how you’d like to apply the new total budget to the campaign(s).
   1. You must select more than one campaign for the **÷ Split** option to appear in the **Change Total Budget** pop-up window.
5. Select **Change** to apply your edits.

text:
## Duplicate a campaign from a dashboard

Follow these steps to duplicate campaigns individually or in bulk:

1. Open an existing dashboard, if desired.
2. Search or filter the dashboard to locate the campaign you’d like to duplicate.
3. Select the checkbox next to the campaign.
4. Click **Duplicate** from the **Actions** menu. This will open the **Duplicate Campaign** pop-up window.
5. Choose the campaign’s insertion order (IO).
6. Set the campaign’s start and end dates.

After you select **Duplicate,** your duplicated campaign gets added to the IO as a draft. You’ll still need to review and activate it in the Campaigns app, if desired.

The resource includes steps on how to change an existing dashboard’s filters and settings, or create a new dashboard.

2. Search or filter the dashboard to locate the campaign(s) you’d like to delete.

text:
## Generate reports and insights

> **Does certain data appear to be incorrect?:** The time zone and date range that you select limits all reporting data to the events that occurred during that timeframe. Refer to [Select a time zone and date range](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471726-create-or-manage-a-dashboard#h_988f22700a), and adjust your selection to review data across a wider or narrower reporting window.

article_title: Generate performance and insights data from a dashboard
context_header: Generate performance and insights data from a dashboard › Generate reports and insights › Export data from a dashboard
text:
### Export data from a dashboard

You can download a dashboard table to your device as a CSV or XLSX file, or save a spreadsheet directly to your Google Drive. Either choice will include each column and row shown in your dashboard’s current view based on the filters you’ve selected.

Follow these steps to download a dashboard table:

1. Open an existing dashboard, if desired.
2. Search or filter the dashboard to determine which details appear in the table.
3. Open the **Columns** menu to add or remove metrics to the table.
4. Select the download icon.
5. Click **Download CSV** or **Download XLSX,** depending on your preferred file format.

2. Search or filter the dashboard to determine which details appear in the table.
3. Select the checkbox(es) next to the desired campaign(s).
4. Click **Create Report** from the **More** menu. This will redirect you to the **Create New Report** page of the **Reports** app.

The new report will automatically include the **Campaign** row, and filter the row to include the campaign(s) you selected in the Dashboard app.

Refer to the instructions included in [Generate, manage, or send a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report) for more support with customizing and running the report.

Locate pacing metrics in the Campaigns app
context_header: Manage pacing › Locate Campaign Pacing, Insertion Order (IO) Pacing, and Daily Pacing metrics › Locate pacing metrics in the Campaigns app
text:
### Locate pacing metrics in the Campaigns app

Follow these steps to locate Campaign Pacing, IO Pacing, and Daily Pacing metrics in the Campaigns app:

1. Open the **Campaigns** app from the homepage.
2. Filter or search your IOs to locate the one(s) for which you want to monitor pacing.
3. Locate the **IO Pacing** column.
   1. You may need to add the **IO Pacing** column to the table by selecting it from the **Columns** menu.
4. Select the IO for which you’d like to review campaign pacing and daily pacing metrics.
5. Filter or search the IO’s campaigns, if desired, to narrow the table view to specific campaigns.
6. Locate the **Campaign Pacing** and **Daily Pacing** columns.
   1. You may need to add these metrics to the table by selecting them from the **Columns** menu.

You can sort the IO table or campaigns table by pacing performance. Click a column’s title once to sort by that metric in ascending order. Click it again to sort by that metric in descending order.

### Locate pacing metrics in the Dashboard app

1. Open the Dashboard app.
2. Open an existing dashboard, if desired.
3. Open the **View by** menu and select **Insertion Orders** or **Campaigns**.
4. If you selected **Campaigns**, locate the **Campaign Pacing** and **Daily Pacing** columns.
   1. You may need to add these metrics to the table by selecting them from the **Columns** menu.
5. If you selected **Insertion Orders**, locate the **IO Pacing** column in the table.
   1. You may need to add the **IO Pacing** column to the table by selecting it from the **Columns** menu.

Like in the Campaigns app, you can sort the IO table or campaigns table by pacing performance. Click a column’s title once to sort by that metric in ascending order. Click it again to sort by that metric in descending order.

context_header: Manage pacing › Manage pacing
text:
## Manage pacing

Campaign Pacing, IO Pacing, and Daily Pacing are reporting metrics—not settings. You can, however, respond to pacing performance by allocating budgets and optimizing campaigns.

context_header: Manage pacing › Manage pacing › Manage IO pacing performance
text:
### Manage IO pacing performance

When an IO is pacing behind, you have the opportunity to allocate resources to the right strategies that are pacing as expected.

Choose one of two methods to move budgets between campaigns that are assigned to the same IO:

- From the Campaigns app
- From the Dashboard app

section_path: Shift budgets from the Campaigns app
context_header: Manage pacing › Manage pacing › Manage IO pacing performance › Shift budgets from the Campaigns app
text:
#### Shift budgets from the Campaigns app

1. Open the **Campaigns** app from the homepage.
2. Choose an IO, then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one(s) for which you want to manage budgets.
3. Select the checkbox next to the campaign(s).
4. Open the **Set Budget** menu and select **Total Budget**. This will open the **Set Total Budget** pop-up window.
5. Enter the new value in the **New Total Budget** field.
6. Select **= Set**, **+ Add**, or **÷ Split** depending on how you’d like to apply the new total budget to the campaign(s).
   1. You must select more than one campaign for the **÷ Split** option to appear in the **Change Total Budget** pop-up window.
7. Select **Set** to apply your edits.

Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Set, Add, Split](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471701-dashboard-overview#h_f2238b5d23) for more information on the ways you can apply a total budget to one or more campaigns.

section_path: Shift budgets from the Dashboard app
context_header: Manage pacing › Manage pacing › Manage IO pacing performance › Shift budgets from the Dashboard app
text:
#### Shift budgets from the Dashboard app

You can change your campaigns’ total budgets from a dashboard. Note that budgets are edible for budget-based campaigns, but not for impression-based ones.

Refer to [Manage a campaign’s budget from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard#h_3589c432de) for step-by-step instructions.

context_header: Manage pacing › Manage pacing
text:
### Manage campaign pacing performance

When a campaign is pacing behind, you can adjust your campaign settings to get spending back on track. Refer to [Troubleshoot a campaign that’s pacing behind](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471960-troubleshoot-a-campaign-that-s-pacing-behind) for support.

### Set a daily budget

You can also set a daily budget to influence how a campaign spends its budget. Daily budgets are distributed evenly throughout the day and include the media costs, data costs, and pre-bid targeting costs associated with the campaign.

Since daily budgets cap the amount that a campaign can spend each day, limit them to campaigns that are [pacing on track or pacing ahead](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8672915-a-guide-to-io-pacing-campaign-pacing-daily-pacing-in-iqm-s-platform#h_6b2774c8f9).

Choose one of two methods to define a daily budget for an existing campaign:

- From the Campaigns app
- From the Dashboard app

context_header: Manage pacing › Manage pacing › Set a daily budget
text:
#### Set a daily budget from the Campaigns app

Follow these steps to add or change a daily budget from the Campaigns app:

1. Open the **Campaigns** app from the homepage.
2. Choose an IO, then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one(s) for which you want to add a daily budget.
3. Select the checkbox(es) next to the campaign(s).
4. Open the **Set Budget** menu and select **Daily Budget.** This will open the **Set Daily Budget** pop-up window.
5. Enter the desired daily budget in the **Daily Budget** field.
6. Select **Set** to confirm your changes.

#### Set a daily budget from the Dashboard app

Refer to [Manage a campaign’s budget from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard#h_3589c432de) for step-by-step instructions on setting a daily budget from the Dashboard app.

article_title: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind › Troubleshoot pacing issues
text:
## Troubleshoot pacing issues

Pacing determines if your strategies are on track to spend in full based on how much they’ve spent so far and how much time is remaining in the campaign or insertion order (IO).

Refer to [Pacing overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8672915-a-guide-to-io-pacing-campaign-pacing-daily-pacing-in-iqm-s-platform) for more information on your pacing options in the IQM platform. Return to this article to review the primary factors that influence a campaign’s pacing performance.

In most cases, a campaign paces behind when bid prices are too low to win in programmatic auctions, or when a campaign’s targeting rules are too restrictive. Follow the guidelines below to assess these factors and apply any necessary changes to help ensure your campaigns spend in full.

article_title: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind › Win rate
text:
## Win rate

Win rate describes the percentage of impressions that you won in a programmatic auction, which is impacted most heavily by the bid price. Low win rates can cause your campaign to pace behind.

Check the campaign’s win rate, then consider optimizing its bidding to catch up on spending.

article_title: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind › Win rate
text:
### Check a campaign’s win rate

1. Open the Dashboard app.
2. Open an existing dashboard, if desired.
3. Choose a time zone and date range for the dashboard’s data.
4. Apply filters to determine which insertion orders (IOs) or campaigns populate in the table.

Review the win-rate data to uncover the percentage of impressions that the campaign won. Note that win rates are ranges, and there’s no one ideal win rate. In general, you can consider a win rate of 50-80% to be good, 20-30% to be normal, and under 20% to signal an opportunity to improve your bidding strategy.

### Optimize bid prices - Max Bid Price

Your Max Bid Price may be limiting the impressions that the campaign can bid on.

You can adjust a Max Bid Price from the same dashboard table that you used to assess your Win Rate performance. Refer to the steps in [Change Max Bid Prices from the Max Bid Price column](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard#h_0bda217a19) to increase a campaign’s Max Bid Price.

article_title: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind › Win rate › Optimize bid prices - Bid Modifiers
text:
### Optimize bid prices - Bid Modifiers

There may be instances where your campaign is pacing behind, and you suspect that it’s due to your bidding strategy, but you only want to increase bids for certain dimensions.

Bid Modifiers allows you to take control of your campaign’s bidding strategy. You can choose to optimize your campaigns by bidding a higher or lower price for the individual creatives that are most or least important to them.

Bid Modifiers are especially useful when a certain targeting rule is non-negotiable. Since you can’t change the targeting rule, you can bid more for it instead to help keep the campaign’s pacing on track. These multipliers can be changed or removed at any time, as needed.

Refer to [What is a Bid Modifier?](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-what-is-a-bid-modifier) for details on requirements and for instructions on applying a Bid Modifier to a creative in the Bid Model app.

article_title: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind › Win rate › Optimize bid prices - Bid Shading
text:
### Optimize bid prices - Bid Shading

Bid shading allows the platform to automatically optimize your campaign to achieve the best effective cost per mille (eCPM). It lowers your bid when you can win at auction for a lower price than the max bid price you specified for a campaign.

We enable bid shading by default across all campaigns to help you bid competitively in first-price auctions without overpaying. However, if a campaign is pacing behind, you might consider temporarily turning off the bid shading feature.

Click the **Bid Shading** toggle switch in the **Campaign Info** section to disable the feature. You’ll know that bid shading is turned off when the toggle switch moves to the left and changes in color from blue to gray.

Select **Save** to apply your updated bid shading settings.

article_title: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind › Bid rate
text:
## Bid rate

The bid rate metric helps you determine how often a campaign’s targeting criteria and other details matched available bid requests. Low bid rates can cause your campaigns to pace behind.

Your campaign’s targeting strategies are the main factors that determine bid rate. It can only pace properly if there are enough available impressions that you can bid on after your targeting is applied. To run a data-driven campaign that still keeps your targetable audience wide enough to spend the entire campaign budget, you’ll need to limit your targeting to only include essential requirements. In other words, finding the balance between scale and value is essential for pacing on track while hitting your campaign goals.

Check the campaign’s bid rate, then consider optimizing its targeting rules to catch up on spending.

article_title: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind › Bid rate › Check a campaign’s bid rate
text:
### Check a campaign’s bid rate

You can assess a campaign’s bid rate by generating a Campaign Bidding Insights report in the Insights app. The charts and figures included in the report highlight the following campaign details:

- What impact each targeting rule had on bid-request drop offs for a campaign
- How many bid requests remained and passed through each subsequent stage
- What final bid rate your campaign achieved after it honored each of the targeting rules you defined

Refer to [Generate and interpret a Campaign Bidding Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10034144-generate-and-interpret-a-campaign-bidding-insights-report) to assess a campaign’s bid rate, and pinpoint which targeting parameters are causing the biggest drop off in your campaign’s bid requests.

article_title: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind › Bid rate › Optimize a campaign’s bid rate
text:
### Optimize a campaign’s bid rate

Use the insights you uncovered in the Campaign Bidding Insights report to adjust certain targeting rules, make your campaign eligible to bid on more impressions, and ultimately improve spend performance when your campaign is pacing behind. For example, if a campaign’s Location targeting settings are too restrictive, you can widen the targeted area to allow the campaign to serve more impressions.

You can apply campaign edits directly from the generated Insights report. Refer to [Apply Campaign Bidding Insights to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10034144-generate-and-interpret-a-campaign-bidding-insights-report#h_6145e7762a) to make adjustments that will allow the campaign to bid on more ad impression opportunities.

article_title: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind › Optimization & Delivery
text:
## Optimization & Delivery

> **AI Based Optimization notice:** When you choose an AI Based Optimization method, you forfeit certain manual-optimization features such as Advanced Modeling. Refer to [Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview) for more information on the differences between the Rule Based and AI Based Optimization methods.

Optimization (Rule Based, AI Based), Budget Capping, Bid Pacing, and Frequency Capping are the four tools that form a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery strategy. How you manage them can impact the campaign’s ability to pace on track.

Adjust budget cap, bid pacing, and frequency cap settings in the campaign’s **Optimization & Delivery** section.

article_title: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind › Optimization & Delivery › Impression caps and budget caps
text:
### Impression caps and budget caps

With Budget Caps, you can customize your pacing strategy by defining a maximum daily spending limit once a certain cost is reached for impressions, clicks, and conversions. You can also set an impression cap to limit the number of impressions that you want to display per day.

article_title: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind
section_path: Increase or remove a budget cap or impression cap
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind › Optimization & Delivery › Impression caps and budget caps › Increase or remove a budget cap or impression cap
text:
#### Increase or remove a budget cap or impression cap

Since impression and Budget Caps cause your campaign to stop spending once the daily limits are reached, we recommend reserving these settings for campaigns and IOs that are pacing on track (90%-100%) or pacing ahead (100%-120%).

Consider increasing the daily cap for the day, or removing the cap, to allow the campaign’s pacing to catch up. Refer to [Manage a campaign's Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings) to complete this step.

article_title: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind › Optimization & Delivery
text:
### Disable Bid Pacing

When enabled, the **Bid Pacing** tool evenly distributes the campaign’s daily budget throughout the day.

Consider disabling this feature if your campaign is pacing behind. This change will allow the campaign to spend the budget as soon as possible without pacing restrictions in place. Refer to [Manage a campaign's Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings) for more information.

### Increase Frequency Cap

While Frequency Caps are critical for creating a positive user experience, a campaign can begin to pace behind when the Frequency Cap you define is too restrictive. Campaigns are highly customized based on the targeting parameters you set and the current bid landscape. This means that there’s not one recommended Frequency Cap for optimal campaign performance.

If you suspect that your Frequency Cap settings are the cause of your campaign pacing behind, consider increasing its frequency gradually while monitoring both reach and performance. Refer to [Frequency capping overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8480958-frequency-capping-overview) and [Manage a campaign's Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings) and for more details.

article_title: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind › Other pacing considerations › Audiences
text:
### Audiences

The size and cost of a campaign’s audience(s) can impact its ability to pace as intended.

If the campaign is pacing behind and you suspect that it’s due to audience targeting settings, check these two items for each of your audiences:

- **Cost:** Review the **Cost (CPM)** column and determine whether you can create a similar audience for a lower CPM.
- **Size:** Review the Reach column and determine whether you’ll need to create a less restrictive audience for your campaign to spend in full.

Manage the audience(s) directly in the **Campaigns** app, or review [Selecting your audiences](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/1387061-selecting-your-audiences) for more resources on creating a new audience or managing an existing one in the **Audiences** app.

article_title: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind › Other pacing considerations › Creatives
text:
### Creatives

Choosing the right ad format helps ensure your message resonates with the intended audience, and affects how users engage with your ad. The size of your creatives also determines where your ad can get placed across digital inventory.

Check a campaign’s creative size(s) when it’s pacing behind. If your creative is a less common size, it can significantly reduce the number of impressions you can bid on. Consider adding more sizes in the same creative format (e.g., Image, Video, Native) to the campaign to win more bids.

Review [Creative formats overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10344323-creative-formats-overview) for more details about the ad formats that are supported on the IQM platform, and refer to [Creative Ad Specs](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019246-creative-ad-specs) to check recommended sizes and requirements.

article_title: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind › Other pacing considerations › Blocklists
text:
### Blocklists

Allowlists and Blocklists help ensure that every marketing dollar goes toward the strategies that are the most likely to reach your target audience—but they also limit the number of impressions that you can bid on. This can put your campaigns at risk of spending in full.

If the campaign is pacing behind, evaluate each of the campaign’s Blocklists and determine whether you can remove any of them. Review [Allowlist and Blocklist overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10472012-allowlist-and-blocklist-overview) and [Manage campaign Allowlists and Blocklists](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10472023-manage-campaign-allowlists-and-blocklists) for more details.

article_title: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind › Proactive pacing tips
text:
## Proactive pacing tips

In the future, take a proactive approach to pacing. Forecasting metrics provide a sense of scale to help you determine whether you have the right targeting and blocking strategies in place to spend your campaign budget in full and achieve campaign objectives.

Before you run a new campaign, leverage forecasting tools in the Campaigns and Planner apps to help ensure your campaign can pace on track or pace ahead.

article_title: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind › Proactive pacing tips › Forecast in the Campaigns app
text:
### Forecast in the Campaigns app

Each time you create a new campaign or edit an existing one, you can select **Run Campaign Estimations** to generate forecasts based on the targeting rules you add to the campaign. These include the approximate size of your targetable audience, estimated reach and impressions, and the number of impressions you can expect to win at different bid prices.

Refer to [Estimate reach, impression and audience size for a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7883438-estimate-reach-impression-and-audience-size-for-a-campaign) for more information on generating campaign forecasts in the Campaigns app.

article_title: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign that's pacing behind › Proactive pacing tips › Forecast in the Planner app
text:
### Forecast in the Planner app

Planner proposals give you powerful insights into your media plan’s potential reach and impressions as you layer each targeting parameter onto your campaigns. This process helps highlight which rules will limit your strategy’s scale the most. You can pre-optimize your audience and targeting details to help ensure each campaign spends in full.

Unlike the Campaigns app, the Planner app creates your campaigns for you based on the rules you share when you create a proposal. You can review and tweak those campaigns, add your creatives, and run the campaigns in just a few clicks.

Refer to [Create or manage a Planner proposal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10104761-create-or-manage-a-planner-proposal) to learn how to add your targeting criteria to a new media plan.

context_header: Allowlist and Blocklist overview › Allowlist and Blocklist overview
text:
## Allowlist and Blocklist overview

Allowlists and Blocklists are the rules you establish to determine which ad impressions a campaign is eligible to bid on. These rules relate to various campaign elements (such as Locations, Device IDs, Audiences, and more. For example, you can choose which relevant audiences you’d like to show your ad to, and which ones you’d like to prevent from seeing the ad, by adding those audiences to an Allowlist or Blocklist. Note that you may see Allowlists referred to as “white lists” or “target lists” and Blocklists referred to as “black lists” in other DSPs.

While customizing a campaign with Allowlists and Blocklists is essential for tailoring a campaign, these elements should be reserved for only the non-negotiable rules you’d like to apply to the campaign. Refer to Impact on reach and impressions for more information on scale considerations.

context_header: Allowlist and Blocklist overview › Allowlist and Blocklist overview
text:
### Allowlists

You’ll apply targeting criteria to a campaign when you want to define who you're willing to serve the ad to based on a specific set of criteria. For example, you can choose to only advertise to users who are browsing on a particular device, located in a particular geographic region, and belonging to a particular audience.

Your targeting settings get added to an “Allowlist” for each relevant dimension category.

### Blocklists

You’ll apply blocking criteria to a campaign when you want to avoid showing your ads to users based on a specific set of criteria. For example, if you’re building an awareness campaign, you might want to prevent users who previously converted on your website from seeing the ad by adding a Retargeting audience to a Blocklist. You can also choose which sites or apps you’d like to avoid in order to maintain the brand’s image or exclude irrelevant inventory.

Your blocking settings get added to a “Blocklist” for each relevant dimension category.

context_header: Allowlist and Blocklist overview › Allowlist and Blocklist overview › AND/OR relationships
text:
### AND/OR relationships

Note that a campaign’s Allowlists and Blocklists are assigned an “OR” relationship, meaning that they work independently for each dimension. Allowlists and Blocklists are specific to each campaign element such as Audience, Location, Inventory, and more. This means that you can, for example, exclude a certain audience and include a certain site domain.

With an “OR” relationship, a campaign won’t bid on an impression if it matches any one of the exclusion criteria included in a Blocklist. For example, you can’t block one user who is located in New York “AND” browsing a particular site domain. The campaign will block any user who is either located in New York “OR” browsing a particular site domain.

Example Blocklist:

- New York
- Site Domain A

| **Impression details** | **Bid decision (Y/N)** |
| --- | --- |
| Texas, **Site Domain A** | N - The impression matches a blocked Site Domain dimension. |
| **New York**, Site Domain C | N- The impression matches a blocked Location dimension. |
| California, **Site Domain A** | N - The impression matches a blocked Site Domain dimension. |
| California, Site Domain B | Y - The impression doesn’t match any blocked dimensions. |

context_header: Allowlist and Blocklist overview › Allowlist and Blocklist overview › AND/OR relationships
text:
### AND/OR relationships

Allowlists follow a similar logic, but will include rather than exclude the items you’ve specified. Using the same example, you can’t target one user who is located in New York “AND” browsing a particular site domain. The campaign will bid on an impression if it matches either one of these inclusion criteria.

Allowlist rules differ slightly from Blocklist rules. If you target certain campaign dimensions, then all other dimensions in the same dimension category are excluded. For example, if your campaign targets New York and California, it’ll only bid on New York impressions or California impressions. This means that all other Locations are effectively blocked from the campaign.

Example Allowlist:

- New York
- California
- Site Domain A

| **Impression details** | **Bid decision (Y/N)** |
| --- | --- |
| **New York**, Site Domain B | N - If only **Site Domain A** is targeted, the campaign won’t serve ads on other site domains. |
| Texas, **Site Domain A** | N - If only **New York** and **California** are targeted, the campaign won’t serve ads to users in other locations**.** |
| **California**, **Site Domain A** | Y - The impression matches all Allowlist rules. |

> **Impressions that match targeted and blocked dimensions:** There may be instances when an available impression matches one targeted dimension and another blocked dimension. For example, the campaign is blocking the site domain and targeting the mobile operating system (OS). The campaign will only bid on impressions that meet every targeting requirement that you’ve defined. In the same way, it will never bid on an impression that matches any of your campaign’s blocked dimensions.

section_path: Campaign elements to allow or block
context_header: Allowlist and Blocklist overview › Campaign elements to allow or block
text:
## Campaign elements to allow or block

You can create an Allowlist or Blocklist for each dimension category, or element, listed below.

| **Element** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Location | In the **Campaigns** app, choose which states, DMAs, counties, cities, or ZIP codes; or congressional districts, state senates, or state houses to include or exclude. |
| Audience | In the **Campaigns** app, choose which audiences to include or exclude based on your own user data, or segments from IQM or any of our data providers. These audiences are made up of groups of users who share common characteristics like age, gender, or home ownership status, for example. |
| Device | In the **Campaigns** app, choose which device IDs to include or exclude. In the **Bid Model** app, choose which device elements to include or exclude after they appear in the ad-serving data. These may include individual devices (TV, tablet, desktop, or mobile) or channels (app, web, connected TV [CTV], or over the top [OTT]). |
| Inventory* | In the **Campaigns** app, choose which Android packages, iOS Apple IDs, and/or site domains to include or exclude. In the **Inventory** app, assign inventory to a **Global Blocklist** to ensure that your ads are only displayed on high-quality websites that align with the brand image and target audience. The platform will immediately stop serving ads across any of the inventory you blocked. In the **Bid Model** app, choose which deal ID(s), Open Exchange inventory, and/or publisher categories that you want the campaign to include or exclude. |
| Advanced | In the **Campaigns** app, indicate which device ID(s) and/or internet protocol (IP) addresses that you want the campaign to include or exclude. |

* Refer to [What are Blocklisted Inventories?](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6962891-what-are-blocklisted-inventories) for more information on inventory Blocklists.

context_header: Allowlist and Blocklist overview › Impact on reach and impressions
text:
## Impact on reach and impressions

Allowlists and Blocklists help ensure that every marketing dollar goes toward the strategies that are the most likely to reach your target audience—but they also limit the number of impressions that you can bid on. This can put your campaigns at risk of spending in full.

Forecasting and reporting metrics provide a sense of scale to help you determine whether you can spend your campaign budget in full and achieve campaign objectives. Leverage your preferred tools in the Campaigns, Planner, Reports, and Insights apps to help right-size your campaigns’ Allowlist and Blocklist strategies:

- **Campaigns app:** Refer to [Estimate reach, impression and audience size for a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7883438-estimate-reach-impression-and-audience-size-for-a-campaign) for more information on generating campaign forecasts in the Campaigns app.
- **Planner app:** Refer to [Create or manage a Planner proposal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10104761-create-or-manage-a-planner-proposal) to learn how to add your targeting criteria to a new media plan.
- **Reports app:** Refer to [Generate, manage, or send a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report) to get started with [Performance reporting metrics](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343812-performance-reporting-metrics-overview) in custom reports.
- **Insights app:** Refer to [Generate and interpret a Campaign Bidding Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10034144-generate-and-interpret-a-campaign-bidding-insights-report) to pinpoint the campaign elements that are causing the biggest drop off in available bid requests.

> **Apply a Bid Model:** Because Allowlists and Blocklists limit a campaign’s scale, it’s important to reserve them for when you only want to bid on certain dimensions, or never want to bid on certain dimensions. If your campaign’s targeting parameters are flexible, consider applying Bid Model components to apply optimizations throughout the campaign. You can stop bidding on the campaign dimensions that aren’t performing well, bid more precisely based on how valuable an impression is to the campaign, and choose which dimensions the campaign should prioritize over others. Refer to [Customize your Bid Model](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5601911-customize-your-bid-model) for more details.

context_header: Manage campaign Allowlists and Blocklists › Allowlist and Blocklist overview
text:
## Allowlist and Blocklist overview

Allowlists and Blocklists are the rules you establish to determine which ad impressions a campaign is eligible to bid on. These rules relate to various [campaign elements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10472012-allowlist-and-blocklist-overview#h_1ee82b6de6) such as Locations, Device IDs, Audiences, and more.

Refer to [Allowlist and Blocklist overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10472012-allowlist-and-blocklist-overview) for more details, or continue reading to add Allowlists and Blocklists to a campaign.

section_path: Add Allowlists and Blocklists from the Campaigns app
context_header: Manage campaign Allowlists and Blocklists › Add Allowlists and Blocklists from the Campaigns app
text:
## Add Allowlists and Blocklists from the Campaigns app

Follow these steps to add Allowlists and Blocklists to a new or existing campaign from the Campaigns app:

1. Open the **Campaigns** app from the homepage.
2. Choose an insertion order (IO).
3. Filter or search your campaigns to locate the campaign.
4. To add targets and blocks to an existing campaign, select its name from the table.
5. To add targets and blocks to a new campaign, select **+ Create Campaign**.

Completing steps 4 or 5 will open the campaign’s details, where you can specify its targets and blocks.

> **Allowlist/Blocklist requirements:** The elements included in your Allowlists and Blocklists can total up to 500 per section and per campaign. For example, you can add a total of 500 location targets and blocks, and a total of 500 inventory targets and blocks, for the same campaign.

section_path: Add Allowlists and Blocklists from the Campaigns app
context_header: Manage campaign Allowlists and Blocklists › Add Allowlists and Blocklists from the Campaigns app › Audience Allowlist/Blocklist
text:
### Audience Allowlist/Blocklist

Refer to [Select an audience for your campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651478-select-an-audience-for-your-campaign) to add the audience(s) that you’d like to target and/or block.

Once you’ve added the audience(s), follow these steps to move them to an Allowlist or Blocklist:

1. Locate the table featuring each audience name that you added to the campaign.
2. In the **Allowlist/Blocklist** column, each audience is automatically added to the campaign’s Allowlist.
   1. You’ll know that the audience is added to the Allowlist when the toggle is switched to the right and shown in green.
3. Click the toggle to add an audience to the campaign’s Blocklist.
   1. You’ll know that the location is successfully added when the toggle moves to the left and changes to red.
4. Save your changes to apply the new Allowlist and/or Blocklist settings to the campaign.

section_path: Add Allowlists and Blocklists from the Campaigns app
context_header: Manage campaign Allowlists and Blocklists › Add Allowlists and Blocklists from the Campaigns app › Locations Allowlist/Blocklist
text:
### Locations Allowlist/Blocklist

Refer to [Choose the target location for your campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7175776-choose-the-target-location-for-your-campaign) to add the specific geos that you’d like to target and/or block.

Once you’ve added the locations, follow these steps to move them to an Allowlist or Blocklist:

1. Locate the **List of Targeted Locations** panel.
2. Select the expand arrow next to any location.
3. Click the toggle next to the location once to add it to the campaign’s Allowlist.
   1. You’ll know that the location is successfully added when the toggle moves to the right and changes from gray to green.
4. Click the toggle a second time to add it to the campaign’s Blocklist.
   1. You’ll know that the location is successfully added when the toggle moves to the left and changes from gray to red.
5. Save your changes to apply the new Allowlist and/or Blocklist settings to the campaign.

section_path: Add Allowlists and Blocklists from the Campaigns app
context_header: Manage campaign Allowlists and Blocklists › Add Allowlists and Blocklists from the Campaigns app › Inventory Allowlist/Blocklist
text:
### Inventory Allowlist/Blocklist

Follow these steps to move ad inventory to an Allowlist or Blocklist:

1. Select **+ Allowlist** or **+ Blocklist** in the Inventory section to specify the inventory that the campaign should target or block.
2. Upload or paste Android package names, iOS Apple IDs, and/or site domains into the appropriate **Android Package Names**, **iOS Apple IDs**, and/or **Site Domains** field.
   1. When you add more than one name, ID, or domain, separate them by either using a comma or selecting **enter** on your keyboard to place each item on its own line.
3. Select **Add**.
4. The **+ Allowlist** and **+ Blocklist** buttons are replaced with **View Allowlist** or **View Blocklist** buttons once you add any inventory targets or blocks.
   1. Review a summary of the Allowlist and/or Blocklist, or select **View Allowlist** or **View Blocklist** to manage them.
5. Save your changes to apply the new Allowlist and/or Blocklist settings to the campaign.

> **More on inventory Allowlists/Blocklists:** You can add Android package names, iOS Apple IDs, and/or site domains to an inventory Allowlist or Blocklist. An Android package name is a unique identifier for Google Play Store apps and the Android operating system. It distinguishes apps from each other and is typically formatted as a reversed domain name such as “com.example.myapp.” An iOS app ID is a unique identifier for Apple iOS platform apps, and used for app management, distribution, and more. A site domain is a unique web address or URL where digital ads are displayed. Each domain represents a specific site or online platform (e.g., example.com and IQM.com).

section_path: Add Allowlists and Blocklists from the Campaigns app
context_header: Manage campaign Allowlists and Blocklists › Add Allowlists and Blocklists from the Campaigns app › Inventory Allowlist/Blocklist - Global Blocklist
text:
### Inventory Allowlist/Blocklist - Global Blocklist

There may be one or more types of digital media placements or websites that you’d like to exclude from all of your ad campaigns. This inventory is typically deemed inappropriate due to adult content, hate speech, or misleading information; or feature low engagement or create a poor user experience.

You can add this inventory to a **Global Blocklist** in the **Inventory** app to automatically exclude the same set of inventory across each of your campaigns. Refer to [How to manage Blocklisted inventories?](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6955342-how-to-manage-blocklisted-inventories) to create or manage a **Global Blocklist**.

section_path: Add Allowlists and Blocklists from the Campaigns app
context_header: Manage campaign Allowlists and Blocklists › Add Allowlists and Blocklists from the Campaigns app › Advanced Allowlist/Blocklist
text:
### Advanced Allowlist/Blocklist

You can use an Advanced campaign’s **Advanced** section to add specific device IDs and internet protocol (IP) addresses to an Allowlist or Blocklist.

Follow these steps to add device IDs and/or IP addresses to an Allowlist or Blocklist:

1. Select **Allowlist** or **Blocklist** toggle switch in the Advanced section. This will expand the section to include the **Device IDs** and **IP** fields.
2. Upload or paste the IDs or IP addresses into the appropriate field.
   1. When you add more than one ID or IP address, separate them by either using a comma or selecting **enter** on your keyboard to place each item on its own line.
3. Save your changes to apply the new Allowlist and/or Blocklist settings to the campaign.

section_path: Add Allowlists and Blocklists from the Bid Model app
context_header: Manage campaign Allowlists and Blocklists › Add Allowlists and Blocklists from the Bid Model app
text:
## Add Allowlists and Blocklists from the Bid Model app

You can manage Allowlists and Blocklists for certain campaign dimensions in the Bid Model app.

Follow these steps to add supported dimensions to an Allowlist or Blocklist for a campaign:

1. Open the **Bid Model** app from the homepage.
2. Choose whether the campaign is **Running**, **Paused**, **Pending**, **Paused**, **Rejected**, or a **Draft** from the status dropdown menu.
3. Search and select the campaign for which you want to apply Bid Model settings.
   1. A campaign or IO is searchable from the **Select Campaign** field when two criteria are met: it is eligible for Bid Modeling, and its status matches the one you chose in step 2.
4. Select a supported campaign dimension category.
5. Use the **Allowlist/Blocklist** column to manage targets and blocks for each dimension within that dimension category.
   1. Each listed item automatically added to the campaign’s Allowlist.
      1. You’ll know a dimension is included in the Allowlist when the toggle is switched to the right and shown in green.
   2. Click the toggle to add the dimension to the campaign’s Blocklist.
      1. You’ll know a dimension is successfully added when the toggle moves to the left and changes to red.

article_title: AdChoices and interest-based advertising frequently asked questions (FAQ)
context_header: AdChoices and interest-based advertising frequently asked questions (FAQ) › What is interest-based advertising?
text:
## What is interest-based advertising?

Advertising supports the free internet. It's the primary way that most website and app publishers make money in order to produce the content consumers want. Not all advertising shown to consumers is relevant to their interests, though. Interest-based advertising is advertising that tries to make the ads you see more interesting and relevant to you based on the types of sites you visit online and other information that does not personally identify you. We conduct interest-based advertising on our website, and work with our clients to help them do the same on their websites and apps.

IQM is a member of the Digital Advertising Alliance (DAA) and adheres to the DAA principles. For more information about the data we collect and how we use it, please refer to the IQM [privacy policy](https://iqm.com/privacy-policy).

For compliance with the EU-US and Swiss-US regulations, IQM is an active participant in the Privacy Shield Framework. [https://www.privacyshield.gov](https://www.privacyshield.gov/).

section_path: What are the benefits of relevant advertising?
context_header: AdChoices and interest-based advertising frequently asked questions (FAQ) › What are the benefits of relevant advertising?
text:
## What are the benefits of relevant advertising?

Without interested-based advertising, you'll still see ads, but those ads likely won't have anything to do with products or services you care about. With interest-based advertising, you receive ads and offers that are more likely to be useful to you.

There's also a second benefit to you: companies that create websites and apps rely on the revenue from interest-based advertising to support the rich array of content they produce. Without that revenue, the content would either be unavailable or consumers would have to pay for it.

text:
## What is AdChoices?

AdChoices gives you control over how information about your interests is used for relevant advertising. This information is based on your online browsing activity across sites and apps on a particular device or browser, and does not personally identify you.

section_path: What does it mean to opt out of interest-based advertising?
context_header: AdChoices and interest-based advertising frequently asked questions (FAQ) › What does it mean to opt out of interest-based advertising?
text:
## What does it mean to opt out of interest-based advertising?

In general, “opting out” means that you want to limit the information we collect and store about your computer or device, and to not target ads that are based on your interests to your browser or device. Your opt-out is only applicable to our platform and does not opt you out from platforms provided by third-party companies. However, you can out from both our platform and many third-party companies at once; to do so, refer to How can users opt out of interest-based advertising?

If you use multiple browsers, computers or mobile devices, and wish to limit the information IQM collects and stores or do not wish to receive IQM interest-based advertising on any of them, you must opt out from each browser, computer, and mobile device individually. Please note that if cookies are not enabled in your browser, or if you use certain ad-blocking tools, our opt-out mechanism may not work properly. Please also note that deleting your cookies does not opt you out.

Users who opt out of interest-based targeting will continue to encounter ads. However, the ads delivered by the companies that you've opted out from will not be as relevant to you.

section_path: Assign a creative to a campaign
context_header: Assign a creative to a campaign › Assign a creative to a campaign › Creatives app - Existing campaign
text:
### Creatives app - Existing campaign

Follow these steps to assign a creative to a campaign that you’ve already created:

1. Use the creative format panel to either select **All** or an individual creative format.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to the creative(s) you’d like to assign to an existing campaign. These creatives must feature the same creative format.
3. Open the **Campaign Actions** menu and click **Assign To Campaign**. This will open the **Assign to Campaigns** pop-up window.
4. Open the **Campaigns** menu to search and select the desired campaign(s).
   1. Campaigns featuring a Draft, Pending, Running, or Paused status are eligible.
5. Select **Update** to apply your changes.

If you’ve already assigned one or more creatives to a campaign, you can add additional ones to it from the **Campaigns** column of the **Creatives** page:

1. Locate the **Campaigns** column.
2. Select the listed number, which represents the total number of creatives already assigned to the campaign. This will open the **Assign to Campaigns** pop-up window.
   1. You can use this workflow only when this number is greater than zero, meaning that you’ve assigned the creative to at least one campaign.
3. Follow steps 4 through 5 of the Assign a creative to an existing campaign workflow.

From the Creatives app - New campaign
context_header: Assign a creative to a campaign › Assign a creative to a campaign › From the Creatives app - New campaign
text:
### From the Creatives app - New campaign

Follow these steps to assign a creative to a new campaign from the Creatives app:

1. Use the creative format panel to either select **All** or an individual creative format.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to the creative(s) you’d like to assign to a new campaign. These creatives must feature the same creative format.
3. Open the **Campaign Actions** menu and click **Create Campaign**. This will open the **Create Campaign** pop-up window, where you’ll enter the new campaign’s details.
4. Open the **Insertion Order** menu to search and select the desired IO.
5. Enter a name for the campaign into the **Campaign Name** field.
6. Choose whether the campaign is **Advanced** or **Programmatic Guaranteed (PG)**.
7. Select **Create**. This will automatically redirect you to the campaign creation workflow in the **Campaigns** app.
8. Complete any required and desired fields for the campaign, as needed.
9. Click **Save as Draft** to apply your changes, or **Run** to create the campaign.

text:
### From the Campaigns app - Existing campaign

Follow these steps to assign a creative to a campaign that you’ve already created:

1. Select the **Campaigns** app from the homepage.
2. Choose an insertion order (IO), then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one for which you want to add a creative.
3. Locate the **Campaign Name** column and click the campaign’s name. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add or update its details and targeting parameters.
4. Locate the **Creatives** section.
5. Click **+ Select Creatives**.
6. In the pop-up window, select the checkbox(es) next to the creative(s) that you’d like to add.
7. Click **Select**.
8. Select **Save** to apply your changes to the existing campaign.

### From the Campaigns app - New campaign

Follow these steps to assign a creative to a new campaign:

1. Select the **Campaigns** app from the homepage.
2. Choose an insertion order (IO), then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one for which you want to add a creative.
3. Select **+ Create Campaign**. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the new campaign, where you can add or update its details and targeting parameters.
4. Locate the **Creatives** section.

context_header: Account Based Marketing (ABM) audience overview › ABM audience overview
text:
## ABM audience overview

With multiple doctors and other medical professionals involved in decision making for a given healthcare account, healthcare campaigns require full-personnel targeting strategies. Targeting at the account level and turning those accounts into customers is the main objective of Account-Based Marketing (ABM).

Healthcare advertisers can create Healthcare Practitioner (HCP) or Generic type ABM audiences to maximize relevance, engagement, and value. These ABM audiences leverage comprehensive hospital data from providers such as HealthLink Dimensions (HLD) or RevOptimal to pass personalized messages to healthcare professionals at scale, and with a privacy-safe approach. You can craft highly specific healthcare audiences using custom and pre-defined segments based on account-based attributes such as health systems, specialty practices, and NPI reach.

Adopt an account-based strategy with ABM audiences to engage with doctors and other key healthcare stakeholders, and ultimately reach your healthcare-campaign goals across accounts.

context_header: Account Based Marketing (ABM) audience overview › ABM audience eligibility requirements
text:
## ABM audience eligibility requirements

If you’re a healthcare advertiser, you may be eligible to create an ABM audience.

A campaign must also meet each of these conditions before it becomes eligible for ABM audience targeting.

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| **Campaign vertical** | Healthcare* |
| **Campaign type** | Advanced |
| **Campaign status** | Draft Running Expired Paused |
| **Audience status** | Processing Ready |
| **Audience type**** | ABM audience |
| **Audience reach** | 10 |

***Healthcare:** Any campaign created under a healthcare advertiser account is a “Healthcare” campaign.

****Audience type:** Campaigns typically support targeting multiple audience types. A campaign targeting an ABM audience, however, must only include one or more ABM audiences. For example, a campaign can’t target an ABM audience if it’s already targeting a retargeted audience consisting of your website’s past visitors.

context_header: Account Based Marketing (ABM) audience overview › ABM audience pricing
text:
## ABM audience pricing

ABM audiences and their individual audience segments each display a CPM price.

An ABM audience’s CPM price isn’t the total price of each of its individual ABM segments. Instead, its CPM price is the cost of the highest-priced ABM segment. For example, if one audience includes 100 ABM segments, and each segment is priced at a $0.10 CPM price, then the ABM audience’s total CPM price is $0.10. In instances where the audience includes differently priced segments, its total CPM price is the cost of the highest priced segment.

Note that there’s no cost associated with adding ABM segments to an ABM audience. The listed CPM prices will apply once you run a campaign that’s targeting the ABM audience.

text:

| **Example scenario of ABM-segment selections** | **Example ABM audience cost (CPM)** |

| 1 $0.10 CPM segment selected 1 $0.15 CPM segment selected | $0.15 |

context_header: Account Based Marketing (ABM) audience overview › ABM audience filters
text:
## ABM audience filters

You can apply filters to customize your ABM audiences based on precise characteristics of healthcare accounts.

Note that certain filter settings may limit the options that are included in another filter category. For example, if only **New York** is selected in the **State** filter, the available options in the **City** filter will be limited to cities located in New York. Choose your filters in top-to-bottom order when you [Create an ABM audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10560205-create-or-manage-an-account-based-marketing-abm-audience) to ensure that only relevant items can be selected.

| **Filter title** | **Filter description** |
| --- | --- |
| **Health System** | The organization or business entity to which a number of hospitals and/or medical services belong. |
| **Account** | The specific medical practice that belongs to the **Health System**. The items available in this filter are dependent on your **Health System** filter selections. |
| **Account Type** | The primary medical specialty for which the account is licensed. The items available in this filter are dependent on your **Account** filter selections. |
| **Account Sub-Type** | The sub-category of healthcare practice for which the account is licensed. The items available in this filter are dependent on your **Account Type** filter selections. |
| **NPI Reach** | The number of unique healthcare providers that can be reached based on their National Provider Identifier (NPI). |
| **Specialty** | The specialty that the healthcare professional evaluates, diagnoses, or manages at a medical practice. |
| **State** | The primary state in which the practice operates. |
| **City** | The primary city in which the practice operates. The items available in this filter are dependent on your **State** filter selections. |

context_header: Account Based Marketing (ABM) audience overview › ABM audience statuses
text:
## ABM audience statuses

You can review an ABM audience’s status on the **Account Based Audiences** page of the Audiences app. Refer to [Review an ABM audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10560205-create-or-manage-an-account-based-marketing-abm-audience#h_8880d0aaa2) for more information on how to access this page.

| **Status** | **Definition** |
| --- | --- |
| **Ready** | Your audience is generated. You can review or manage the audience and assign it to a campaign. |
| **Processing** | We’re working on generating your new or duplicated audience. Depending on the audience’s size, this process may take up to 48 hours. |
| **Failed** | You encountered a technical error during audience creation. We’ll attempt to regenerate it for you in a few minutes. |
| **Deleted** | Deleted audiences are automatically removed from the Audiences app as soon as you complete this action. For this reason, none of your ABM audiences will feature a **Deleted** status at any time. |

context_header: Account Based Marketing (ABM) audience overview › Key terms and concepts
text:
### National Provider Identifier (NPI)

ABM audience segments allow you to target NPIs on the account level.

An NPI is a component of the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) and serves as a unique identification number for covered healthcare providers. It’s used to correlate those providers with their respective digital identities.

Refer to [What is NPI Matching?](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8499905-what-is-npi-matching) for more information.

### ABM segment relationships

ABM audiences apply an “OR” relationship to your ABM audience segment selections. This means that your campaign will target a user if they’re included in any of the ABM segments that you added to the audience, as long as all other campaign targeting criteria are met.

context_header: Account Based Marketing (ABM) audience overview › Key terms and concepts
text:
### ABM Audience Breakdown

Once an ABM audience features a **Ready** status, its **Audience Breakdown** will populate with key audience insights across genders, age groups, devices, and geographies. You can review these insights and apply them to your campaign to craft a personalized strategy based on the audience’s key characteristics.

Refer to [Review an ABM audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10560205-create-or-manage-an-account-based-marketing-abm-audience#h_8880d0aaa2) for instructions on how to locate these insights for a given audience.

### Script Lift Study (SLS) and Provider Level Data (PLD) Insights reports

HCP-type ABM audiences are compatible with SLS Insights reports and PLD Insights reports.

SLS Insights reports help you evaluate the effectiveness of your healthcare campaigns based on pre- and post-campaign prescription (Rx/TRx) volumes and competitors’ prescription patterns. Refer to the [Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights reports collection](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/12083517-script-lift-study-sls-insights-reports) for more information.

PLD Insights reports help you uncover ad-exposure and engagement data, demographic data, and physician-specialty data for your healthcare campaigns. Refer to the [Provider Level Data (PLD) Insights reports collection](https://help.iqm.com/en/collections/12010878-provider-level-data-pld-insights-reports) for more information.
