section_path: Remove an audience from a campaign
context_header: Assign an audience to a campaign › Remove an audience from a campaign
text:
## Remove an audience from a campaign

You can remove an audience from a campaign in the following ways:

- From the Campaigns app
- From the Audiences app

article_title: Assign an audience to a campaign
section_path: Remove an audience from a campaign
context_header: Assign an audience to a campaign › Remove an audience from a campaign › Campaigns app
text:
### Campaigns app

Follow these steps to remove an audience that’s currently assigned to a campaign from the Campaigns app:

1. Follow steps 1 through 4 of the Campaigns app - Existing campaign workflow to open the campaign.
2. In the **Remove** column, select the trashcan icon next to each audience that you’d like to remove from the campaign.
3. Save your changes.
   1. Select **Save as Draft** to apply the changes in a draft format.
   2. Select **Run** to apply the changes and create the campaign.
   3. Select **Save** if the campaign is already running to apply your changes to the active campaign.

The campaign will no longer target the audience(s) that you removed. Note that the audience(s) will remain available in the Audiences app, and other campaigns that are targeting the audience(s) won’t be impacted.

article_title: Assign an audience to a campaign
section_path: Remove an audience from a campaign
context_header: Assign an audience to a campaign › Remove an audience from a campaign › Audiences app
text:
### Audiences app

Follow these steps to remove an audience that’s currently assigned to one or more campaigns from the Audiences app:

1. Follow steps 1 through 4 of the Audiences app - Existing campaign workflow.
2. Select the checkbox(es) next to the desired campaigns.
   1. Select the checkbox in the header row of the table to select all assigned campaigns instead.
3. Click **Unassign**.
4. Select **Update** to apply your changes.

The campaign(s) will no longer target the audience that you removed. Note that the audience will remain available in the Audiences app, and other campaigns that are targeting it won’t be impacted.

context_header: Campaign scheduling (dayparting) overview › Campaign scheduling overview
text:
## Campaign scheduling overview

Add campaign scheduling settings to a campaign to spend more effectively and engage your audience when they are most likely to be consuming digital media.

Not every time of day or day of the week is ideal for every business. For example, you may want to reflect your business’s operating hours. Your target audience’s online behavior can also vary depending on factors like their work schedule, lifestyle, and even the type of device they use.

With campaign scheduling, you can set a weekly schedule to determine when your ads will be displayed. These settings help ensure your message reaches the right users, and at the right time.

The way in which you’ll set up scheduling can differ by platform. For example, certain platforms will prompt you to choose days and times to block, while others will prompt you to choose days and times to permit. In the IQM platform, you’ll choose which days and times you’d like for your ads to appear. All non-selected days and times will be blocked from serving ad impressions to users.

Refer to [Schedule a campaign’s ads (dayparting)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11498313-schedule-a-campaign-s-ads-dayparting) to apply your preferred settings to new or existing campaigns.

context_header: Campaign scheduling (dayparting) overview › Key terms and concepts › Cell colors
text:
### Cell colors

A campaign can only serve impressions to users during the days and times that are selected:

- **White cells:** The campaign is blocked from serving impressions during this time period.
- **Blue cells:** The campaign is permitted to serve impressions during this time period. By default, all days and times are selected for all campaigns, meaning that there are no restrictions placed on the days or times that the campaign can serve impressions to users.

section_path: Cell colors example – Campaign scheduling settings are not applied
context_header: Campaign scheduling (dayparting) overview › Key terms and concepts › Cell colors › Cell colors example – Campaign scheduling settings are not applied
text:
#### Cell colors example – Campaign scheduling settings are not applied

An advertiser creates a new campaign with no **Scheduling** settings applied to it. This campaign is permitted to serve impressions on any day of the week, and at any time.

If the advertiser changes their mind and selects one or more time ranges to target, then any days and times that aren’t selected (**White cells**) will be blocked from serving impressions. Refer to Cell colors example – Campaign scheduling settings are applied for more information.

section_path: Cell colors example – Campaign scheduling settings are applied
context_header: Campaign scheduling (dayparting) overview › Key terms and concepts › Cell colors example – Campaign scheduling settings are applied
text:
### Cell colors example – Campaign scheduling settings are applied

An advertiser creates a new campaign and wants to apply **Scheduling** settings to it. By default, the campaign is permitted to serve impressions on any day of the week, and at any time. The advertiser chooses which days and times to block (**White cells**) and which days and times to allow (**Blue cells**) ad serving.

In this example, the advertiser adds the **Scheduling** settings shown above. Refer to the table below for more details on the campaign’s ad-serving behavior based on these settings for a given day of the week and time frame. In summary, the campaign is allowed to serve ad impressions between 6:00am-6:59am on Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays, Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays; and between 12:00am-5:59am and 7:00am-11:59pm on Wednesdays.

| **Day** | **Time Block** | **Cell Color** | **Serving Behavior** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Monday** | 12:00am-5:59am | White (unselected) | Blocked from serving |
| **Monday** | 6:00am-6:59am | Blue (selected) | Allowed to serve |
| **Monday** | 7:00am-11:59pm | White (unselected) | Blocked from serving |
| **Tuesday** | 12:00am-5:59am | White (unselected) | Blocked from serving |
| **Tuesday** | 6:00am-6:59am | Blue (selected) | Allowed to serve |
| **Tuesday** | 7:00am-11:59pm | White (unselected) | Blocked from serving |
| **Wednesday** | 12:00am-5:59am | Blue (selected) | Allowed to serve |
| **Wednesday** | 6:00am-6:59am | White (unselected) | Blocked from serving |
| **Wednesday** | 7:00am-11:59pm | Blue (selected) | Allowed to serve |
| **Thursday** | 12:00am-5:59am | White (unselected) | Blocked from serving |
| **Thursday** | 6:00am-6:59am | Blue (selected) | Allowed to serve |
| **Thursday** | 7:00am-11:59pm | White (unselected) | Blocked from serving |
| **Friday** | 12:00am-5:59am | White (unselected) | Blocked from serving |
| **Friday** | 6:00am-6:59am | Blue (selected) | Allowed to serve |
| **Friday** | 7:00am-11:59pm | White (unselected) | Blocked from serving |
| **Saturday** | 12:00am-5:59am | White (unselected) | Blocked from serving |
| **Saturday** | 6:00am-6:59am | Blue (selected) | Allowed to serve |
| **Saturday** | 7:00am-11:59pm | White (unselected) | Blocked from serving |
| **Sunday** | 12:00am-5:59am | White (unselected) | Blocked from serving |
| **Sunday** | 6:00am-6:59am | Blue (selected) | Allowed to serve |
| **Sunday** | 7:00am-11:59pm | White (unselected) | Blocked from serving |

Since the advertiser selected individual time ranges to target (**Blue cells**), any days and times that aren’t selected will be blocked from serving impressions (**White cells**).

context_header: Schedule a campaign's ads (dayparting) › Campaign scheduling overview
text:
## Campaign scheduling overview

With campaign scheduling, you can set a weekly schedule to determine when your ads will be displayed to your target audience. By default, every campaign is permitted to serve impressions on any day of the week, and at any time. If you would like to schedule ads instead, you’ll select the specific dates and times that you’d like to allow, and any dates and times you don’t select will be blocked from serving ad impressions.

Refer to [Campaign scheduling (dayparting) overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11498297-campaign-scheduling-dayparting-overview#h_aa002a8c54) for more details on how your campaign’s scheduling settings are executed.

context_header: Schedule a campaign's ads (dayparting) › Schedule a campaign’s ads
text:
## Schedule a campaign’s ads

You can add scheduling settings to a new or existing campaign from the Campaigns app:

- From the Campaigns app - Existing campaign
- From the Campaigns app - New campaign

context_header: Schedule a campaign's ads (dayparting) › Schedule a campaign’s ads › Campaigns app - Existing campaign
text:
### Campaigns app - Existing campaign

Follow these steps to schedule ads for a campaign that you’ve already created:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Select the insertion order (IO), and search or browse the IO’s campaigns to locate the one for which you want to add scheduling settings.
3. Click the campaign’s name in the Campaign Name column. You’ll be redirected to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add or update its targeting parameters, including scheduling details.
4. Locate and expand the **Scheduling** section.
5. Click the checkbox in the top-left corner of the table to deselect all cells.
6. Choose which days and times the campaign will be allowed to serve ad impressions:
   1. Click individual cells to allow ad serving for an individual hour-hour time block.
   2. Click a time heading to allow ad serving during that time on every day of the week.
   3. Click a day heading to allow ad serving during any time on that day of the week.
   4. Click a cell and drag your cursor to select multiple time blocks at once to allow ad serving during those selected days and times.
7. If desired, save your campaign’s targeting settings as a new [campaign template](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign#h_49ff912ba6).
8. Click **Save** to apply the new schedule to the existing campaign.

The campaign will be allowed to serve ad impressions during the selected days and times (**Blue cells**), and will be blocked from serving impressions during any unselected days and times (**White cells**). Refer to [Campaign scheduling (dayparting) overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11498297-campaign-scheduling-dayparting-overview) to review examples and more details on how your campaign’s scheduling settings are executed in the IQM platform.

text:
### Campaigns app - New campaign

Follow these steps to schedule ads for a new campaign:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Select the insertion order (IO) to arrive at the **Insertion Order Info** page.
3. Click **+ Create Campaign**. You’ll be redirected to a landing page for the new campaign, where you can add or update its details and targeting parameters.
4. Locate and expand the **Scheduling** section.
5. Click the checkbox in the top-left corner of the table to deselect all cells.
6. Choose which days and times the campaign will be allowed to serve ad impressions:
   1. Click individual cells to allow ad serving for an individual hour-hour time block.
   2. Click a time heading to allow ad serving during that time on every day of the week.
   3. Click a day heading to allow ad serving during any time on that day of the week.
   4. Click a cell and drag your cursor to select multiple time blocks at once to allow ad serving during those selected days and times.
7. If desired, save your campaign’s targeting settings as a new [campaign template](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign#h_49ff912ba6).
8. Click **Save as Draft** to apply your changes to the campaign in a draft format, or select **Run** if you’ve completed all other required and applicable sections for this campaign.

The campaign will be allowed to serve ad impressions during the selected days and times (**Blue cells**), and will be blocked from serving impressions during any unselected days and times (**White cells**). Refer to [Campaign scheduling (dayparting) overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11498297-campaign-scheduling-dayparting-overview) to review examples and more details on how your campaign’s scheduling settings are executed in the IQM platform.

context_header: Schedule a campaign's ads (dayparting) › Remove a campaign’s scheduling settings
text:
## Remove a campaign’s scheduling settings

Follow these steps to clear a campaign’s existing scheduling settings:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Select the insertion order (IO), and search or browse the IO’s campaigns to locate the one for which you want to add scheduling settings.
3. Click the campaign’s name in the **Campaign Name** column. You’ll be redirected to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add or update its targeting parameters, including scheduling details.
4. Locate and expand the **Scheduling** section.
5. Select the checkbox in the top-left corner of the table to select all cells.
   1. You’ll know that all scheduling settings are successfully cleared once the calendar grid shows only blue cells. If the calendar grid shows only white cells, then the campaign will be blocked from serving ad impressions at any time. Review [Key terms and concepts: Cell colors](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11498297-campaign-scheduling-dayparting-overview#h_c7190a67ab) for more details.
6. Click Save to apply your changes to the existing campaign.

With all cells selected in the Scheduling section, this campaign is now allowed to serve impressions on any day of the week, and at any time of the day.

## Campaigns FAQ

context_header: Campaigns frequently asked questions (FAQ) › Campaign function FAQ
text:
##### Q: What is the purpose of a campaign?

**A:** The primary function of a campaign is to define how you’ll serve ads, when those ads will be served, and where they’ll be placed. It contains a set of targeting parameters, an ad format and versions, bidding strategies, and any other targeting settings that you specify. You’ll set these parameters at the start of a campaign and adjust them throughout its flight to optimize performance.

Refer to [Campaigns overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview) for more information.

##### Q: How do campaigns differ from IOs?

**A:** While campaigns include individual strategies, IOs function as an organizational framework. They’re the parent hierarchy that houses a set of campaigns, which you can oversee and manage individually or as a group.

Refer to [Campaigns versus insertion orders (IOs)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_1b806ca883) for more information on the individual functions that can be managed at the campaign level and/or IO level.

context_header: Campaigns frequently asked questions (FAQ) › Campaign function FAQ › Q: Are campaigns in the IQM platform the same as campaigns in other demand-side platforms (DSPs)?
text:
##### Q: Are campaigns in the IQM platform the same as campaigns in other demand-side platforms (DSPs)?

**A:** The naming conventions of both IOs and campaigns differ by DSP. Refer to the table below for a comparison of common naming conventions across DSPs.

| **Platform** | **Parent Hierarchy** | **Child Hierarchy** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **IQM** | IO | Campaign |
| **DV360, Xandr Invest** | IO | Line Item |
| **Beeswax** | Campaign | Line Item |
| **Adelphic, Samsung Ads** | Campaign | Flight |
| **GroundTruth, The Trade Desk** | Campaign | Ad Group |
| **Basis** | Campaign Groups | Campaign |

section_path: Q: What is the purpose of a campaign budget?
context_header: Campaigns frequently asked questions (FAQ) › Campaign budget FAQ › Q: What is the purpose of a campaign budget?
text:
##### Q: What is the purpose of a campaign budget?

**A:** A campaign budget determines the total amount of monetary spend or impressions that you’d like to allocate to that particular strategy. The campaign will stop serving impressions once it reaches that amount, even if its End Date hasn’t been reached.

Note that the IO’s budget, however, ensures that all assigned campaigns will stop serving once their cumulative spend reaches the monetary budget or impression budget that you’ve defined. In other words, the IO’s budget settings supersede an individual campaign’s budget settings when the IO budget is reached before the campaign budget.

context_header: Campaigns frequently asked questions (FAQ) › Campaign budget FAQ
text:
##### Q: Should I choose a monetary budget or impression budget for my campaigns?

**A:** The choice between a monetary or impression depends on your goals, budget preferences and flexibility, and desired outcomes. Refer to [Budget-based and impression-based insertion order (IO) overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8481053-budget-based-and-impression-based-insertion-order-io-overview) to learn more about the differences between these IO types and inform which type you should create for your campaigns.

##### Q: How do campaign budgets differ from IO budgets?

**A:** Your IO-budget settings outweigh individual campaigns’ budget settings. The cumulative monetary spend or impressions of the campaigns associated with an IO won’t exceed the IO budget. This remains true even if an individual campaign hasn’t yet reached its campaign-level budget.

context_header: Campaigns frequently asked questions (FAQ) › Campaign budget FAQ
text:
##### Q: What happens if the sum of my campaigns’ budgets exceed the budget of the IO that they’re associated with?

**A:** All campaigns associated with the IO will stop service once their cumulative monetary spend or impression spend reaches the IO budget that you’ve set. Each individual campaign will stop serving if they reach the IO budget or their individual campaign budget—whichever event occurs first.

##### Q: Why did my campaign stop serving ads even though it didn’t reach its budget?

**A:** A campaign may stop serving ads when any of the following are true:

- The campaign reached its individual budget.
- The campaign’s parent IO reached its budget, meaning that this campaign and all other campaigns associated with it will stop serving regardless of their individual budgets.
- The campaign reached its End Date.
- The campaign’s parent IO reached its End Date, meaning that this campaign and all other campaigns associated with it will stop serving regardless of their individual End Dates.

section_path: Q: Can I restart ad serving for a campaign after the campaign budget was reached?
context_header: Campaigns frequently asked questions (FAQ) › Campaign budget FAQ › Q: Can I restart ad serving for a campaign after the campaign budget was reached?
text:
##### Q: Can I restart ad serving for a campaign after the campaign budget was reached?

**A:** Yes, you can increase the campaign’s monetary or impression budget at any time. The campaign will automatically begin serving if the budget is increased and the campaign hasn’t reached its End Date.

context_header: Campaigns frequently asked questions (FAQ) › Campaign creation and management FAQ
text:
##### Q: How can I create a new campaign?

**A:** Refer to [Create or manage a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign) for step-by-step instructions on creating a new campaign.

##### Q: How can I manage (Review, Edit, Duplicate, Reactivate, Measure, Optimize, Restore) an existing campaign?

**A:** Refer to [Create or manage a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign) for step-by-step instructions on managing an existing campaign.

##### Q: Can I assign the same campaign to multiple IOs?

**A:** No, the IO you choose during campaign creation will remain associated with it and govern its settings. Additional IOs aren’t supported.

context_header: Campaigns frequently asked questions (FAQ) › Campaign creation and management FAQ
text:
##### Q: How does my campaign’s Start Date and End Date differ from the IO’s Start Date and End Date?

**A:** The IO’s Start Date and End Date outweighs campaign-level date settings. The IO’s date settings are definitive, and campaigns won’t serve ads outside of these dates even if their individual dates occur before or after this time frame.

##### Q: Can I change an existing campaign’s budget (budget-based, impression-based) settings?

**A:** No, a campaign’s **Budget Type** settings are inherited from the IO that it’s associated with. The IO and all of its associated campaigns will continue to reflect the budget-based or impression-based settings that you initially chose during setup.

section_path: Q: Why is my campaign pacing behind, and how can I fix it?
context_header: Campaigns frequently asked questions (FAQ) › Campaign creation and management FAQ › Q: Why is my campaign pacing behind, and how can I fix it?
text:
##### Q: Why is my campaign pacing behind, and how can I fix it?

**A:** In most cases, a campaign paces behind when bid prices are too low to win in programmatic auctions, or when a campaign’s targeting rules are too restrictive. For example:

- The daily Max Bid is too low and should be increased.
- The target audience is too small, and additional audiences should be added.
- The target audience was large enough, but other parameters such as geotargeting made it smaller, and should be removed or expanded.
- The targeted creative(s)’ sizes are different from those outlined in [Creative ad specs and requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019246-creative-ad-specs-and-requirements).
- The targeted creative(s)’ [Advanced Targeting (Video)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide#h_29233aacf8) or [Advanced Targeting (Audio)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide#h_301973f77a) settings are too restrictive and should be adjusted or removed.
- The [Frequency Capping](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-bid-strategy-overview#h_a8647394e9) settings are too restrictive and should be increased.
- The targeted inventory group(s)’ scale is too limited and should be broadened.

Refer to [Troubleshoot a campaign that’s pacing behind](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471960-troubleshoot-a-campaign-that-s-pacing-behind) for more support with uncovering the primary factors that are influencing a specific campaigns’ pacing performance, and applying any necessary changes to help ensure it spends full.

section_path: Q: What does each campaign status mean?
context_header: Campaigns frequently asked questions (FAQ) › Campaign creation and management FAQ › Q: What does each campaign status mean?
text:
##### Q: What does each campaign status mean?

**A:** A **Draft** campaign is one that you’ve started creating but haven’t chosen to **Run**.

A **Pending** campaign is one that you chose to **Run**, but it’s currently under review and will begin serving once it’s approved.

A **Rejected** campaign is one that you chose to **Run**, but it wasn’t approved. You’ll need to make the required updates before it can move to a **Running** status.

A **Running** campaign was approved and is within the Start Date and End Date that you selected, and its monetary or impression budget hasn’t been reached.

A **Paused** campaign has temporarily stopped serving because you chose to suspend it. It will resume serving once you choose to **Run** it if its End Date hasn’t been reached and the IO it’s associated with hasn’t reached its IO budget.

A **Deleted** campaign was manually deleted by a user. You can view a **Deleted** campaign, but you can’t reactivate it.

An **Expired** campaign reached its End Date. You can update the End Date to restore the campaign if you’d like for it to continue serving ads. Refer to [Restore an expired campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign#h_a0301f8c39) for step-by-step instructions.

context_header: Campaigns frequently asked questions (FAQ) › Campaign creation and management FAQ
text:
##### Q: Why does my campaign still feature a Running status after it reaches its budget?

**A:** The status of a campaign remains **Running** if its End Date hasn’t yet been reached, regardless of spend or budget. However, the individual campaign will stop serving impressions once the IO budget or individual campaign budget is reached–whichever event takes place first. Campaigns will feature a warning icon next to their names in the IQM platform when ad serving has stopped.

##### Q: What happens when a campaign features an Expired status?

**A:** A campaign features an **Expired** status once its End Date is reached. The campaign will stop serving ads when its status changes from **Running** to **Expired**.

You can extend a campaign’s End Date to restore its **Running** status and resume serving ads. Refer to [Restore an expired campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign#h_a0301f8c39) for step-by-step instructions.

context_header: Campaigns frequently asked questions (FAQ) › Campaign creation and management FAQ
text:
##### What makes a campaign eligible for AI Insights?

**A:** Refer to [Campaigns overview: CampaignPulse eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_7a4988ae55) for all eligibility criteria and related details.

##### Q: How often will a campaign run AI Insights?

**A:** All [eligible](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_7a4988ae55) campaigns are automatically and continuously monitored by the “CampaignPulse” AI Insights feature. CampaignPulse will surface when something needs attention without the need to manually check in.

If you’d like to check in sooner than the automatic monitoring would, you can manually run the “CampaignPulse” AI Insights feature for an [eligible](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_7a4988ae55) campaign by following the steps outlined in [Create or manage a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign) or [Manage a campaign from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard).

context_header: Campaigns frequently asked questions (FAQ) › Campaign creation and management FAQ
text:
##### Q: Can I manually run the CampaignPulse feature for a campaign?

**A:** Yes. You can manually run the “CampaignPulse” AI Insights feature for an [eligible](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_7a4988ae55) campaign by following the steps outlined in [Create or manage a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651476-create-or-manage-a-campaign) or [Manage a campaign from a dashboard](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471766-manage-a-campaign-from-a-dashboard).

##### Q: What campaign performance elements does AI Insights check?

**A:** CampaignPulse checks for human errors, conflicting campaign settings, and account issues that could put your campaigns at medium or high risk.

This feature continuously monitors campaign health to discover issues that could limit or stop ad delivery. It highlights actionable insights across account readiness, campaign setup, targeting, budgeting, delivery settings, and more to help keep campaigns running smoothly.

Review all CampaignPulse delivery insights closely for instructions on how to address the issues that can put your campaigns at risk.

context_header: Campaigns frequently asked questions (FAQ) › Campaign creation and management FAQ
text:
##### Q: What should I do if my campaign is underperforming but it passes all AI Insights checks?

**A:** The “CampaignPulse” AI Insights feature is designed to help you detect and address significant risks to campaign delivery. For other campaign-optimization tools and strategies, refer to [Optimization overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12004298-optimization-overview).

##### Q: Is there an AI Insights feature for insertion orders (IO)?

**A:** No. Instead of reflecting targeting details and requirements, IOs function as an organizational framework. The primary function of an IO is to provide an effective means of organizing and managing campaigns that share similar traits. It’s also a means of managing the budgets of those campaigns.

CampaignPulse does, however, assess certain IO-level settings that can impact a campaign’s ability to serve ad impressions. Refer to [Campaigns overview: CampaignPulse delivery insights](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497668-campaigns-overview#h_595b0bbe29) for a comprehensive list and related details.

context_header: Set or manage campaign priorities › Campaign priority overview
text:
## Campaign priority overview

Campaign priority settings allow you to take control of the way your insertion order’s (IO) individual campaigns deliver their impressions. These settings are optional but recommended as they establish a sequential order of bidding once you choose the order in which each campaign should be executed. These priorities can range from 1 to 10, with smaller numbers indicating a higher priority, and larger numbers indicating a lower priority.

Refer to [Campaign priority overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9090645-campaign-priority-overview) for more information on how campaign priorities work and to learn what makes a campaign eligible for these settings.

context_header: Set or manage campaign priorities › Set or manage campaign priorities
text:
## Set or manage campaign priorities

> **More on bulk edits:** Note that, while applying priorities in bulk in supported, bulk edits are reserved for when multiple campaigns will feature the same priority.

You’ll follow the same steps to set a campaign’s priority for the first time, or to change or remove a campaign’s priority. You can complete these processes for one campaign at a time or in bulk.

section_path: Set or manage campaign priorities individually
context_header: Set or manage campaign priorities › Set or manage campaign priorities › Set or manage campaign priorities individually
text:
### Set or manage campaign priorities individually

Follow these steps to apply priorities to one campaign at a time:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Search or browse your existing insertion orders (IOs) to locate the one that should serve as the parent hierarchy for the campaign(s) that you’ll create.
3. Click on the name of the desired IO. This will open the **Insertion Order Info** page, which lists each of the campaigns that you’ve associated with the IO.
4. Locate the **Priority** column and select the cell next to the desired campaign.
5. Type a whole number between 1 and 10 to indicate the campaign’s priority.
   1. The highest priority is 1 and the lowest priority is 10.
6. Select the checkmark icon to apply the new or updated priority, or select the cancel icon to discard your changes.

section_path: Set or manage campaign priorities in bulk
context_header: Set or manage campaign priorities › Set or manage campaign priorities › Set or manage campaign priorities in bulk
text:
### Set or manage campaign priorities in bulk

Follow these steps to assign the same priority to multiple campaigns:

1. Follow steps 1 through 3 of the Set or manage campaign priorities individually workflow.
2. Select the checkbox next to each campaign that should feature the same priority.
3. Click **Set Priority**. This will open the **Set/Change Priority** pop-up window.
   1. The **Set Priority** button is enabled only when the selected campaign(s) meet the [eligibility criteria](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9090645-campaign-priority-overview#h_8da0e61031).
4. Type a whole number between 1 and 10 to indicate the priority of the selected campaigns.
   1. The highest priority is 1 and the lowest priority is 10.
5. Select **Set** to add a priority to the campaign for the first time, or **Change** to apply your edits to an existing priority setting.

You can extend an IO’s End Date to restore its **Running** status and resume serving ads.

text:
## Matched audience overview

Matched audiences are made up of users from your first-party data such as Customer Relationship Management (CRM) data for specialty campaigns, NPI lists for Healthcare campaigns, or past voters for Political campaigns, for example.

You’ll add your customer lists to the Matched audience. While the audience is generating, it recognizes consumers across channels and devices through IQM’s privacy-compliant [Identity Graph](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8615247-iqm-identity-graph), which unifies offline and online identifiers to a single profile. Targeting this segment allows you to reach these offline users through digital channels.

Review this article for more details and requirements, and refer to [Create or manage a Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience) to upload a file for audience matching.

text:
### HCP, Nurse, Non-NPI Nurse, Patient, and Generic Matched audiences (Healthcare)

> Access to Patient Matched audiences is currently limited to users participating in a closed, invitation-only beta testing program. General availability for this feature is coming soon.

Matched audiences help ensure maximum unique reach to the healthcare professionals or current and future patients who move the needle for your healthcare brand.

NPI-based HCP and Nurse Matched audiences deliver industry-leading NPI match rates to reach your campaign’s most relevant healthcare professionals. We directly ingest NPI numbers from leading industry sources, which power our identity graph with over 80% coverage of the HCP universe and result in maximum unique campaign reach. Refer to [Create an NPI-based (HCP, Nurse) Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience#h_f59a22b312) to upload your NPI list for audience matching.

Certain healthcare professionals, such as nurses who don’t bill for services, aren’t assigned an NPI number. You can still reach these individuals by generating and targeting Non-NPI Nurse audiences. Refer to [Create or manage a Non-NPI Nurse Matched audience (Healthcare)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience#h_577bcf29d2) for more details.

Drive patient awareness and loyalty with Patient Matched audiences. Add user lists to continue the conversation with these current and potential customers across their connected devices. Refer to [Create a Patient Matched audience (Healthcare)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience#h_e0d104b9ee) to upload your patient list for audience matching.

The option to create an HCP, Nurse, Non-NPI Nurse, or Patient Matched audience is optional: Healthcare advertisers can choose to [Create a Generic Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience#h_ae53aae5b9) instead, if desired.

### Voter ID Matched audiences (Political)

When you create a Matched audience from a list of Voter IDs or Voter emails, phone numbers, or addresses; you supercharge your political campaigns based on known user details. Target the right audience with personalized messaging both inside and outside of election cycles to stay top-of-mind for voters.

For Political Matched audiences created after August 20, 2026, both Reach and Household Reach metrics are available.

Refer to [Create a Matched audience (Specialty, Political)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience#h_a50f1a4473) to upload your voter list for audience matching.

context_header: Matched audience overview › Matched audience eligibility requirements
text:
## Matched audience eligibility requirements

All advertisers are eligible to create and target Matched audiences. The types of Matched audience segments you can create, however, depend on the brand’s vertical. For example, only Healthcare advertisers are eligible to [upload a file for NPI matching](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience#h_9c96dd379b), and only Political advertisers are eligible to [upload a voter file for audience matching](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience#h_a50f1a4473).

The following conditions must also be met before an advertiser or campaign becomes eligible for Matched audience targeting:

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| **Advertiser vertical*** | Specialty Healthcare Political |
| **Campaign type** | Advanced |
| **Campaign status** | Draft Running Expired Paused |
| **File format** | CSV XLSX |
| **File contents - Non-Voter file** | First Name, Last Name, ZIP Code, and State -*OR*- Last Name, Street Address, ZIP Code, and State -*OR*- Street Address, ZIP Code, and State |
| **File contents - Voter file** | Voter ID -*AND/OR*- Voter Email -*AND/OR*- Voter Phone Number -*AND/OR*- Voter Street Address, City, ZIP Code, and State |
| **File records (rows)** | 25 (minimum) to 5M (maximum) |
| **Audience status** | Processing Ready |
| **Audience type**** | Matched Segmented Retargeted Geofarmed Contextual Lookalike Campaign Pre-bid |
| **Audience reach** | 100 |

***Advertiser vertical: Specialty** advertisers are eligible to create and target Matched audiences that include only non-Healthcare and non-Political data. **Healthcare** advertisers may be eligible to create and target Matched audiences that include Specialty and/or NPI data. **Political** advertisers may be eligible to create and target Matched audiences that include Specialty and/or voter audience data.

****Audience type:** Campaigns typically support targeting multiple audience types. A campaign targeting an NPI-based audience, however, must only include one or more NPI-based audiences. For example, a campaign can’t target an HCP Matched audience if it’s already targeting a Retargeted audience consisting of your website's past visitors.

text:
## Matched audience insights

> **Matched audience eligibility notice:** Audience Insights reports are available for eligible standard Matched audiences, Voter ID Matched audiences, NPI-based HCP or Nurse Matched audiences, and Non-NPI based Nurse Matched audiences. Patient Matched audiences are not supported.

The Audience Insights report surfaces insights about users that you add to a Matched audience. It includes data such as audience characteristics, interests, and behaviors. The report also includes a **National Average** and **Audience Value** for each metric. The delta between these values measures how much of the audience deviates from the average population in terms of demographic, geographic, interest, and more. You can use this data to identify areas where the audience is unique, and tailor your marketing strategies and creatives accordingly.

Generate and apply these insights at no charge to gain a holistic and in-depth view of user attributes and craft highly targeted and personalized campaigns.

Refer to these resources to learn more about generating Audience Insights reports for your Matched audiences:

- [Audience Insights report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8337863-audience-insights-report-overview#h_cba54235f2)
- [Audience Insights report metrics](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8337863-audience-insights-report-overview#h_cba54235f2)
- [Generate or manage an Audience Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8337876-generate-or-manage-an-audience-insights-report)

context_header: Matched audience overview › Matched audience statuses
text:
## Matched audience statuses

You can review a Matched audience’s status on the **Matched Audience** page of the Audiences app. Refer to [Review a Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience#h_ff01825ca6) for more information on how to access this page.

| **Status** | **Definition** |
| --- | --- |
| **Ready** | Your audience is generated. You can review or manage the audience and [assign it to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience#h_153d1c7dfb). |
| **Ready (Re-Matching)** | The audience is currently undergoing the Re-Match process. Associated campaigns will continue to target the existing audience until the Re-Matching process is complete. |
| **Processing** | We’re working on generating your new or duplicated audience. Depending on the audience’s size, this process may take up to 48 hours. |
| **Pending** | Your audience is pending for approval. |
| **Failed** | You encountered a technical error during audience creation. We’ll attempt to regenerate it for you in a few minutes. |
| **Deleted** | Deleted audiences are automatically removed from the Audiences app as soon as you complete this action. For this reason, none of your Matched audiences will feature a **Deleted** status at any time. |

context_header: Matched audience overview › Key terms and concepts › Records, Match Rate, and Reach
text:
### Records, Match Rate, and Reach

> **More on metric calculations:** Certain metric calculations for Matched audiences can vary based on the type of file you upload when you create the audience. Refer to Metric calculations by file contents for more information.

When a Matched audience reaches a **Ready** status, it includes three metrics: **Records**, **Match Rate**, and **Reach**. Political Matched audiences also include **Household Reach**.

**Records** are the total number of line items—individual IDs or addresses, for example—across all of the source files that you uploaded when you created the Matched audiences. In other words, **Records** represent the number of those files’ rows.

The audience’s **Match Rate** represents the percentage of users whose digital identities we were able to correlate to the identifiers that you included in your source file(s). The average match rate on the IQM platform is 80%.

In campaign reporting, **Reach** represents the number of unique individuals who were exposed to your ad. In Matched audiences, however, this metric represents the total targetable audience (unique users) that you can potentially reach by targeting that particular audience. Note that the actual addressable audience will become smaller as you apply additional targeting rules and other settings to your campaign.

When you multiply the Matched audience’s total number of **Records** by its **Match Rate**, you’re left with the audience’s **Reach**. For example, if your audience achieves a 99.7% **Match Rate** and includes 1,000 **Records**, then the audience’s **Reach** is 997.

context_header: Matched audience overview › Key terms and concepts › Records, Match Rate, and Reach › Achieving optimal Match Rates
text:
#### Achieving optimal Match Rates

You’re more likely to achieve optimal Match Rates for an audience when you:

- Include as much accurate data as possible in the file you upload when you [Create a Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience).
- Ensure the file’s data is accurate and properly formatted. Start by downloading the **Sample File** to check whether your file is formatted correctly as only correctly formatted rows can match.

context_header: Matched audience overview › Key terms and concepts › Metric calculations by file contents
text:
### Metric calculations by file contents

Certain metric calculations for Matched audiences can vary based on the information contained in your file that will be used for audience matching. Refer to the table below for more details.

| **Type** | **Matching** **Criteria** | **Match Rate** **Formula** | **Reach Formula** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Political - Voter | L2 ID | Total Unique Rows Matched/ Total Unique Rows | Total Unique Rows Matched |
| Political - Generic | L2 ID + PII Non-L2 ID Phone/Email Full Address PII | Total Unique Rows Matched/ Total Unique Rows | Total Unique Rows Matched |
| Healthcare - HCP | NPI ID NPI ID + PII Phone/Email | Total Unique NPI IDs Matched/ Total Unique NPI IDs | Total Unique NPI IDs Matched |
| Healthcare - Generic | PII Phone/Email | Total Unique Rows Matched/ Total Unique Rows | Total Unique Rows Matched |
| Healthcare - Patient | N/A | Match Rate based on Ramp IDs | Reach based on Ramp IDs |

context_header: Matched audience overview › Key terms and concepts › Household Reach (Political)
text:
### Household Reach (Political)

For Political Matched audiences, **Household Reach** represents the number of distinct households among the audience’s matched voters. IQM uses the Household ID in L2’s voter data, so everyone L2 places in one household counts once.

You can review an audience’s **Household Reach** in the **Household Reach** column next to **Reach** on the **Matched Audience** page, and in the audience’s details. Household Reach is available only for Political Matched audiences created after August 20, 2026.

Because several voters can share a household, an audience’s **Household Reach** is always less than or equal to its **Reach**. For example, if an audience’s **Reach** includes two voters whom L2 places in the same household, they count as one household.

Note that the **Household Reach** metric in campaign reporting is calculated differently. Refer to [Household Reach overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15656937-household-reach-overview) for more information on the campaign reporting metric.

context_header: Matched audience overview › Key terms and concepts › Re-Match
text:
### Re-Match

> **Re-Match notice:** After a Re-Match is complete, the Matched audience’s Reach may increase, decrease, or remain the same. Note that—if the Re-Matched audience is the only mapped audience and its Reach is lower than the original Matched audience’s reach—the campaign may stop delivering. No campaign disruption will occur during Re-Match processing; any associated campaigns will continue to target the existing Matched audience until the process is complete.

Certain Matched audiences support the “Re-Match” feature. Re-Matching will retrigger the audience-matching process, which fetches the most recent and relevant match data and updates the audience’s Reach and Match Rate details.

Note that Re-Matching is not an automated process. You can manually Re-Match an eligible audience by following the steps outlined in [Re-Match a Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience#h_66e99a6202).

text:
#### Re-Match eligibility

Refer to the table below for more details on the factors that impact an audience’s Re-Match eligibility.

| **Audience sub-type** | **Re-Match eligibility criteria** |
| --- | --- |
| Specialty | Every 90 days for audiences with a **Ready** status |
| Political | Every 90 days for audiences with a **Ready** status |
| Healthcare (HCP) | Every 90 days for audiences with a **Ready** status |
| Healthcare (Nurse) | Every 90 days for audiences with a **Ready** status |
| Healthcare (Non-NPI Nurse) | Every 90 days for audiences with a **Ready** status |
| Healthcare (Patient) | Until 21 days from creation date for audiences with a **Failed** status |

context_header: Matched audience overview › Key terms and concepts › National Provider Identifier (NPI)
text:
#### NPI numbers

A National Provider Identifier (NPI) is a 10-digit numeric identifier. It’s a component of the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) that serves as a unique identification number for covered healthcare providers.

#### NPI matching

When you create a Matched audience from an NPI list, you correlate these providers with their respective digital identities while upholding stringent data privacy regulations. This process enables you to effectively deliver healthcare-related ads that reach the appropriate medical professionals.

Advertisers who’d like to leverage NPI lists for audience matching should [Create an NPI-based (HCP, Nurse) Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience#h_f59a22b312).

context_header: Matched audience overview › Key terms and concepts › Data privacy measures for Matched audiences
text:
### Data privacy measures for Matched audiences

IQM’s identity graph is fully privacy compliant. IQM doesn’t track any device or cookie with “Do not track” settings enabled, and follows all CCPA and GDPR guidelines. When you create an [ABM audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10560051-account-based-marketing-abm-audience-overview), create a Matched audience with first-party data, or enable other audience-targeting features, you also agree to comply with applicable data laws and regulations including but not limited to GDPR, CCPA, and HIPAA.

IQM takes the following measures to provide a secure and compliant audience-matching solution (NPI matching, Voter matching, and other first-party data matching) that not only benefits our customers but also respects the privacy rights of individuals:

- **HIPAA compliance:** Healthcare advertisers can create Matched audiences from NPI lists, as well as create HCP Matched audiences. Our foremost priority is aligning with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA). This legislation mandates safeguarding individuals' healthcare information, a responsibility we discharge meticulously in our NPI matching process.
- **Robust data encryption:** When NPI, voter, or other first-party data files include personally identifiable information (PII) such as first name, last name, and address, IQM anonymizes the data during the audience-matching process. Files are stored behind a firewall and encrypted in the case of a data breach. The rigorous data encryption measures that we have implemented are intended to preserve the confidentiality and integrity of data. These techniques also ensure data remains shielded during transit and while at rest, mitigating the risk of unauthorized access.
- **Secure data storage:** All data processed within IQM undergoes secure storage, complemented by stringent access controls and comprehensive audit trails. This not only bolsters data security but also establishes traceability, an essential facet for demonstrating compliance.
- **Routine compliance audits:** IQM conducts ongoing compliance audits to ascertain the continued alignment of our NPI, Voter, and other sensitive-data matching processes with the latest data privacy regulations. This unwavering commitment to compliance provides our customers with confidence, knowing they can utilize our platform without encountering legal concerns.

context_header: Create or manage a Matched audience › Create a Matched audience (Specialty, Political)
text:
## Create a Matched audience (Specialty, Political)

Follow these steps to create a Matched audience for Specialty or Political campaigns:

1. Open the Audiences app.
2. Select **Matched Audience**.
3. Click **+ Create New**. This will open the **Create Matched Audience** pop-up window.
4. Enter a name for the audience.
5. Add an XLSX or CSV file containing the customer list or voter list.
   1. Download the **Sample File** to ensure your file is formatted correctly.
   2. If the desired file is stored in your device’s local files and you’d like to upload it, click **Upload File** and select it.
   3. If the desired file is stored in your device’s local files and you’d like to drag and drop it, select the desired file and drag it into any area of the dashed rectangle.
   4. If the desired file is stored in an external account such as Google Drive or Dropbox, select the corresponding company’s icon.
      1. A pop-up window will open and prompt you to log in, accept any applicable privacy settings, and select the desired file from the online drive.
6. Open the **Select Matching Criteria** menu and select the system field(s) contained in your file that will be used for audience matching.
7. If you’re a Political advertiser who uploaded a file containing **Voter ID** contents, make a selection from the **Data Partner** menu.
8. Complete the required **System Fields** and **Uploaded File Columns** in the table.
   1. Click **+ Add Field** to add additional fields to the table.
   2. Only one row is required; however, completing more will help increase the chances of a [high](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview#h_4230c7d4ca)**[Match Rate](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview#h_4230c7d4ca)**.
9. Select **Create**.

Your Matched audience will immediately begin processing. You can monitor its current status by following the steps outlined in Review a Matched audience.

   1. Search by **ID** or **Audience Name**.
   2. Filter by **Status** for all audiences and by **Type** for Healthcare audiences.
   3. Open the column selector to add or remove a table column.
2. Select the desired audience’s ID in the **ID** column. This will open the audience in a pop-up window, where you can review its details.
3. Once the audience features a **Ready** status, you can also review additional data and insights.
   1. Review the audience’s **Reach**, **Records**, **Match Rate**, **Cost (CPM)**, and **Status** in the summary panel.
   2. If you created a Healthcare audience, review the **Type** and **Data Partner** in the summary panel.
   3. Review and/or download the file you uploaded when you created the audience.
4. Select **Done** to close the pop-up window and return to the **Matched Audience** page

article_title: Create or manage a Matched audience

text:
### Re-Match a Matched audience

> **Re-Match notice:** After a Re-Match is complete, the Matched audience’s Reach may increase, decrease, or remain the same. Note that–if the Re-Matched audience is the only mapped audience and its Reach is lower than the original Matched audience’s reach–the campaign may stop delivering. No campaign disruption will occur during Re-Match processing; any associated campaigns will continue to target the existing Matched audience until the process is complete. Refer to [Matched audience overview - Re-Match](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview#h_0cc9c103cf) for more details on audience Re-Matching and eligibility criteria.

Follow these steps to retrigger the audience-matching process, which fetches the most recent and relevant match data and updates the audience’s Reach and Match Rate details:

1. Select the refresh icon next to an eligible audience. This will open the **Confirm Audience Re-Match** pop-up window.
2. Review the disclaimer and select **Re-Match** to confirm your selection.

article_title: Create or manage a Matched audience
context_header: Create or manage a Matched audience › Manage a Matched audience
text:
### Retry a failed Matched audience

Follow these steps to attempt to Re-Match a Matched audience featuring a **Failed** status:

1. Select the refresh icon next to an eligible **Failed** audience. This will open the **Confirm Audience Retry** pop-up window.
2. Review the disclaimer and select **Retry** to confirm your selection.

### Edit a Matched audience

> **More on editing Matched audiences:** Only an existing Matched audience’s name can be edited. If you’d like to apply changes to the audience’s other settings—such as its source file or type—creating a new one instead.

Follow these steps to edit an existing Matched audience’s name:

1. Select the existing name from the table’s **Audience Name** column, and type the new audience name directly in the cell.
2. Click the checkmark icon to confirm your selection.

article_title: Create or manage a Matched audience
context_header: Create or manage a Matched audience › Manage a Matched audience
text:
### Duplicate a Matched audience

Duplication isn't supported for Matched audiences.

Follow the steps outlined in Create a Matched audience (Specialty, Political) or Create a Matched Audience (Healthcare) to create a new audience instead.

### Delete a Matched audience

> **Audience deletion notice:** Note that deleted audiences are unrecoverable, and this action is permanent.

You can delete Matched audiences individually or in bulk. They must feature a **Ready**, **Processing**, or **Failed** status; and their **Allowlist/Blocklist** count must be **0**.

Follow these steps to delete a Matched audience.

1. Select the checkboxes next to the desired audience(s).
2. Click **Delete**.

The deleted audience(s) will no longer appear in the Audiences app.

You can generate, download, and send insights for each of your Matched audiences at no additional cost. These insights provide a holistic and in-depth view of user attributes to help you craft highly targeted and personalized campaigns.

Refer to these dedicated resources to learn more about generating Audience Insights for your Matched audiences:

context_header: Troubleshoot a Matched audience › Matched audience troubleshooting overview
text:
## Matched audience troubleshooting overview

All advertisers can create and target Matched audiences if their account and campaign meet certain eligibility criteria. Advertisers belonging to certain verticals, such as Healthcare and Political, may also be eligible to use NPI data or Voter data to generate audience segments that are specific to those verticals.

If you encounter an error or are blocked from creating, managing, or targeting a Matched audience, refer to these resources first:

- [Matched audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview)
- [Create or manage a Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience)

Return to this article to address and resolve other issues that you may encounter related to Matched audiences.

section_path: Troubleshoot Matched audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Matched audience › Troubleshoot Matched audience creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to duplicate an audience

Duplication isn't supported for Matched audiences.

Follow the steps outlined in [Create a Matched audience (Specialty, Political)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience#h_a50f1a4473) or [Create a Matched Audience (Healthcare)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience#h_9c96dd379b) to create a new audience instead.

### Unable to edit an audience

Only an existing Matched audience’s name can be edited. You can rename an audience directly from the **Matched Audience** table by selecting the cell containing the existing name.

section_path: Troubleshoot Matched audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Matched audience › Troubleshoot Matched audience creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to change an audience’s name

You can change an existing audience’s name by selecting it in the table’s **Audience Name** column.

Type the new audience name directly in the cell, and confirm your selection by clicking the checkmark icon.

### Unable to delete an audience

You can delete audiences individually or in bulk. Every selected audience must be unassigned from all campaigns before you can delete them.

You can easily reference whether an audience is assigned to any campaigns in the **Allowlist/Blocklist** column. Audiences with an **Allowlist/Blocklist** value of **0** can be deleted.

section_path: Troubleshoot Matched audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Matched audience › Troubleshoot Matched audience creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to locate a deleted audience

Deleted audiences are automatically removed from the Audiences app as soon as you complete this action. For this reason, none of the Matched audiences listed in the Audiences app will feature a **Deleted** status.

### Unable to review audience reach

Audience reach details generate automatically once the audience progresses from a **Processing** status to a **Ready** status. Refer to [Matched audience statuses](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview#h_7fca54b9c5) and [Key terms and concepts - Records, Match Rate, and Reach](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview#h_d4f8225cc8) for more information.

section_path: Troubleshoot Matched audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Matched audience › Troubleshoot Matched audience creation or management issues
text:
### Audience is in Processing status

Depending on the size of the Matched audience, it may take 24 to 48 hours for us to complete the audience-matching process. Once completed, the audience’s status will change from **Processing** to **Ready**. If something goes wrong during audience creation, then it’ll feature a **Failed** status instead.

### Unable to locate HCP, Nurse, Non-NPI Nurse, or Patient ( beta ) Matched audience options

> Access to Patient Matched audiences is currently limited to users participating in a closed, invitation-only beta testing program. General availability for this feature is coming soon.

You’ll have the option to select an audience **Type** when you add your audience’s settings. Refer to [Create a Matched audience (Healthcare)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience#h_9c96dd379b) for step-by-step instructions.

Note that only Healthcare advertisers are eligible to create HCP, Nurse, Non-NPI Nurse, or Patient Matched audiences. Contact your account admin if you believe you should have access to these audience-creation options but are unable to locate them in the Audiences app.

section_path: Troubleshoot Matched audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Matched audience › Troubleshoot Matched audience creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to locate Voter Matched audience options

Note that only Political advertisers are eligible to create Matched audiences from voter data. However, Political advertisers can complete this step by creating a standard Matched audience and uploading a file that contains voter details. Refer to [Create a Matched audience (Specialty, Political)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience#h_a50f1a4473) for step-by-step instructions.

### Unable to generate audience insights

You can generate audience insights for Matched audiences that feature a **Ready** status and include at least 10K **Records**. Note that Audience Insights reporting doesn’t currently support Patient Matched audiences; however, all other Matched audience types are supported when they meet the other [eligibility criteria](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8337863-audience-insights-report-overview).

Refer to [Audience Insights report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8337863-audience-insights-report-overview) and [Generate or manage an Audience Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8337876-generate-or-manage-an-audience-insights-report) for additional support.

section_path: Troubleshoot Matched audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Matched audience › Troubleshoot Matched audience creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to further segment an audience

Each file you upload to a Matched audience creates a single target audience. This audience can’t be further segmented.

If you’d like to segment your NPI list, Voter list, or other first-party data into multiple audiences, you’ll need to create one file for each audience you wish to target. Refer to [Create or manage a Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience) for step-by-step instructions.

### Unable to upload additional source files

Each Matched audience can include one source file containing your NPI list, Voter list, or other first-party data. In other words, the ratio of source file to Matched audience is 1:1. Repeat the processes outlined in [Create or manage a Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience) for each audience.

section_path: Troubleshoot Matched audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Matched audience › Troubleshoot Matched audience creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to Re-Match an audience

An audience’s Re-Match eligibility is determined by the audience sub-type and the number of days that have passed since the audience was last created or Re-Matched.

Refer to [Matched audience overview - Re-Match](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview#h_0cc9c103cf) for more details.

### Audience Re-Match failed

An audience undergoing the Re-Match process may fail for any of the following reasons:

- A system error or technical error occurred during processing.
- The newly Re-Matched audience’s Reach would have equaled less than 10 users.

Follow the steps outlined in [Retry a failed Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience#h_a2f9791667) to try again.

context_header: Troubleshoot a Matched audience › Troubleshoot Matched audience targeting issues
text:
### New campaign - Unable to select a PG campaign type

PG campaigns aren’t eligible for Matched audience targeting. When you create a new campaign that will target the Matched audience, the **Advanced** option is selected by default, and the **PG** option is disabled.

### Existing campaign - Unable to add to a PG campaign

Only **Advanced** campaigns are eligible for targeting Matched audiences. For this reason, the **Audiences** section is intentionally excluded from **PG** campaigns.

### Existing campaign - Unable to add to an Advanced campaign

Campaigns typically support targeting multiple audience types. A campaign targeting an ABM audience, however, must only include one or more ABM audiences. For example, a campaign can’t target a Matched audience if it’s already targeting an ABM audience. Refer to [ABM audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10560051-account-based-marketing-abm-audience-overview) for more information, and confirm that the audience is targeting only non-ABM audiences and segments.

If the campaign isn’t targeting an ABM audience, confirm how many audiences it’s targeting instead. One campaign can target up to 20 audiences.

context_header: Troubleshoot a Matched audience › Troubleshoot Matched audience targeting issues
text:
### Existing campaign - Campaign is missing from list

If you’re attempting to add the Matched audience to an existing campaign, and that campaign isn’t available in the **Campaigns** list, the campaign isn’t eligible for Matched audience targeting. Refer to [Matched audience eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview#h_6cd565b71b) for more details.

### Add To Campaign button is disabled

The **Add To Campaign** button becomes disabled when the audience(s) you selected aren’t currently eligible for targeting and/or none of your campaigns are currently eligible.

Confirm that each audience you selected features a **Ready** or **Processing** status, and refer to [Matched audience eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview#h_6cd565b71b) for more details.

context_header: Troubleshoot a Matched audience › Troubleshoot Matched audience targeting issues › Create Campaign button is disabled
text:
### Create Campaign button is disabled

The **Create Campaign** button becomes disabled when the audience(s) you selected aren’t currently eligible for targeting.

Confirm that each audience you selected features a **Ready** or **Processing** status, and refer to [Matched audience eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview#h_6cd565b71b) for more details.

article_title: Create or manage a Segmented audience
context_header: Create or manage a Segmented audience › Segmented audience overview
text:
## Segmented audience overview

> **Partner with Vera:** Vera serves as a versatile partner that simplifies and streamlines complex operations across the campaign lifecycle. This includes creating and managing Matched audiences in the Vera app. Refer to ["Vera - IQM's artificial intelligence (AI) agent" collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/15493648-vera-iqm-s-artificial-intelligence-ai-agent-collection-overview) to get started.

Segmented audiences include groups of users who share common characteristics. You’ll add segments or groups of segments to the audience to reach that unique group of users. These audiences can be highly specific or more broad, depending on your campaign’s goals and your scale considerations.

Refer to [Segmented audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview) for more information and eligibility requirements, or continue reading to create and manage a Segmented audience in the IQM platform.

article_title: Create or manage a Segmented audience
context_header: Create or manage a Segmented audience › Create a Segmented audience
text:
## Create a Segmented audience

You can create one Segmented audience at a time in the Audiences app. Follow these steps to create a new Segmented audience:

1. Open the Audiences app.
2. Select **Segmented Audience**.
3. Click **+ Create New**. This will open the **Create Segmented Audience** pop-up window.
4. Enter a name for the audience.
5. Select the search bar to browse and select audience segments from the data provider of your choice.
   1. Enter search terms, separated by commas, to search for specific audience characteristics.
   2. Download your search results if you’d like to review them in a file.
   3. Sort the segments **By Reach** or **By Price**.
   4. Filter by **Vertical** or **Source** to refine your search results.
   5. Select one or more audience segments to add them to the audience, and note that all segments added to this [Segment Group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview#h_31da47f45c) are assigned an [“OR” relationship](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview#h_31da47f45c).
6. If desired, select **+ Add Segment Group** to a new group.
   1. Choose whether the segments in the new [Segment Group](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview#h_31da47f45c) are assigned an [“OR” or “AND” relationship](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview#h_31da47f45c).
   2. Follow step 5 to select the segments you’d like to add to the second Segment Group.
   3. Repeat step 6, if desired, to add more Segment Groups.
7. Review estimated **Reach** and **Cost** details for the audience.
8. Select **Create** to create the Segmented audience.

Your Segmented audience will immediately begin processing. You can monitor its current status by following the steps outlined in Review a Segmented audience.

article_title: Create or manage a Segmented audience
context_header: Create or manage a Segmented audience › Manage a Segmented audience
text:
## Manage a Segmented audience

Use the **Segmented Audience** page of the Audiences app to review, search, sort, or filter your existing Segmented audiences. You can also use this page to edit, duplicate, or delete them; and to assign them to campaigns.

article_title: Create or manage a Segmented audience
context_header: Create or manage a Segmented audience › Manage a Segmented audience › Review a Segmented audience
text:
### Review a Segmented audience

Follow these steps to locate and review an existing Segmented audience:

1. Locate the audience you’d like to review.
   1. Search by **ID** or **Audience Name**.
   2. Filter by **Status**.
   3. Open the column selector to add or remove a table column.
2. Select the desired audience ID in the **ID** column. This will open the audience in a pop-up window, where you can review its details.
3. Once the Segmented audience features a **Ready** status, you can review additional details.
   1. Review the audience’s **Reach**, **Cost (CPM)**, and **Status** in the summary panel.
   2. Review each audience segment and its details, including which belong to each Segment Group, in the table.
   3. Review available insights related to genders, age groups, devices, and/or geographies in the **Audience Breakdown** panel.
4. Select **Done** to close the pop-up window and return to the **Segmented Audience** page.

article_title: Create or manage a Segmented audience
context_header: Create or manage a Segmented audience › Manage a Segmented audience › Edit a Segmented audience
text:
### Edit a Segmented audience

> **Audience-edit notice:** The edits you apply to an existing audience will automatically be reflected in the campaigns you’ve assigned it to. These changes may affect the performance of those campaigns.

Follow these steps to edit an existing Segmented audience:

1. Select the pencil icon from the desired audience’s **Actions** column. This will open the **Edit Segmented Audience** pop-up window.
2. Follow the steps outlined in Create a Segmented audience to apply your desired changes to the audience’s name, Segment Groups, and/or Segment Group relationships.
3. Select **Save** to apply your changes to the existing audience.

article_title: Create or manage a Segmented audience
context_header: Create or manage a Segmented audience › Manage a Segmented audience › Duplicate a Segmented audience
text:
### Duplicate a Segmented audience

You can duplicate one **Ready**, **Processing**, or **Failed** Segmented audience at a time.

Follow these steps to duplicate an existing Segmented audience:

1. In the **Actions** column, select the page icon next to the audience that you’d like to duplicate. This will open the **Duplicate Segmented Audience** pop-up window.
2. Follow steps 4 through 7 of the Create a Segmented audience workflow to name the audience and choose which segments and Segment Groups it should include.
   1. If no changes are applied, the duplicated audience will include the same segments as the existing audience, and its **Audience Name** will show “Copy of” followed by the existing audience’s name.
3. Select **Duplicate** to create the duplicated audience.

The duplicated audience will appear in the **Segmented Audience** table of the Audiences app and feature a **Processing** status. The original audience will remain unchanged.

article_title: Create or manage a Segmented audience
context_header: Create or manage a Segmented audience › Manage a Segmented audience › Delete a Segmented audience
text:
### Delete a Segmented audience

> **Audience deletion notice:** Note that deleted audiences are unrecoverable, and this action is permanent. As a safeguard, consider duplicating and updating the existing audience to reflect any desired changes.

You can delete Segmented audiences individually or in bulk. They must feature a **Ready**, **Processing**, or **Failed** status; and their **Allowlist/Blocklist** count must be **0**.

Follow these steps to delete a Segmented audience.

1. To delete audiences individually, use the **Actions** column to select the trash can icon next to the individual audience that you’d like to delete.
2. To delete audiences in bulk:
   1. Select the checkboxes next to the desired audiences.
   2. Click **Delete**.

The deleted audience(s) will no longer appear in the Audiences app.

Refer to [Segmented audience statuses](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview#h_2182acc925) for more information.

text:
