Refer to [Segmented audience statuses](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview#h_2182acc925) for more information.

### Audience is in Processing status

Depending on the size of the Segmented audience, it may take 24 to 48 hours for its status to change from **Processing** to **Ready**. If something goes wrong during audience creation, then it’ll feature a **Failed** status instead.

section_path: Troubleshoot Segmented audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Segmented audience › Troubleshoot Segmented audience creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to locate Healthcare audience segments

All Healthcare audience segments are included in the **IQM Healthcare** data segment category. Segments from individual data providers are included in this category.

Note that only Healthcare advertisers are eligible to browse and add Healthcare segments to Segmented audiences. Contact your account admin if you believe you should have access to these segments but are unable to locate them in the Audiences app.

### Unable to locate Political audience segments

All Political audience segments are included in the **IQM Political** data segment category. Segments from individual data providers are included in this category.

Note that only Political advertisers are eligible to browse and add Political segments to Segmented audiences. Contact your account admin if you believe you should have access to these segments but are unable to locate them in the Audiences app.

section_path: Troubleshoot Segmented audience creation or management issues
Unable to apply an “AND” relationship to a Segment Group
context_header: Troubleshoot a Segmented audience › Troubleshoot Segmented audience creation or management issues › Unable to apply an “AND” relationship to a Segment Group
text:
### Unable to apply an “AND” relationship to a Segment Group

A single Segment Group always applies an “OR” relationship to each audience segment within it. This means that your campaign will target a user if they’re included in any of the Segmented audience segments that you added to the group, as long as all other campaign targeting criteria are met.

You can, however, choose an “AND” or an “OR” relationship between each Segment Group. Refer to [Segment Groups and relationships](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview#h_04c5d75525) for more information.

context_header: Troubleshoot a Segmented audience › Troubleshoot Segmented audience targeting issues
text:
### New campaign - Unable to select a PG campaign type

PG campaigns aren’t eligible for Segmented audience targeting. When you create a new campaign that will target the Segmented audience, the **Advanced** option is selected by default, and the **PG** option is disabled.

### Existing campaign - Unable to add to a PG campaign

Only **Advanced** campaigns are eligible for targeting Segmented audiences. For this reason, the **Audiences** section is intentionally excluded from **PG** campaigns.

### Existing campaign - Unable to add to an Advanced campaign

Campaigns typically support targeting multiple audience types. A campaign targeting an NPI-based audience, however, must only include one or more NPI-based audiences. For example, a campaign can’t target [IQM Healthcare audience segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview#h_cde05c8585) if it’s already targeting a Retargeted audience consisting of your website's past visitors.

If the campaign isn’t targeting an NPI-based audience, confirm how many audiences it’s targeting instead. One campaign can target up to 20 audiences.

context_header: Troubleshoot a Segmented audience › Troubleshoot Segmented audience targeting issues
text:
### Existing campaign - Campaign is missing from list

If you’re attempting to add the Segmented audience to an existing campaign, and that campaign isn’t available in the **Campaigns** list, the campaign isn’t eligible for Segmented audience targeting. Refer to [Segmented audience eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview#h_8903263db7) for more details.

The **Add To Campaign** button becomes disabled when the audience(s) you selected aren’t currently eligible for targeting and/or none of your campaigns are currently eligible.

Confirm that each audience you selected features a **Ready** or **Processing** status, and refer to [Segmented audience eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview#h_8903263db7) for more details.

text:
## Lookalike audience troubleshooting overview

All advertisers can create and target Lookalike audiences from their eligible Matched audiences if their account and campaigns meet certain requirements. If you encounter or are blocked from creating, managing, or targeting a Lookalike audience, refer to these resources first:

- [Lookalike audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6966832-lookalike-audience-overview)
- [Create or manage a Lookalike audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7019248-create-or-manage-a-lookalike-audience)

Return to this article to address and resolve other issues that you may encounter related to Lookalike audiences.

section_path: Troubleshoot Lookalike audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Lookalike audience › Troubleshoot Lookalike audience creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to duplicate an audience

You can duplicate **Ready**, **Processing**, or **Failed** Lookalike audiences; however, bulk duplication isn’t currently supported. Ensure that you select only one Lookalike audience at a time before attempting to duplicate those audiences.

### Unable to edit an audience

Editing isn’t currently supported for Lookalike audiences. Consider duplicating the audience instead to create a new audience based on an existing one.

### Unable to change an audience’s name

You can change an existing audience’s name by selecting it in the table’s **Audience Name** column.

Type the new audience name directly in the cell, and confirm your selection by clicking the checkmark icon.

section_path: Troubleshoot Lookalike audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Lookalike audience › Troubleshoot Lookalike audience creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to delete an audience

You can delete audiences individually or in bulk. Every selected audience must be unassigned from all campaigns before you can delete them.

You can easily reference whether an audience is assigned to any campaigns in the **Allowlist/Blocklist** column. Audiences with an **Allowlist/Blocklist** value of **0** can be deleted.

### Unable to locate a deleted audience

Deleted audiences are automatically removed from the Audiences app as soon as you complete this action. For this reason, none of the Lookalike audiences listed in the Audiences app will feature a **Deleted** status.

Refer to [Lookalike audience statuses](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6966832-lookalike-audience-overview#h_d856cc9a62) for more information.

### Source audience is missing from list

Only eligible Matched audiences will appear in the campaign selection field as you build your new Lookalike audience. Refer to [Lookalike audience eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6966832-lookalike-audience-overview#h_2a84cf69b8) for additional support.

Unsure of Audience Size and Similarity settings
context_header: Troubleshoot a Lookalike audience › Troubleshoot Lookalike audience creation or management issues › Unsure of Audience Size and Similarity settings
text:
### Unsure of Audience Size and Similarity settings

Your Lookalike audience’s **Audience Size and Similarity** settings are intended to help you strike the balance between scale and value. Keep in mind that the relationship between the audience’s size and similarity is inversely proportional. This means that a highly similar audience will be smaller in size, and a less similar audience will be larger in size.

Refer to [Lookalike audience key terms and concepts - Audience Size and Similarity](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6966832-lookalike-audience-overview#h_713ea3f391) for additional support.

section_path: Troubleshoot Lookalike audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Lookalike audience › Troubleshoot Lookalike audience creation or management issues › Audience reach is too small
text:
### Audience reach is too small

The more narrow your audience settings, the fewer users will be added to that audience. We recommend loosening the audience’s **Size and Similarity** settings and/or adding additional locations to its **Geo Expansion** settings to allow for greater reach.

Consider also using forecasting and reporting tools to determine your campaigns’ ability to scale based on the audience’s reach in combination with the campaign’s other parameters and settings. Learn more about these features below.

section_path: Troubleshoot Lookalike audience creation or management issues
Pre-campaign forecasting in the Campaigns app
context_header: Troubleshoot a Lookalike audience › Troubleshoot Lookalike audience creation or management issues › Audience reach is too small › Pre-campaign forecasting in the Campaigns app
text:
#### Pre-campaign forecasting in the Campaigns app

Each time you create a new campaign or edit an existing one, you can select **Run Campaign Estimations** to generate forecasts based on the targeting rules you add to the campaign. These include the approximate size of your targetable audience, estimated reach and impressions, and the number of impressions you can expect to win at different bid prices. Refer to [Estimate reach, impression and audience size for a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7883438-estimate-reach-impression-and-audience-size-for-a-campaign) for more information on generating campaign forecasts in the Campaigns app.

context_header: Troubleshoot a Lookalike audience › Troubleshoot Lookalike audience creation or management issues › Audience reach is too small › During-campaign and post-campaign reporting in the Insights app
text:
#### During-campaign and post-campaign reporting in the Insights app

You can assess a campaign’s bid rate by generating a Campaign Bidding Insights report in the Insights app. The charts and figures included in the report highlight the following campaign details:

- What impact each targeting rule had on bid-request drop offs for a campaign?
- How many bid requests remained and passed through each subsequent stage?
- What final bid rate your campaign achieved after it honored each of the targeting rules you defined?

Refer to[Generate and interpret a Campaign Bidding Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10034144-generate-and-interpret-a-campaign-bidding-insights-report) to assess a campaign’s bid rate, and pinpoint which targeting parameters are causing the biggest drop off in your campaign’s bid requests.

article_title: Create or manage a Retargeted audience
context_header: Create or manage a Retargeted audience › Retargeted audience overview
text:
## Retargeted audience overview

Retargeted audiences consist of individuals who have visited your website where a [Pixel Script Code](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651485-retargeted-audience-overview#h_228a7dff7e) was installed, and during the [data collection period](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651485-retargeted-audience-overview#h_9c82625517) you defined. Depending on your campaign objectives, you can target or block the Retargeted audience based on their previous engagement with your brand.

Refer to [Retargeted audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651485-retargeted-audience-overview) for more information and eligibility requirements, or continue reading to create and manage a Retargeted audience in the IQM platform.

article_title: Create or manage a Retargeted audience
context_header: Create or manage a Retargeted audience › Create a Retargeted audience
text:
## Create a Retargeted audience

You can create one Retargeted audience at a time in the Audiences app. Follow these steps to create a new Retargeted audience:

1. Open the Audiences app.
2. Select **Retargeted Audience**.
3. Click **+ Create New**. This will open the **Create Retargeted Audience** pop-up window.
4. Enter a name for the audience.
5. To set a data collection period spanning a specific date range:
   1. Select **Dates**.
   2. Open the **Data Collection Period** date fields.
   3. Make your starting and ending date selections and click **Apply**.
6. To set a data collection period spanning a specific number of months:
   1. Select **Months**.
   2. Open the **Data Collection Period** menu and make your selection of up to 12 months.
7. Click **Create**.

Creating the audience will automatically redirect you to the **Integrate Tag** screen, which includes a [Pixel Script Code](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651485-retargeted-audience-overview#h_228a7dff7e) and step-by-step instructions to integrate the Pixel Script Code.

article_title: Create or manage a Retargeted audience
context_header: Create or manage a Retargeted audience › Manage a Retargeted audience
text:
## Manage a Retargeted audience

Use the **Retargeted Audience** page of the Audiences app to review, search, sort, or filter your existing Retargeted audiences. You can also use this page to obtain or send the Pixel Script Code; or edit or delete Retargeted audiences; and assign them to campaigns.

article_title: Create or manage a Retargeted audience
context_header: Create or manage a Retargeted audience › Manage a Retargeted audience › Review a Retargeted audience
text:
### Review a Retargeted audience

Follow these steps to locate and review an existing Retargeted audience:

1. Locate the audience you’d like to review.
   1. Search by **ID** or **Audience Name**.
   2. Open the column selector to add or remove a table column.
2. Select the desired audience ID in the **ID** column. This will open the audience in a pop-up window, where you can review its details.
3. Once the Retargeted audience features a **Ready** status, you can review additional details.
   1. Review the details you entered when you created the audience such as the **Data Collection Period**.
   2. Review the audience’s **Reach**, **Cost (CPM)**, and **Status** in the summary panel.
   3. Locate the **Pixel Code Preview** and copy it to your clipboard.
4. Select **Done** to close the pop-up window and return to the **Retargeted Audience** page.

article_title: Create or manage a Retargeted audience
context_header: Create or manage a Retargeted audience › Manage a Retargeted audience
text:
### Obtain a Pixel Script Code

When you create a new Retargeted audience, we’ll automatically redirect you to the **Integrate Tag** screen, which includes a [Pixel Script Code](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651485-retargeted-audience-overview#h_228a7dff7e) and step-by-step instructions to integrate the Pixel Script Code.

Refer to Review a Retargeted audience to obtain a Pixel Script Code for a Retargeted audience that you previously created.

### Integrate the Pixel Script Code

> **More on a website’s header section:** The header section immediately follows “<head>” in a website’s code. The “<head>” element is a container that stores information that isn’t directly displayed to the end user. For example, it can include a tracking pixel, define webpage styles and scripts, and determine other metadata. You can locate the “<head>” element by reviewing the code placed between the “<html>” tag and the “<body>” tag.

Follow these steps to integrate the Pixel Script Code, and refer to the simplified representation of what your header might look like in the code snippet shown above.

1. Obtain the Pixel Script Code and copy it to your clipboard.
2. Locate the header section of the website’s code. If you’re using a CMS or web platform to manage the site, locate the header template instead.
3. Locate the section’s closing tag, “</head>”.
4. Paste the code directly above “</head>”.
   1. By placing the code here, you’ll ensure that the script loads early in the page’s overall rendering process. This allows the pixel to collect data efficiently.

If installed correctly, the pixel will immediately begin firing and collecting user-visit data. However, note that it may take up to two hours for pixel fires to reflect in the IQM platform.

article_title: Create or manage a Retargeted audience
context_header: Create or manage a Retargeted audience › Manage a Retargeted audience › Send the Pixel Script Code
text:
### Send the Pixel Script Code

Follow these steps to send a Pixel Script Code and integration instructions to up to 15 recipients:

1. Select the checkbox next to the desired audience.
2. Click **Integrate tag**. This will open the **Integrate Tag** pop-up window.
   1. You can review and send the Pixel Script Code for one Retargeted audience at a time. Selecting multiple audiences will disable the **Integrate tag** option.
3. Select the **Email Pixel Script Code** tab.
4. Enter each recipient’s email address into the **Email ID** field, separated by commas.
5. Click **Send** to share the Pixel Script Code and installation instructions.
6. Select **Done** to close the window and return to the **Retargeted Audience** page.

article_title: Create or manage a Retargeted audience
context_header: Create or manage a Retargeted audience › Manage a Retargeted audience › Edit a Retargeted audience
text:
### Edit a Retargeted audience

> **Audience-edit notice:** The edits you apply to an existing audience will automatically be reflected in the campaigns you’ve assigned it to. These changes may affect the performance of those campaigns.

Follow these steps to edit an existing Retargeted audience:

1. Select the pencil icon from the desired audience’s **Actions** column. This will open the **Edit Retargeted Audience** pop-up window.
2. Follow the steps outlined in Create a Retargeted audience to apply your desired changes.
3. Select **Save** to apply the changes to the existing Retargeted audience.

article_title: Create or manage a Retargeted audience
context_header: Create or manage a Retargeted audience › Manage a Retargeted audience
text:
### Duplicate a Retargeted audience

While you can edit or delete existing Retargeted audiences, duplication isn’t supported because each Retargeted audience includes a unique Pixel Script Code.

Follow the steps outlined in Create a Retargeted audience to generate a new Retargeted audience, which also creates a new Pixel Script Code that you can install to begin capturing users.

### Delete a Retargeted audience

> **Audience deletion notice:** Note that deleted audiences are unrecoverable, and this action is permanent.

You can delete Retargeted audiences individually or in bulk. They must feature a **Ready**, **Processing**, or **Failed** status; and their **Allowlist/Blocklist** count must be **0**.

Follow these steps to delete a Retargeted audience.

1. To delete audiences individually, use the **Actions** column to select the trash can icon next to the individual audience that you’d like to delete
2. To delete audiences in bulk:
   1. Select the checkboxes next to the desired audiences.
   2. Click **Delete**.

The deleted audience(s) will no longer appear in the Audiences app.

The **Create Campaign** button becomes disabled when the audience(s) you selected aren’t currently eligible for targeting.

Confirm that each audience you selected features a **Ready** or **Processing** status, and refer to [Retargeted audience eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651485-retargeted-audience-overview#h_77110c6fbd) for more details.

### Retargeting campaign is pacing behind

Depending on a Retargeted audience’s **Reach**, you may need to target additional audiences to a campaign to help ensure that it has enough data to [pace](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8672915-pacing-overview) appropriately. Note that the actual addressable audience will also become smaller as you apply additional targeting rules and other settings to your campaign.

We recommend applying forecasting and reporting methods to determine whether a Retargeted campaign is expected to spend its budget in full. Refer to [Other campaign targeting considerations](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide#h_8b32ef79d4) to leverage your preferred tools in the Campaigns, Planner, Reports, and Insights app and right-size your Retargeted campaign strategy. You can also review [Troubleshoot a campaign that’s pacing behind](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471960-troubleshoot-a-campaign-that-s-pacing-behind) to rule out other facts that may impact the campaign’s pacing performance.

context_header: Troubleshoot a Geofarmed audience › Geofarmed audience troubleshooting overview
text:
## Geofarmed audience troubleshooting overview

All advertisers can create and target Geofarmed audiences if their account and campaign meet certain eligibility criteria. They must also follow specific steps to successfully create an audience and assign it to a campaign.

If you encounter an error or are blocked from creating, managing, or targeting a Geofarmed audience, refer to these resources first:

- [Geofarmed audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871135-geofarmed-audience-overview)
- [Create or manage a Geofarmed audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871106-create-or-manage-a-geofarmed-audience)

Return to this article to address and resolve other issues that you may encounter related to Geofarmed audiences.

section_path: Troubleshoot Geofarmed audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Geofarmed audience › Troubleshoot Geofarmed audience creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to duplicate an audience

You can duplicate **Ready**, **Processing**, or **Failed** Geofarmed audiences; however, bulk duplication isn’t currently supported. Ensure that you select only one Geofarmed audience at a time before attempting to duplicate those audiences.

### Unable to edit an audience

You can edit **Ready**, **Processing**, or **Failed** Geofarmed audiences; however, bulk edits aren’t currently supported. Ensure that you select only one Geofarmed audience at a time before attempting to edit those audiences.

Note that selecting an audience will open its details, but will not enable any fields for editing. Instead, follow the steps outlined in [Edit a Geofarmed audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871106-create-or-manage-a-geofarmed-audience#h_104070fd08) to apply and save changes to an audience element.

section_path: Troubleshoot Geofarmed audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Geofarmed audience › Troubleshoot Geofarmed audience creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to change an audience’s name

You can change an existing audience’s name by selecting it in the table’s **Audience Name** column.

Type the new audience name directly in the cell, and confirm your selection by clicking the checkmark icon.

### Unable to delete an audience

You can delete audiences individually or in bulk. Every selected audience must be unassigned from all campaigns before you can delete them.

You can easily reference whether an audience is assigned to any campaigns in the **Allowlist/Blocklist** column. Audiences with an **Allowlist/Blocklist** value of **0** can be deleted.

section_path: Troubleshoot Geofarmed audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Geofarmed audience › Troubleshoot Geofarmed audience creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to locate a deleted audience

Deleted audiences are automatically removed from the Audiences app as soon as you complete this action. For this reason, none of the Geofarmed audiences listed in the Audiences app will feature a **Deleted** status.

### Unable to review audience reach

Audience reach details generate automatically once the audience progresses from a **Processing** status to a **Ready** status.

Refer to [Geofarmed audience statuses](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871135-geofarmed-audience-overview#h_56b6dde468) for more information.

### Unable to create a healthcare Geofarmed (HCP, Nurse, Non-NPI Nurse) audience

Certain healthcare advertisers may be eligible to create and target NPI-based and non-NPI-based Geofarmed audiences. Refer to [Geofarmed audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871135-geofarmed-audience-overview) to review related requirements.

Note that healthcare Geofarmed audiences are still created through the standard “Geofarmed audience” workflow. In other words, you won’t see a “Healthcare Geofarmed audience” option in the Audiences app. Instead, you’ll complete additional, healthcare-audience-specific fields and settings in order to create the [NPI-based Geofarmed audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871106-create-or-manage-a-geofarmed-audience#h_fb017c4d84) or [non-NPI-based Geofarmed audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871106-create-or-manage-a-geofarmed-audience#h_f1f5b7509e).

section_path: Troubleshoot Geofarmed audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Geofarmed audience › Troubleshoot Geofarmed audience creation or management issues › Audience reach is too small
text:
### Audience reach is too small

The more narrow your audience settings, the fewer users will be added to that audience. If the specific locations you chose are non-negotiable and can’t be expanded, we recommend loosening the audience’s Frequency, Frequency Type, and Date Range settings.

Consider also using forecasting and reporting tools to determine your campaigns’ ability to scale based on the audience’s reach in combination with the campaign’s other parameters and settings. Learn more about these features below.

section_path: Troubleshoot Geofarmed audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Geofarmed audience › Troubleshoot Geofarmed audience creation or management issues › Audience reach is too small › Pre-campaign forecasting tools
text:
#### Pre-campaign forecasting tools

- **Forecast in the Campaigns app:** Each time you create a new campaign or edit an existing one, you can select Run Campaign Estimations to generate forecasts based on the targeting rules you add to the campaign. These include the approximate size of your targetable audience, estimated reach and impressions, and the number of impressions you can expect to win at different bid prices. Refer to [Estimate reach, impression and audience size for a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7883438-estimate-reach-impression-and-audience-size-for-a-campaign) for more information on generating campaign forecasts in the Campaigns app.

- **Forecast in the Planner app:** Planner proposals give you powerful insights into your media plan’s potential reach and impressions as you layer each targeting parameter onto your campaigns, including your Geofarmed audiences. This process helps highlight which rules will limit your strategy’s scale the most. You can pre-optimize your audience and targeting details to help ensure each campaign spends in full. Refer to [Create or manage a Planner proposal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10104761-create-or-manage-a-planner-proposal) to learn how to add your targeting criteria to a new media plan.

text:
#### During-campaign and post-campaign reporting tools

- **Generate bidding Insights in the Insights app:** You can assess a campaign’s bid rate by generating a Campaign Bidding Insights report in the Insights app. The charts and figures included in the report highlight the following campaign details:
  - What impact each targeting rule had on bid-request drop offs for a campaign?
  - How many bid requests remained and passed through each subsequent stage?
  - What final bid rate your campaign achieved after it honored each of the targeting rules you defined?

Refer to[Generate and interpret a Campaign Bidding Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10034144-generate-and-interpret-a-campaign-bidding-insights-report) to assess a campaign’s bid rate, and pinpoint which targeting parameters are causing the biggest drop off in your campaign’s bid requests.

context_header: Troubleshoot a Geofarmed audience › Troubleshoot Geofarmed audience creation or management issues
text:
### Audience is in Processing status

Depending on the size of the Geofarmed audience, it may take 24 to 48 hours for its status to change from **Processing** to **Ready**. If something goes wrong during audience creation, then it’ll feature a **Failed** status instead.

### Unable to apply an “AND” relationship to a list of locations

A single Geofarmed always applies an “OR” relationship to each location within it. This means that your campaign will target a user if they’re included in any of the selected locations, as long as all other audience criteria (e.g., Frequency, Frequency Type, Start Date, End Date) and campaign targeting criteria are met.

Note that the same is true when a campaign targets or blocks multiple Geofarmed audiences: the relationship between those two audiences is an “OR” relationship.

Refer to Key terms and concepts: Location relationship logic for more information and examples.

context_header: Troubleshoot a Geofarmed audience › Troubleshoot Geofarmed audience targeting issues
text:
### New campaign - Unable to select a PG campaign type

PG campaigns aren’t eligible for Geofarmed audience targeting. When you create a new campaign that will target the Geofarmed audience, the **Advanced** option is selected by default, and the **PG** option is disabled.

### Existing campaign - Unable to add to a PG campaign

Only **Advanced** campaigns are eligible for targeting Geofarmed audiences. For this reason, the **Audiences** section is intentionally excluded from **PG** campaigns.

### Existing campaign - Unable to add to an Advanced campaign

A Geofarmed audience can be added to a campaign once it reaches a **Processing** or **Ready** status.

Campaigns typically support targeting multiple audience types. A single campaign, however, can never target both NPI-based and non-NPI-based audiences. For example, a campaign can’t target an HCP Geofarmed (NPI-based) audience if it’s already targeting a Non-NPI Nurse (non-NPI-based) Geofarmed audience.

Refer to [Geofarmed audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871135-geofarmed-audience-overview) for more information, and confirm that the audience is targeting only accepted audiences and segments.

If the campaign isn’t targeting a conflicting audience type, confirm how many audiences it’s targeting instead. One campaign can target up to 20 audiences.

context_header: Troubleshoot a Geofarmed audience › Troubleshoot Geofarmed audience targeting issues
text:
### Existing campaign - Campaign is missing from list

If you’re attempting to add the Geofarmed audience to an existing campaign, and that campaign isn’t available in the **Campaigns** list, the campaign isn’t eligible for Geofarmed audience targeting. Refer to [Geofarmed audience eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871135-geofarmed-audience-overview#h_36fb6cd424) for more details.

### Add To Campaign button is disabled

The **Add To Campaign** button becomes disabled when the audience(s) you selected aren’t currently eligible for targeting and/or none of your campaigns are currently eligible.

Healthcare advertisers should note that one of these eligibility requirements relates to audience-targeting rules: a campaign must only target the same audience subtype. For example, if you create an NPI-based Geofarmed audience and select both **Nurse** and **HCP** subtypes, then two audiences will be created. Although both of these audiences are NPI-based, a single campaign can’t target both of them since they feature different subtypes. For this reason, we’ll disable the **Add To Campaign** and **Assign To Campaign** buttons if you select audiences featuring different subtypes. Refer to the table below for more information.

| **Audience subtype(s)** | **Allowed combination (Y/N)** |
| --- | --- |
| NPI-based HCP only | Y |
| NPI-based HCP + Legacy audience created prior to audience subtype support | Y |
| NPI-based Nurse only | Y |
| NPI-based Nurse + Legacy audience created prior to audience subtype support | Y |
| Non-NPI-based Nurse only | Y |
| Non-NPI-based Nurse + Legacy audience created prior to audience subtype support | Y |
| NPI-based HCP + NPI-based Nurse | N |
| NPI-based HCP + Non-NPI-based Nurse | N |
| NPI-based Nurse + Non-NPI-based Nurse | N |
| NPI-based HCP + NPI-based Nurse + Legacy audience created prior to audience subtype support | N |

All advertisers should confirm that each audience they selected features a **Ready** or **Processing** status, and refer to [Geofarmed audience eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/6871135-geofarmed-audience-overview#h_36fb6cd424) for more details.

context_header: "Audience targeting and data management" collection overview › Collection summary
text:
## Collection summary

When you generate data-backed audiences, you help ensure you identify and reach the right users, and drive better campaign results. Bring your own first-party data and leverage IQM’s data-management platform (DMP) to build audiences that perform.

The “Audience targeting and data management” collection is your guide to generating, managing, and targeting audiences. Refer to this article’s content catalog to discover each of the resources that are available in this collection.

article_title: "Audience targeting and data management" collection overview
context_header: "Audience targeting and data management" collection overview › Audiences
text:
## Audiences

The audiences you build and target will determine the types of users who should see your ad. The types of audiences vary by your campaign’s objectives, and many advertisers add multiple audiences to meet their goals. For example, your upper-funnel awareness campaigns might target a Lookalike audience to identify and reach new, qualified prospects; and block a Campaign audience made up of users you’ve reached in past or current campaigns to help ensure that budgets are allocated to exposing new users to your brand.

context_header: Custom advertiser segments overview › Custom advertiser segments overview
text:
## Custom advertiser segments overview

Segmented audiences include groups of users who share similar traits. You’ll add segments or groups of segments to the audience to reach that unique group of users. These audiences can be highly specific or more broad, depending on your campaign’s goals and your scale considerations.

You can also add custom data segments to a Segmented audience: Target custom audiences across various data partners, and onboard and apply your own custom segments. Targeting general Segmented audience segments is acceptable for most campaigns; however, we recommend that advertisers intending to reach very specific audiences create a custom Segmented audience. When you create a Segmented audience from your own custom segments, you can target a more precise segment of users based on the criteria you define, and tailor your messaging to select populations.

Refer to [Segmented audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview) to learn more about in-platform Segmented audience segments, or continue reading to learn more about onboarding your own.

context_header: Custom advertiser segments overview › Custom advertiser segments eligibility requirements
text:
## Custom advertiser segments eligibility requirements

Your account, Segmented audience, and campaign must meet the same criteria as the [Segmented audience eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview#h_8903263db7) to onboard and target the custom segments that you onboard to the IQM platform.

context_header: Custom advertiser segments overview › Supported data partners
text:
## Supported data partners

While you can onboard your own custom segments outside of these entities, we also partner with the following data providers to support custom audience onboarding. Note that the data onboarding process may differ between each partner, as this process takes place directly with them.

Refer to your preferred data partner’s Help documentation for more information on how to share your data with them for custom segment creation.

| **Supported data provider** | **Process name** | **Provider’s Help documentation** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LiveRamp | “Activation” | [Getting started with Activation](https://docs.liveramp.com/connect/en/onboarding-your-data.html) |
| Semcasting | “AudienceDesigner” | [AudienceDesigner by Semcasting](https://www.semcasting.com/solutions_ads) |
| L2 Political | “Transmit Universe” | [Data user checklist](https://www.l2-data.com/new-year-l2-data-user-checklist/) |
| Tunnl | “Activate” | [Activate your Tunnl audiences](https://www.tunnldata.com/guides/activate-audiences) |

context_header: Custom advertiser segments overview › Onboard custom advertiser segments
text:
## Onboard custom advertiser segments

When you bring your own data and would like to create a custom audience from it, we recommend doing so by creating a Matched audience. You can complete this process by following the steps outlined in [Create or manage a Matched audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11748442-create-or-manage-a-matched-audience).

If you’d still like to create a segment out of this data instead, onboarding custom advertiser segments takes place outside of the IQM platform and includes the following process:

1. Choose a supported data partner, if desired, and follow their company’s process for onboarding your audience data. Otherwise, proceed to step 2.
2. Contact us at [support@IQM.com](mailto:support@IQM.com), or contact your account representative, to notify us that you’ve created a custom audience with a supported data partner or have advertiser data to onboard directly. At this stage, you’ll share the following details with us:
   1. **Seat ID:** The Advertiser ID (numeric).
   2. **Segment Name:** The name of the custom segment.
   3. **Description:** A brief, one-to-two line description of the segment.
   4. **CPM:** The data cost for the segment.
   5. **PathKey:** The display pathKey of the segment in the platform (e.g., IQM > Custom > Segment Name).
   6. **Data File Path:** The data containing PII or other first-party data via S3 Storage, Google Drive, or SFTP.
3. IQM ingests and processes the data taxonomy that you provided, and transforms it into targetable audience segments.
4. IQM manages account permissions to grant you exclusive access to your custom audience segments.
5. Add custom advertiser segments to a [Segmented audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview) in the IQM platform.
6. [Target the Segmented audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11749120-create-or-manage-a-segmented-audience#h_a25d7a25ac) via new or existing campaigns in the IQM platform.

section_path: Add custom advertiser segments to a Segmented audience
context_header: Custom advertiser segments overview › Add custom advertiser segments to a Segmented audience
text:
## Add custom advertiser segments to a Segmented audience

You can use the Audiences app to create one Segmented audience at a time. You’ll follow the same process as you would if you created a standard Segmented audience, but you’ll select your custom advertiser segments rather than our curated ones.

Refer to [Create or manage a Segmented audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11749120-create-or-manage-a-segmented-audience) for step-by-step audience creation instructions.

context_header: Custom advertiser segments overview › Target a Segmented audience
text:
## Target a Segmented audience

Segmented audiences can be targeted via new or existing campaigns in the Audiences app or Campaigns app. Refer to [Create or manage a Segmented audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11749120-create-or-manage-a-segmented-audience) to learn how to assign a Segmented audience to your campaigns.

context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign audience › Campaign audience troubleshooting overview
text:
## Campaign audience troubleshooting overview

All advertisers can create and target Campaign audiences if their account and source campaigns meet certain eligibility criteria. If you encounter an error or are blocked from creating, managing, or targeting a Campaign audience, refer to these resources first:

- [Campaign audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7033794-campaign-audience-overview)
- [Create or manage a Campaign audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7033837-create-or-manage-a-campaign-audience)

Return to this article to address and resolve other issues that you may encounter related to Campaign audiences.

section_path: Troubleshoot Campaign audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign audience › Troubleshoot Campaign audience creation or management issues
text:
### Audience is stuck in Processing status

A lengthy **Processing** status typically indicates that the audience’s start date is still in the future. The Campaign audience will continue to show a **Processing** status until the audience’s selected start date is reached.

### Unable to select a data partner

The **Data Partner** field is applicable only to Healthcare Campaign audiences when the **HCP** or **Nurse** types are selected from the **Select Type** menu.

### Unable to duplicate an audience

You can duplicate **Ready**, **Processing**, or **Failed** Campaign audiences; however, bulk duplicate isn’t supported. Ensure that you select only one Campaign audience at a time before attempting to duplicate those audiences.

section_path: Troubleshoot Campaign audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign audience › Troubleshoot Campaign audience creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to edit an audience

Editing isn’t currently supported for Campaign audiences. Consider duplicating the audience instead to create a new audience based on an existing one.

### Unable to change an audience’s name

You can change an existing audience’s name by selecting it in the table’s **Audience Name** column.

Type the new audience name directly in the cell, and confirm your selection by clicking the checkmark icon.

### Unable to delete an audience

You can delete audiences individually or in bulk. Every selected audience must be unassigned from all campaigns before you can delete them.

You can easily reference whether an audience is assigned to any campaigns in the **Allowlist/Blocklist** column. Audiences with an **Allowlist/Blocklist** value of **0** can be deleted.

section_path: Troubleshoot Campaign audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign audience › Troubleshoot Campaign audience creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to locate a deleted audience

Deleted audiences are automatically removed from the Audiences app as soon as you complete this action. For this reason, none of the Campaign audiences listed in the Audiences app will feature a **Deleted** status.

### Desired source campaign is missing from list

If you’re attempting to add a source campaign to the Campaign audience, and that campaign isn’t available in the **Campaigns** list, the campaign isn’t eligible for Campaign audience targeting. Refer to [Campaign audience eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7033794-campaign-audience-overview#h_3b54e027b4) for more details.

If you’ve confirmed that your account and the desired source campaigns are eligible, review the **Start Date** and **End Date** that you chose for the Campaign audience. The campaign must have served impressions during those dates to populate in the **Campaigns** menu during audience setup.

Finally, Healthcare advertisers should note that only campaigns targeting one or more audiences of the selected type (**HCP**, **Nurse**, **Non-NPI Nurse**, **Patient**, **Generic**) will populate in the **Campaigns** menu during audience setup.

section_path: Troubleshoot Campaign audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign audience › Troubleshoot Campaign audience creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to review audience reach

Audience reach details generate automatically once the audience progresses from a **Processing** status to a **Ready** status.

### Audience reach is zero

Audience reach details generate automatically once the audience progresses from a **Processing** status to a **Ready** status. In the meantime, the **Reach** metric will display “0.”

If an audience’s reach remains zero after it features a **Ready** status, then none of the conversion events you selected for the campaign (**Impressions**, **Clicks**, or **Conversions**) took place in the selected source campaign(s) during the date range that you chose for the audience.

context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign audience › Troubleshoot Campaign audience targeting issues
text:
### New campaign - Unable to select a PG campaign type

PG campaigns aren’t eligible for Campaign audience targeting. When you create a new campaign that will target the Campaign audience, the **Advanced** option is selected by default, and the **PG** option is disabled.

### Existing campaign - Unable to add to a PG campaign

Only **Advanced** campaigns are eligible for targeting Campaign audiences. For this reason, the **Audiences** section is intentionally excluded from **PG** campaigns.

### Existing campaign - Unable to add to an Advanced campaign

Campaigns typically support targeting multiple audience types. Healthcare advertisers should note, however, that a single campaign can never target both NPI-based and non-NPI-based audiences. For example, a campaign can’t target a Campaign audience consisting of users you reached in prior campaigns if it’s already targeting an HCP Geofarmed audience.

If the campaign isn’t targeting conflicting audience types, confirm how many audiences it’s targeting instead. One campaign can target up to 20 audiences.

context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign audience › Troubleshoot Campaign audience targeting issues
text:
### Existing campaign - Campaign is missing from list

If you’re attempting to add the Campaign audience to an existing campaign, and that campaign isn’t available in the **Campaigns** list, the campaign isn’t eligible for Campaign audience targeting. Refer to [Campaign audience eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7033794-campaign-audience-overview#h_3b54e027b4) for more details.

### Add To Campaign button is disabled

The **Add To Campaign** button becomes disabled when the audience(s) you selected aren’t currently eligible for targeting and/or none of your campaigns are currently eligible.

Confirm that each audience you selected features a **Ready** or **Processing** status, and refer to [Campaign audience eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7033794-campaign-audience-overview#h_3b54e027b4) for more details.

context_header: Troubleshoot a campaign audience › Troubleshoot Campaign audience targeting issues
text:
### Create Campaign button is disabled

The **Create Campaign** button becomes disabled when the audience(s) you selected aren’t currently eligible for targeting.

Confirm that each audience you selected features a **Ready** or **Processing** status, and refer to [Campaign audience eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7033794-campaign-audience-overview#h_3b54e027b4) for more details.

### Campaign targeting a Campaign audience is pacing behind

Depending on a Campaign audience’s **Reach**, you may need to target additional audiences to help ensure that it has enough data to [pace](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8672915-pacing-overview) appropriately. Note that the actual addressable audience will also become smaller as you apply additional targeting rules and other settings to your campaign.

We recommend applying forecasting and reporting methods to determine whether a campaign targeting a Campaign audience is expected to spend its budget in full. Refer to [Other campaign targeting considerations](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497708-campaign-targeting-guide#h_8b32ef79d4) to leverage your preferred tools in the Campaigns, Planner, Reports, and Insights app and right-size your campaign strategy. You can also review [Troubleshoot a campaign that’s pacing behind](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471960-troubleshoot-a-campaign-that-s-pacing-behind) to rule out other facts that may impact the campaign’s pacing performance.

context_header: Troubleshoot a conversion › Conversion troubleshooting overview
text:
## Conversion troubleshooting overview

All advertisers can create Pixel and Postback conversions and add them to campaigns if the conversions and those campaigns meet certain eligibility criteria. They must also follow specific steps to successfully create a conversion and assign it to a campaign.

Certain advertisers are also eligible to create a [Universal Pixel](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735105-conversions-overview#h_20fa954083) conversion if an IQM Super Admin has enabled this feature for your account.

If you encounter an error or are blocked from creating or managing a conversion, or adding it to a campaign, refer to these resources first:

- [Conversions overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735105-conversions-overview)
- [Create or manage a conversion](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735120-create-or-manage-a-conversion)
- [Conversion reporting metrics](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343706-conversion-reporting-metrics)

Return to this article to address and resolve other issues that you may encounter related to conversions.

section_path: Troubleshoot conversion creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a conversion › Troubleshoot conversion creation or management issues
text:
### A Pixel conversion features a Pending status

A Pixel conversion’s status will change from **Pending** to **Active** once you successfully [Integrate the Pixel Script Code](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735120-create-or-manage-a-conversion#h_d093ac69d8) and [Test the Pixel Script Code](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735120-create-or-manage-a-conversion#h_f5d684792e).

Note that it may take up to two hours for the Pixel conversion’s status to change to **Active** after a successful conversion is completed.

### A Universal Pixel conversion features a Pending status

A Universal Pixel conversion’s status will change from **Pending** to **Active** once you successfully [Integrate the Pixel Script Code](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735120-create-or-manage-a-conversion#h_d093ac69d8) and [Test the Pixel Script Code](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735120-create-or-manage-a-conversion#h_f5d684792e).

Note that it may take up to two hours for the Universal Pixel conversion’s status to change to **Active** after a successful conversion is completed.

section_path: Troubleshoot conversion creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a conversion › Troubleshoot conversion creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to locate the Conversion app

All advertisers are eligible to create a Pixel or Postback conversion in the Conversion app. Note, however, that app-level permissions are managed by your Workspace admin. Contact yours if the Conversion app isn’t available in your apps list and you believe that you should have access.

Certain advertisers are also eligible to create a [Universal Pixel](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735105-conversions-overview#h_20fa954083) conversion if an IQM Super Admin has enabled this feature for your account.

### Unable to edit a conversion

The **Edit Conversion** option is disabled when multiple conversion events are selected. You can edit one conversion event at a time.

Follow the steps outlined in [Edit a conversion](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735120-create-or-manage-a-conversion#h_3eddf3eac7) to apply changes. Note that only edits to a conversion’s name are supported.

section_path: Troubleshoot conversion creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a conversion › Troubleshoot conversion creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to duplicate a conversion

Duplication isn’t supported because each conversion event includes a unique Pixel Script Code or unique URLs.

Follow the steps outlined in [Manage a conversion](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735120-create-or-manage-a-conversion#h_b0a123f37b) to create a new one instead.

### Unable to delete a conversion

You can delete a conversion from the Conversion app when it isn’t assigned to any campaigns. A conversion can only be removed from a campaign if it hasn’t begun serving ad impressions.

Note that bulk deletion is supported for conversions, but each selected conversion must also be unassigned from all campaigns to enable the **Delete** button.

section_path: Troubleshoot conversion creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a conversion › Troubleshoot conversion creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to locate a deleted conversion

Deleted conversions are automatically removed from the Conversion app as soon as you complete this action. For this reason, none of the conversion events listed in the Conversion app will feature a **Deleted** status.

### Unable to send Pixel Script Code to desired recipients

If the option to send a Pixel Script Code is disabled, you likely only entered one alias. Enter a comma after the alias or click outside of the **Email ID** field to ensure that the field registers your entry.

Follow the steps outlined in [Send the Pixel Script Code](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735120-create-or-manage-a-conversion#h_3f2ec1c9bc) to rule out any other issues.

context_header: Troubleshoot a conversion › Troubleshoot conversion targeting issues
text:
### Create Campaign is disabled

The option to create a campaign isn’t available for one of the following reasons:

- You selected two types of conversions: Pixel and Postback. You can add one conversion type per campaign.
- You selected more than one Postback conversion. You can add one Postback conversion per campaign, or multiple Pixel conversions per campaign.

### Add To Campaign is disabled

The option to add the selected conversion(s) to an existing campaign isn’t available for one of the following reasons:

- You selected two types of conversions: Pixel and Postback. You can add one conversion type per campaign.
- You selected one type of conversion, but all eligible campaigns already include one or more conversions of the opposite type.
- You selected more than one Postback conversion. You can add one Postback conversion per campaign, or multiple Pixel conversions per campaign.
- None of your existing campaigns are currently eligible because they either don’t meet the [eligibility criteria](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735105-conversions-overview#h_6b8b09faa7), or you’ve already added one or more conversions that conflict with your selection(s).

section_path: Desired campaign is missing from list
context_header: Troubleshoot a conversion › Troubleshoot conversion targeting issues › Desired campaign is missing from list
text:
### Desired campaign is missing from list

A campaign is excluded from the **Add To Campaign** list when it’s ineligible for the conversion(s) you selected. This is likely due to one of the following reasons:

- You selected two types of conversions: Pixel and Postback. You can add one conversion type per campaign.
- You selected more than one Postback conversion. You can add one Postback conversion per campaign, or multiple Pixel conversions per campaign.
- None of your existing campaigns are currently eligible because they either don’t meet the [eligibility criteria](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5735105-conversions-overview#h_6b8b09faa7), or you’ve already added one or more conversions that conflict with your selection(s).
- The campaign has already begun serving ad impressions. You can only add or remove conversion events prior to ad serving.

section_path: Option to Change Conversion Type is missing in Campaigns app
context_header: Troubleshoot a conversion › Troubleshoot conversion targeting issues › Option to Change Conversion Type is missing in Campaigns app
text:
### Option to Change Conversion Type is missing in Campaigns app

The option to change a campaign’s conversion type is unavailable because the campaign has begun serving ad impressions. You can only add or remove conversion events–and change the conversion type–prior to ad serving.

context_header: "Conversions and tracking" collection overview › Collection summary
text:
## Collection summary

When you track conversions using a tracking pixel, you’ll place a small image pixel on your website to allow IQM to measure user actions such as page visits, purchases, or signups. We attribute those conversions to specific ads or campaigns to provide insights into user behavior and preferences, as well as campaign performance.

Mobile app-based conversions use postback conversions only. Postback conversions allow for server-to-server communication with measurement partners such as Kochava, Appsflyer, Singular, and Adjust. You’ll set up the postback on your preferred measurement partner’s platform and copy a click URL, then return to the IQM platform to add the click URL to a new postback conversion and assign it to your campaign.

The “Conversions and tracking” collection is your guide to conversion creation, installation, and attribution. Refer to this article’s content catalog to discover each of the resources that are available in this collection.

context_header: "Conversions and tracking" collection overview › Conversions overview
text:
## Conversions overview

In a campaign’s **Conversion** section, you’ll associate tracking pixels, postback URLs, or a Universal Pixel with your campaign to assign credit for a conversion. Depending on how you set up the conversion, this attribution may be view based (the ad that was last viewed), click based (the ad that was last clicked), or a combination of the two.

text:
## More resources

This page includes all of the articles that you’ll find in the “Conversions and tracking” collection.

Refer to the “Locate more resources” section at the bottom of each article that you review to uncover more, relevant information about the same topic or workflow. For example, these resources will lead you to the [Conversion reporting metrics article](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343706-conversion-reporting-metrics) in the “Reporting and analytics” collection.

context_header: Campaign Estimations overview › Campaign Estimations overview
text:
## Campaign Estimations overview

The Campaign Estimations forecasting feature takes place directly from a campaign. This tool generates projections for the campaign’s Reach, Impressions, and Audience Size based on the targeting parameters that you add to it. You'll use this information to evaluate the potential performance of your campaigns before investing ad budgets, and learn which targeting rules will have the greatest restriction on your campaign’s ability to scale.

We recommend refreshing the **Campaign Estimations** panel after you complete each applicable section of your campaign. You can also run forecasts for in-flight campaigns before you apply changes to them.

Refer to [Run Campaign Estimations](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7883438-run-campaign-estimations) to get started, or continue reading to learn more about the Campaign Estimations feature and how it works.

context_header: Campaign Estimations overview › Eligibility requirements
text:
## Eligibility requirements

All advertisers are eligible to generate Campaign Estimations while they create a campaign or while it’s in flight. However, you’ll need to complete certain fields before those forecasts populate for your campaign. Refer to Forecasts to learn more about the minimum required fields for each Campaign Estimation metric.

context_header: Campaign Estimations overview › Campaign parameters affecting calculation
text:
## Campaign parameters affecting calculation

Campaign Estimations are available for certain campaign targeting parameters. Refer to the table below to determine which of these parameters impacts each forecasting metric. Note that Campaign Estimations don’t account for campaign fields that aren’t included in this table, such as frequency capping.

| **Parameter** | **Targetable Audience** | **Reach & Impression** | **Bid Landscape** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Location** | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **Device Type** | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **Traffic Type** | No | Yes | Yes |
| **Age** | Yes | No | No |
| **Gender** | Yes | No | No |
| **Income** | Yes | No | No |
| **Ethnicity** | Yes | No | No |
| **Deal ID** | No | Yes | Yes |
| **Inventory Group** | No | Yes | Yes |
| **Exchange** | No | Yes | Yes |
| **Site & App** | No | Yes | Yes |
| **Creative Type** | No | Yes | Yes |
| **Audiences*** | No | Yes | Yes |

***Audiences**: All audience types, with the exception of third-party Segmented audiences, affect forecasting metric calculations.

context_header: Campaign Estimations overview › Forecasts
text:
## Forecasts

> **Forecasting notice:** Provided forecasts are available for US campaigns, and represent estimates based on the last seven days of data across the IQM bid landscape. The bid landscape is variable based on changes in available impressions, market seasonality, and other dynamic factors.

The Campaign Estimator tool generates **Targetable Audience**, **Reach & Impressions**, and **Bid Landscape** forecasts.

context_header: Campaign Estimations overview › Forecasts › Targetable Audience
text:
### Targetable Audience

The **Targetable Audience** section displays your campaign’s estimated audience size based on your audience targeting selections and other campaign targeting rules. It compares this targetable audience size to the total addressable audience to determine whether it’s **Broad**, **Moderate**, or **Specific**.
**Targetable Audience size descriptions:**
- **Broad:** The targetable audience is greater than or equal to 70% of the total addressable audience.
- **Moderate:** The targetable audience is greater than 30%, but less than 70%, of the total addressable audience.
- **Specific:** The targetable audience is less than or equal to 30% of the total addressable audience.
At minimum, location targeting settings must be added to a campaign for **Targetable Audience** insights to generate.

context_header: Campaign Estimations overview › Forecasts › Reach & Impressions
text:
### Reach & Impressions

The **Reach & Impressions** section displays your campaign’s estimated reach and impressions based on your audience targeting selections and other campaign targeting rules. It includes two metrics:
- **Unique Reach:** The estimated number of individuals who will be exposed to an ad at least once while the campaign is running.
- **Total Impressions:** The total number of times the ad will be served to the target audience.
You can also enter your preferred unique reach and total impressions. The system will automatically display a recommended total budget and maximum bid that would help you achieve those results. Refer to [Run Campaign Estimations](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7883438-run-campaign-estimations) to learn more.
At minimum, the campaign’s **Start Date**, **End Date**, **Total Budget**, and **Max Bid** fields must be completed for reach and impression insights to generate.

context_header: Campaign Estimations overview › Forecasts › Bid Landscape
text:
### Bid Landscape

The **Bid Landscape** section displays the estimated number of impressions that you can expect your campaign to win at different bid prices.
You can hover your cursor over each **Max Bid** price to review the associated **Impressions**.
At minimum, the campaign’s **Total Budget** and **Max Bid** fields must be completed for bid landscape-related insights to generate.

context_header: Campaign Estimations overview › Other forecasting and reporting tools
text:
## Other forecasting and reporting tools

The IQM platform offers more pre-campaign, during-campaign, and post-campaign tools to help you forecast and report on performance. Leverage your preferred tools in the Planner, Reports, and Insights apps to help right-size your campaigns’ strategies:

- **Planner app:** Refer to [Create or manage a Planner proposal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10104761-create-or-manage-a-planner-proposal) to learn how to add your targeting criteria to a new media plan.
- **Reports app:** Refer to [Generate, manage, or send a report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343879-generate-manage-or-send-a-report) to get started with adding [Performance reporting metrics](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10343812-performance-reporting-metrics-overview) to custom reports.
- **Insights app:** Refer to [Generate and interpret a Campaign Bidding Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10034144-generate-and-interpret-a-campaign-bidding-insights-report) to pinpoint the factors that are causing the biggest drop off in your campaign’s available bid requests.

context_header: "Ad inventory and placements" collection overview › Collection summary
text:
## Collection summary

When you add an inventory-targeting strategy, you choose the most valuable impressions for your campaign based on contextual relevance. You can customize this strategy by choosing particular ad exchanges; publisher categories; other criteria such as ad format, placement type, targeting options, and any other relevant attributes. While not every campaign requires inventory targeting, those that include it may earn higher engagement and lead to more efficient ad spend.

context_header: Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) inventory overview › PG inventory overview
text:
## PG inventory overview

Programmatic guarantee (PG) inventory deals are used to purchase a fixed amount of ad inventory at a pre-determined price through direct negotiation with publishers. These deals are made between one publisher and one advertiser via direct agreements.

Targeting PG inventory deals comes with a tradeoff: removing the highly specific targeting options available in **Advanced** campaigns. However, many advertisers target PG inventory deals to deliver more impressions at a lower rate. They’re also attractive to advertisers because they offer more budget predictability, guarantee ad placements, and avoid volatile auction environments.

context_header: Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) inventory overview › PG inventory use case examples
text:
## PG inventory use case examples

| **Use case** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Access coveted inventory | Secure coveted inventory in times of high demand, such as during holidays, specific content windows, or election cycles. |
| Secure premium inventory | Gain access to premium ad placements on high-quality publishers’ websites to increase brand visibility and audience engagement. |
| Meet required guarantees | Ensure you meet your commitments when guarantees are required to run with certain publishers. |
| Meet upfront commitments | Add PG dollars to count toward upfront commitments to a specific publisher network. |
| Drive cost and reach performance | Focus on driving efficient reach with often lower CPM rates. |

context_header: Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) inventory overview › PG inventory targeting
text:
## PG inventory targeting

Here’s how PG deals work to ensure smooth execution and fulfillment of the agreed-upon terms.

1. You and the supply side platform (SSP) or publisher negotiate deal terms, such as the amount of inventory, pricing details, targeting criteria, and campaign duration.
2. Once the two parties reach an agreement, the SSP or publisher generates a Deal ID and shares it with you.
3. You input the deal ID into a demand-side platform (DSP) such as IQM. In the IQM platform, this process can take place in the Inventory or Campaigns apps.
4. You create a campaign that targets the deal ID and is set up according to the negotiated terms with the SSP or publisher.
5. The IQM platform uses the deal ID to access and purchase the guaranteed inventory, ensuring that the agreed-upon impressions are delivered at the pre-negotiated price.
6. After and throughout the campaign, the platform integrates audience data and other targeting details to optimize ad delivery and reach your target audience. These details are included in real-time reporting and analytics, which you can monitor to ensure your campaign meets its objectives.
7. Once the campaign concludes, reporting data can be used to manage financial reconciliation. This process allows us to facilitate the automated execution, monitoring, and optimization of the PG deal to help ensure compliance with the terms you negotiated.

text:
## Eligibility requirements

All advertisers are eligible to add PG inventory deals to the IQM platform and assign them to campaigns. The following conditions must also be met before a campaign can target a deal.

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| **Advertiser vertical** | Specialty Healthcare Political |
| **Campaign type** | PG |
| **Campaign status** | Draft Running Expired Paused |
| **PG deal status** | Active |
| **PG deal ID** | Up to 500 alphanumeric characters |
| **Exchanges** | 1 per deal |
| **Targetable PG deals** | 1-25 per campaign |

text:
### PG inventory versus PMP inventory deals

PG deals differ from Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory deals. Like PG inventory deals, PMP deals provide more control and premium inventory than inventory obtained through Open Exchange auctions. However, PMP inventory deals are used to purchase ad inventory through a private, invitation-only auction rather than via a one-to-one fixed deal.

Advertisers typically choose PMP inventory deals over PG ones when they want to access premium inventory, but with more control over campaign delivery. For example, they may wish to control frequency, pacing, and audience strategies.

Refer to [Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview#h_bc8dfb92a9) for more information on PMP inventory targeting.

context_header: Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) inventory overview › Key terms and concepts › PG campaigns versus Advanced campaigns
text:
### PG campaigns versus Advanced campaigns

When you create a new campaign, we’ll prompt you to choose whether it’s an **Advanced** or **Programmatic Guaranteed (PG)** campaign. The option you’ll select depends on the type of inventory that the campaign will target.

Choose **Advanced** if your campaign will target Open Exchange inventory or Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory deals. Select **PG** instead if you’ll purchase inventory directly from a specific publisher.

Note that certain features are supported for **Advanced** campaigns only. Selecting **PG** will reduce your campaign-targeting options as you instead agree to commit a set budget for a fixed number of impressions, and at a guaranteed price. You’ll specify only essential criteria for PG deals such as campaign information, budget details, and the PG deal(s) that the campaign will target.

Refer to [Open Exchange inventory groups](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9615716-inventory-groups-overview#h_64b8b6de94), Private Marketplace (PMP) inventory groups, and this article for more information on the differences between these inventory sources.

text:
## PG deal overview

Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) inventory deals are used to purchase a fixed amount of ad inventory at a pre-determined price through direct negotiation with publishers. Once you and the publisher reach an agreement, the publisher generates a Deal ID, which you’ll add to the IQM platform by following the steps outlined in this article.

Refer to [Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) inventory overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12002251-programmatic-guaranteed-pg-inventory-overview) for more information on PG deals, and review [Assign Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) inventory deals to campaigns](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12002417-assign-programmatic-guaranteed-pg-inventory-deals-to-a-campaign) when you’re ready to choose which campaigns will target the PG deals that you’ve added to the IQM platform.

article_title: Create or manage a Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) inventory deal
context_header: Create or manage a Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) inventory deal › Create a PG inventory deal › Inventory app
text:
### Inventory app

Follow these steps to add a new PG inventory deal to the Inventory app:

1. Open the Inventory app.
2. Select the **PG** tab.
3. Click **+ Add Deal**. This will open the **Add Deal** pop-up window.
4. Enter the unique **Deal ID** provided by the supply-side platform (SSP) or publisher partner.
5. Enter a **Deal Name** to help you identify this deal in the IQM platform.
6. Select the one **Exchange** in which the auction for the PG inventory deal will take place.
7. Choose whether the current **Deal Status** is **Active** or **Inactive**.
   1. Campaigns can target or block only **Active** PG inventory deals.
8. Define how payments for the PG campaigns assigned to this deal will be processed.
9. If desired, complete the optional **CPM** and/or **Description** fields.
   1. **CPM** refers to the CPM information provided by the SSP or publisher, which you can store within this deal for reference. The CPM value you enter won’t be used in auctions.
10. Select **Add** to finish adding the new PMP inventory deal to the Inventory app.

article_title: Create or manage a Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) inventory deal
context_header: Create or manage a Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) inventory deal › Create a PG inventory deal › Campaigns app - Existing campaign
text:
### Campaigns app - Existing campaign

Follow these steps to add a new PG inventory deal to a campaign that you’ve already created:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Choose an insertion order (IO), then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one for which you want to add the deal.
3. Locate the **Campaign Name** column and click the campaign’s name. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can add or update its inventory details.
4. Locate and expand the **Inventory** section.
5. Select **+ Add Deal**. This will open the **Add Deal** pop-up window.
6. Follow steps 4 through 9 of the Create a PG inventory deal - Inventory app workflow.
7. Select **Add**. The deal will appear in a **PG Deals** subsection of the campaign.
8. Save your changes to apply the new PG deal to the existing campaign.

article_title: Create or manage a Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) inventory deal
context_header: Create or manage a Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) inventory deal › Create a PG inventory deal › Campaigns app - New campaign
text:
### Campaigns app - New campaign

Follow these steps to add a new PG inventory deal to a new campaign in the Campaigns app:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Click on the name of the desired insertion order (IO).
3. Select **+ Create Campaign**. Once you enter key details such as the campaign type (**PG)** and name, we’ll redirect you to a landing page that you’ll use to add inventory details.
4. Locate and expand the **Inventory** section.
5. Select **+ Add Deal**. This will open the **Add Deal** pop-up window.
6. Follow steps 4 through 9 of the Create a PG inventory deal - Inventory app workflow.
7. Select **Add**. The deal will appear in a **PG Deals** subsection of the campaign.
8. Complete the campaign’s other required and applicable fields, as needed.
9. Save your changes.
   1. Select **Save as Draft** to apply your selections in a draft format.
   2. Select **Run** to apply your selections and create the campaign.

text:
### Edit a PG inventory deal

You can edit one PG inventory deal at a time. Note that all fields are edible for deals that aren’t associated with a campaign. Once deals are associated with a campaign, the **Deal Status** and **Payment To** fields become un-editable.

Follow these steps to apply changes to a PG inventory deal:

1. Select the **PG** tab in the Inventory app.
2. Search, filter, or browse the deals to locate the one you want to edit.
3. Select the checkbox next to the deal.
4. Click **Edit**. This will open the **Edit Deal** pop-up window.
5. Apply your desired changes.
   1. Certain fields become un-editable once the deal is assigned to one or more campaigns.
6. Select **Save** to apply your changes to the existing deal.

article_title: Create or manage a Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) inventory deal
context_header: Create or manage a Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) inventory deal › Manage a PG inventory deal › Delete a PG inventory deal
text:
### Delete a PG inventory deal

> **PG inventory deal deletion notice:** Both **Active** and **Inactive** deals are eligible for deletion, but only if they aren’t currently assigned to any **Pending**, **Running**, **Paused**, or **Expired** campaigns. Note that deletion is permanent, and deleted PG inventory deals are unrecoverable.

You can delete PG inventory deals individually or in bulk. Follow these steps to delete PG inventory deals from the Inventory app:

1. Select the **PG** tab in the Inventory app.
2. Search, filter, or browse the deals to locate the one(s) you want to delete.
3. Select the checkbox next to the deal(s).
4. Click **Delete**. This will open the **Delete Deals?** pop-up window, where you can review any warnings and confirm your selection.

## Remove a PG deal from a campaign

> **PG deal removal notice:** PG deal removal is disabled when the deal is the only inventory assigned to a **Running**, **Paused**, **Expired**, or **Pending** campaign. In other words, at least one PG deal must always be associated with the campaign. This safeguard is intended to prevent performance issues and interruptions to ad serving.

Follow these steps to remove a PG deal that you previously assigned to a campaign:

1. Open the Campaigns app.
2. Choose an insertion order (IO), then filter or search your campaigns to locate the one for which you want to remove inventory.
3. Locate the **Campaign Name** column and click the campaign’s name. We’ll redirect you to a landing page for the campaign, where you can update its inventory details.
4. Locate and expand the **Inventory** section.
5. Select the trashcan icon next to any PG deals that you’d like to remove.
6. Save your changes.
   1. Select **Save as Draft** to apply your selections in a draft format.
   2. Select **Run** to apply your selections and create the campaign.
   3. Select **Save** to apply your selects to the existing campaign.
