context_header: Optimization & Delivery frequently asked questions (FAQ) › Optimization & Delivery FAQ overview
text:
## Optimization & Delivery FAQ overview

When you create a campaign, you’ll choose whether you’d like to apply manual optimizations ([Rule Based Optimization](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview#h_7ba6f52bdf)) or let the IQM platform’s AI engine automatically apply optimizations that aim to achieve the campaign’s primary objective and goal ([AI Based Optimization](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview#h_4753688f6d)). You also have the option to apply Frequency Capping, Bid Pacing, and Budget Capping.

While all advertisers can create campaigns with either AI Based Optimization or Rule Based Optimization enabled, each campaign must meet certain eligibility requirements. If you encounter an error or experience questions related to Optimization & Delivery, refer to these resources first:

- [Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview)
- [Manage a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings)

Return to this article to address and resolve other factors related to a campaign’s Delivery & Optimization section.

context_header: Optimization & Delivery frequently asked questions (FAQ) › Rule Based Optimization FAQ
text:
## Rule Based Optimization FAQ

**Q: What happens if Bid Shading and Advanced Modeling are enabled at the same time?**

**A:** Bid Shading is compatible with the [Spend Ratio](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298415-spend-ratio-overview) and [Priority](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298440-priority-overview) Bid Model settings. The [Bid Modifier](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/9298560-bid-modifier-overview) Bid Model setting cannot be applied at the same time as the Bid Shading feature.

**Q: Why can’t I enable Advanced Modeling for my campaign?**

**A:** While selecting Rule Based Optimization does give you access to the IQM platform’s Advanced Modeling feature, the campaign must meet certain requirements before you can enable it. Refer to [Bid Model overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10870472-bid-model-overview) for more information related to eligibility criteria.

**Q: Which manual optimization features can I use to manage my campaign’s performance?**

**A:** Refer to the [“Reporting and analytics” collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10471834-reporting-and-analytics-collection-overview) article to review each of the reports, dashboards, and data insights that you can leverage to uncover and interpret campaign performance details; and refer to [Optimization overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/?q=optimization+overview) to apply those learnings to your campaign with tools including Advanced Modeling, Pacing, and the Optimization & Delivery features included in this article.

**Q: Why is the Rule Based option not selectable in my campaign’s Optimization & Delivery section?**

**A:** Rule Based Optimization becomes disabled when any of the following are true:

- The campaign has started serving impressions, and the AI Based Optimization option was already selected for the campaign.
- Rule Based Optimization was at one point enabled for the campaign, but the campaign is no longer eligible because it stopped meeting the minimum requirements.

Refer to [Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview) for more information on the eligibility criteria for Rule Based Optimization.

**Q: Where can I locate the Campaign Objective, Campaign Goal, and Target KPI fields?**

**A:** These goal-setting options are exclusive to the AI Based Optimization feature. Refer to [AI Based Optimization](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview#h_4753688f6d) for more details.

context_header: Optimization & Delivery frequently asked questions (FAQ) › AI Based Optimization FAQ
text:
## AI Based Optimization FAQ

**Q: Why is my preferred Campaign Goal unavailable?**

**A:** The list of goals is dependent upon your **Campaign Objective** selection. Refer to [AI Based Optimization - Campaign Objective and Campaign Goal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview#h_6b15684c1c) for a full list of goals that are available for each objective.

**Q: Why is the Campaign Goal field disabled?**

**A:** The **Campaign Goal** field becomes enabled after you select a **Campaign Objective**.

**Q: What are the minimum and maximum Target KPI values that I can choose?**

**A:** Minimum and maximum values are dependent on your **Campaign Goal** selection and the campaign’s **Creative Type**. Refer to [AI Based Optimization - Campaign Objective and Campaign Goal](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview#h_6b15684c1c) for a full list of supported ranges.

**Q: What happens if I choose not to specify a Target KPI value?**

**A:** If you choose not to specify an optional value, the AI engine will aim to optimize for the best possible performance.

**Q: Can I change the Campaign Objective, Campaign Goal, and/or Target KPI value?**

**A:** Whether you can change these selections depends on the campaign’s current status. You can adjust these settings while the campaign features a Draft or Pending status, but not after the campaign begins serving.

**Q: Can I add AI Based Optimization & Delivery settings to my Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) campaigns?**

**A:** No, AI Based Optimization & Delivery settings are supported for Advanced campaigns only.

Creating PG campaigns reduces your campaign-targeting options as you instead agree to commit a set budget for a fixed number of impressions, and at a guaranteed price. You’ll specify only essential criteria for PG deals such as campaign information, budget details, and the PG deal(s) that the campaign will target.

Refer to [Programmatic Guaranteed inventory overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12002251-programmatic-guaranteed-pg-inventory-overview#h_f3d42be8ed) for more information on PG campaigns.

context_header: Optimization & Delivery frequently asked questions (FAQ) › AI Based Optimization FAQ
text:
## AI Based Optimization FAQ

**Q: Why haven’t any optimizations been applied to my campaign with AI Based Optimization enabled?**

**A:** The campaign’s learning stage is still in progress. No optimizations will be applied by the IQM platform’s AI engine until this period concludes.

**Q: What is a learning phase?**

**A:** The learning phase is a process during which the AI Optimization engine gathers data and monitors trends to inform its campaign optimizations. No optimizations are applied during this phase.

**Q: How long does the learning phase last?**

**A:** The learning phase is based on campaign spend rather than a specific number of days. It extends from the moment the campaign starts serving until 20% of the campaign’s total monetary or impression budget is spent. In other words, two separate campaigns may have different learning phase durations.

**Q: Where can I monitor performance data for the AI Based optimizations that were applied to my campaign?**

**A:** You can access performance details directly from the Campaigns app. Refer to [Review performance details for AI Based campaigns](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings#h_f819a47eed) for step-by-step instructions to access the data.

**Q: Where can I reference the specific changes applied by the AI engine?**

**A:** You can access performance details directly from the Campaigns app in the campaign’s **Action Log**. This log includes the following details by date:

- **Time:** The time that the action was performed by the AI engine.
- **AI Action:** The action that was performed by the AI engine.
- **Dimension:** The specific campaign element that was added or updated.
- **Value:** The new amount, percentage, or multiplier that was assigned to the dimension.

Refer to [Review performance details for AI Based campaigns](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings#h_f819a47eed) for step-by-step instructions to access this data.

context_header: Optimization & Delivery frequently asked questions (FAQ) › AI Based Optimization FAQ
text:
## AI Based Optimization FAQ

**Q: Can I search or download an Action Log?**

**A:** Yes. **AI Actions** can be searched for the specific date you selected in the **Actual KPI vs target KPI** chart, and all **Action Log** details can be downloaded as a CSV file for all dates.

Refer to [Review performance details for AI Based campaigns](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings#h_f819a47eed) for step-by-step instructions to complete these processes.

**Q: How should I interpret performance data for the AI Based optimizations that were applied to my campaign?**

**A:** Review [AI Based Optimization - KPI Performance Insights](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview#h_9b5c185bf6) for more information on included metrics and their details.

**Q: What happens if my campaign stops meeting the minimum requirements for using the AI Based Optimization feature?**

**A:** If your campaign becomes ineligible for AI Based Optimization at any time, the AI engine will stop applying optimizations until the campaign meets the requirements.

**Q: Why is the AI Based option not selectable in my campaign’s Optimization & Delivery section?**

**A:** AI Based Optimization becomes disabled when any of the following are true:

- The campaign has started serving impressions, and the Rule Based Optimization option was already selected for the campaign.
- AI Based Optimization was at one point enabled for the campaign, but the campaign is no longer eligible because it stopped meeting the minimum requirements.

Refer to [Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview) for more information on the eligibility criteria for AI Based Optimization.

**Q: Which campaign dimensions can the AI engine adjust when optimizing the campaign?**

**A:** AI Based Optimization may apply changes to one or more of the following dimensions based on its performance against the **Campaign Goal** you specify:

- Creative Size
- Pacing
- Frequency (if no Frequency Settings are specified in the campaign’s settings)
- Inventory
- Audience
- Demographics (Age Group, Gender Group, Income Group, Language Group, Interest Group, Ethnic Group)
- Device (Manufacturers, OS, Carrier, Network, Traffic Type, Device Type)
- Location
- Exchange

context_header: Optimization & Delivery frequently asked questions (FAQ) › AI Based Optimization FAQ
text:
## AI Based Optimization FAQ

**Q: Can AI Based Optimizations apply Frequency optimizations to my campaign if I have the Frequency Capping feature disabled?**

**A:** Depending on campaign performance, the AI engine may apply Frequency optimizations. A limit of 100 impressions will be set to help your target audience avoid ad fatigue. You can enable Frequency Capping at any time to choose settings that will take precedence over AI Based Optimizations.

context_header: Optimization & Delivery frequently asked questions (FAQ) › Frequency Capping FAQ
text:
## Frequency Capping FAQ

**Q: Is Frequency Capping compatible with both AI Based and Rule Based Optimization?**

**A:** Yes. You can set and manage Frequency Capping settings for a campaign regardless of whether AI Based or Rule Based Optimization are selected.

**Q: What is the purpose of a campaign’s Frequency Cap?**

**A:** Frequency Caps limit the number of impressions a user can see during a given time frame. This setting helps advertisers walk the fine line of driving brand awareness and earning conversions without over-serving ads.

**Q: What Frequency Cap do you recommend for my campaign?**

**A:** Each campaign is unique based on the targeting parameters you set and the current bid landscape. This means that there’s not one recommended Frequency Cap for optimal campaign performance. We recommend starting with a lower Frequency Cap (e.g., 3 impressions per day) and gradually increasing it, as needed, based on the campaign’s reach and overall performance.

**Q: Can I set a different Frequency Cap for a campaign’s creatives, audiences, or inventory?**

**A:** No, Frequency Capping is set at the campaign level rather than for individual campaign elements.

**Q: Can I set a different Frequency Cap for multiple durations?**

**A:** Yes, a maximum of four frequency rules are supported per campaign. You can add one rule for each duration type (daily, weekly, monthly, campaign).

**Q: What happens if I choose a Frequency Cap rule based on Campaign Duration, but I haven’t chosen an end date for the campaign?**

**A:** You’ll need to define a campaign end date before you can save a Frequency Cap rule that’s based on Campaign Duration. You can complete this step directly from the Frequency Capping section of your campaign.

**Q: What is the relationship between my campaign’s multiple Frequency Cap rules?**

**A:** Your campaign applies an "AND" relationship to Frequency Cap rules. If any single rule is met within a timeframe, it takes precedence, preventing further impressions to the user during that period.

**Q: What are the devices for which IQM receives Device IDs?**

**A:** We receive Device IDs for mobile, connected TV (CTV), over-the-top (OTT), and tablet devices.

context_header: Optimization & Delivery frequently asked questions (FAQ) › Frequency Capping FAQ
text:
## Frequency Capping FAQ

**Q: What scenarios might cause a campaign to exceed its Frequency Cap?**

**A:** A given user may get served your ad additional times depending on whether a unique identifier (IQM ID or Ramp ID) is available.

For example, consider an advertiser who sets a Frequency Cap of 1 impression for a campaign. The first impression is counted at the Ramp ID level. Later, the campaign bids on a request for the same user because no unique identifier–such as a Ramp ID–is available. In this scenario, the cookie ID becomes the primary identifier and the bid is sent again. The cookie ID is counted as a unique user.

**Q: What percentage of traffic is capped at the IQM ID or Ramp ID level?**

**A:** Approximately 45-50% of bid request traffic is capped at the IQM ID or Ramp ID level. The remaining traffic is capped at the Device ID, Cookie ID, or IP Address level.

**Q: When does Frequency Capping management take place?**

**A:** You can add optional Frequency Capping settings to your campaign when you complete the campaign’s **Optimization & Delivery** section. A campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings determine how aggressively it should bid based on how much you’d like to spend, how you’d like to pace bidding, and how often you’d like for users to see an ad. Refer to [Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview) for more information.

**Q: How do I set up new Frequency Capping settings for a campaign?**

**A:** Refer to the steps outlined in [Manage a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings) to complete this process.

**Q: How do I change existing Frequency Capping settings for a campaign?**

**A:** Refer to the steps outlined in [Manage a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings) to complete this process.

**Q: What happens if I choose AI Based Optimization for my campaign and I don’t enable Frequency Capping?**

**A:** Depending on campaign performance, the AI engine may apply Frequency optimizations. A limit of 100 impressions will be set to help your target audience avoid ad fatigue. You can enable Frequency Capping at any time to choose settings that will take precedence over AI Based Optimizations.

text:
## Bid Pacing FAQ

**Q: Is Bid Pacing compatible with both AI Based and Rule Based Optimization?**

**A:** Yes. You can enable the Bid Pacing feature for a campaign regardless of whether AI Based or Rule Based Optimization are selected.

**Q: When does it make sense to enable Bid Pacing?**

**A:** The decision to apply Bid Pacing can depend on its pacing performance. For example, consider disabling the Bid Pacing feature if the campaign is pacing behind. This change will allow it to spend the daily budget as soon as possible without pacing restrictions in place.

**Q: When does Bid Pacing management take place?**

**A:** You can enable the optional Bid Pacing feature when you complete a campaign’s **Optimization & Delivery** section. A campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings determine how aggressively it should bid based on how much you’d like to spend, how you’d like to pace bidding, and how often you’d like for users to see an ad. Refer to [Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview) for more information.

**Q: How do I enable Bid Pacing for a campaign?**

**A:** Refer to the steps outlined in [Manage a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings) to complete this process.

## Budget Capping FAQ

**Q: Is Budget Capping compatible with both AI Based and Rule Based Optimization?**

**A:** Yes. You set and manage Budget Capping settings for a campaign regardless of whether AI Based or Rule Based Optimization are selected.

**Q: When does Budget Capping management take place?**

**A:** You can enable optional Budget Capping settings when you complete a campaign’s **Optimization & Delivery** section. A campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings determine how aggressively it should bid based on how much you’d like to spend, how you’d like to pace bidding, and how often you’d like for users to see an ad. Refer to [Optimization & Delivery overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10906959-optimization-delivery-overview) for more information.

**Q: How do I add my Budget Capping setting to a campaign?**

**A:** Refer to the steps outlined in [Manage a campaign’s Optimization & Delivery settings](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651517-manage-a-campaign-s-optimization-delivery-settings) to complete this process.

**Q: When does it make sense to apply Budget Capping?**

**A:** Since impression and budget caps cause your campaign to stop spending once the daily limits are reached, we recommend reserving these settings for campaigns and IOs that are pacing on track (90%-100%) or pacing ahead (100%-120%). You might also consider increasing a budget cap to allow the campaign’s pacing to catch up. Refer to [Pacing overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/8672915-pacing-overview) for more information on how pacing performance is calculated, and how it differs for budget-based and impression-based campaigns.

text:
## Account security overview

> **More on account security:** Only Admin, Workspace Owners, Advertiser Owners, Default Users, and Full-Access users can manage the MFA settings of other users. Use only when required.

Providing at least two different forms of identification when logging into any online account can make it significantly harder for hackers to access it.

The IQM platform supports Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) to add an extra layer of security to your account. This feature requires users to verify their identity by entering their password and a one-time verification code sent to their email.

Workspace Owners and Advertiser Owners can manage MFA security settings for users linked to their accounts in the Organization app, and individual users can manage MFA security settings for their own account in the My Profile app. The most recent MFA settings configured by any user type will reflect across the account; in other words, any existing settings will be overwritten.

text:
### Enable or disable MFA for individual users

Follow these steps to manage MFA settings for one user at a time:

1. Select the **Profile** tab of the Organization app.

3. In the **MFA Status** column, select the toggle switch to change to enable or disable MFA for a user.

### Enable or disable MFA for multiple users

Follow these steps to manage MFA settings for multiple users at a time:

1. Select the **Profile** tab of the Organization app.
2. Click **Security Settings**.
3. Select the checkboxes next to the desired users.
4. Click **Enable MFA** or **Disable MFA** to enable or disabled MFA for the selected users.

## Log in with an MFA verification code

When MFA is enabled for your account, you’ll be prompted to enter a one-time verification code to confirm your identity when you log in.

Follow these steps to log in with an MFA verification code:

1. Enter your email ID.
2. Click **Next**.
3. Enter your password.
4. Click **Next**.
5. Open the email inbox that’s associated with your platform login to retrieve your one-time verification code.
   1. Check your spam folder if you didn’t receive a code.
   2. The code pictured in the sample image is for example purposes only.
6. Enter the code into the **Enter verification code** field.
7. If the code has expired, click **Resend code** to receive a new one.
8. Select **Verify identity** to finish logging in.

article_title: Political creative approval process for publishers
context_header: Political creative approval process for publishers › Political creative approval process overview
text:
## Political creative approval process overview

Certain publishers complete compliance checks before Political ads start running. To help streamline the creative review-and-approval process for these ads, they use a specific Creative Submission API. It’s a request that, once sent, returns any creatives attached to Political campaigns that include a [Federal Election Commission Identifier (FEC ID) or a state equivalent](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12003037-organization-profile-overview#h_fa4aa3286f). This process allows the publisher partners to manually review Political creatives prior to approving them.

Publisher partners complete a simple three-step process when they use an API to review Political campaign creatives:

article_title: Political creative approval process for publishers
context_header: Political creative approval process for publishers › Obtain the right permissions (access token)
text:
## Obtain the right permissions (access token)

> **Client ID and Client Secret notice:** Contact your IQM representative to obtain a **ClientID** and **ClientSecret**. These items are required before you can obtain the access token and send a Creative Submission API request for Political campaign creatives.

The publisher partner will obtain client credentials, also known as the access token, to confirm they have the proper authorization to access a particular Political campaign’s creatives. They’ll send a POST API request containing the following details to ask for these credentials:

| **Section** | **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Header** | x-iaa-host | api.iqm.com [Global Host] |
| **Header** | Authorization* | Basic <base64(ClientID:ClientSecret)> |
| **Header** | Content-Type | application/x-www-form-urlencoded |
| **Body** | Grant-Type | grant_type=client_credentials |

*Refer to Obtain the base64 string for additional support with the Authorization header.

article_title: Political creative approval process for publishers
context_header: Political creative approval process for publishers › Obtain the right permissions (access token)
text:
### Obtain the base64 string

Obtaining the base64 string for the Authorization header is a two-step process:

1. Concatenate the Client ID and Client Secret with a colon.
2. Base64-encode the result.

Refer to the example below for more information.

| **Item** | **Example value** |
| --- | --- |
| Example ClientID | Test |
| Example ClientSecret | 123456 |
| Example concatenation | Test:123456 |
| Example base64 | cm9rdV8yOjEyMzQ1Ng== |

### Example cURL request

Refer to the block below to review an example of a request to obtain the access token.

```
curl --location 'http://api.iqm.com/api/v3/ua/oauth/token' \
  --header 'x-iaa-host: api.iqm.com' \
  --header 'Authorization: Basic cm9rdV8yOjEyMzQ1Ng==' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials'
```

article_title: Political creative approval process for publishers
context_header: Political creative approval process for publishers › Obtain the right permissions (access token) › Example token response
text:
### Example token response

> **Access token notice:** After you successfully submit the access token request, remember to save the **access token** included in the response. You’ll need to include this token when you call the Creative Submission API.

Refer to the block below to review an example of a successful response to your access-token request. Pay special attention to the **scope**: when a response excludes the “creative.submit” scope, it means the client isn’t authorized to submit creatives via this API.

```
{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJI...kVJhsWWDCL3...",
  "expires_at": 1763632934684,
  "scope": "creative.submit"
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "expires_in": 1799,
  "jti": "1c04c09a-67ab-4fe0-a626-a5f1475d283e"
}
```

article_title: Political creative approval process for publishers
context_header: Political creative approval process for publishers › Request a Political campaign’s creatives
text:
## Request a Political campaign’s creatives

The publisher partner will use the credentials they obtained to request all of the creatives associated with a specific Political campaign. They’ll send an API request containing the following details to submit a request for these creatives. This request is called the “Creative Submission API.”

| **Section** | **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **API Endpoint** | URL | [http://api.iqm.com/api/v3/crt/creatives/submit](http://api.iqm.com/api/v3/crt/creatives/submit) |
| **Header** | Authorization* | Bearer <access_token> |
| **Header** | x-iaa-host | api.iqm.com |
| **Query Parameters** | Limit (Optional) | If desired, limit the number of creatives submitted. The default value is “-1”, meaning all valid creatives will be submitted when you send the API request. |

*Replace the <access_token> value with the actual access token you received.

article_title: Political creative approval process for publishers
context_header: Political creative approval process for publishers › Request a Political campaign’s creatives
text:
### Example cURL request

Refer to the block below to review an example of a Creative Submission API request.

```
curl --location 'http://api.iqm.com/api/v3/crt/creatives/submit?limit=10' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' \
  --header 'x-iaa-host: api.iqm.com'
```

### Example response

Publisher partners know that their request was successful when they receive a **200 OK** API response that includes the information shown in the example below. A successful request means that the details of the request were valid and the publisher obtained the proper authorization before sending the request.

```
{
    "success": true,
    "data": [
        {
            "creativeId": 715863,
            "creativeName": "Sample Creative Name",
            "creativeSource": "https://cdn.example.com/creatives/715863/sample-creative.jpg",
            "advertiserDetails": {
                "advertiserName": "Sample Advertiser",
                "website": "https://www.sampleadvertiser.com",
                "chiefName": "John Doe",
                "contactNumber": "+1-202-555-0147",
                "address": "123 Main Street, New York, NY 10001",
                "politicalIdentifier": "POL-45678",
                "advertiserId": 11124,
                "legalInfo": "Verified advertiser with compliance clearance",
                "links": [
                    "https://www.sampleadvertiser.com/about",
                    "https://www.sampleadvertiser.com/campaigns"
                ]
            }
        }
    ]
}
```

section_path: Unsuccessful requests for a Political campaign’s creatives
context_header: Political creative approval process for publishers › Request a Political campaign’s creatives › Unsuccessful requests for a Political campaign’s creatives
text:
### Unsuccessful requests for a Political campaign’s creatives

Requests for a Political campaign’s creative details aren’t always successful. Refer to the table below for more information on errors that a publisher partner may encounter.

| **Error** | **Error description** |
| --- | --- |
| 401 Unauthorized | Either the token is missing, invalid, or expired; or the client is expired. |
| 403 Forbidden | The token is valid, but does not have the required “creative.submit” scope. This can occur if you use an access token issued for a client that isn’t otherwise authorized to submit creatives. |

## Collection summary

Inventory targeting allows you to choose the most valuable impressions for your campaign based on contextual relevance. You can specify where your ads will run by choosing particular ad exchanges; publisher categories; other criteria such as ad format, placement type, targeting options, and any other relevant attributes. While not every campaign requires inventory targeting, those that include it may earn higher engagement and lead to more efficient ad spend.

This collection includes a list of tutorial videos to take you through the process of adding, grouping, and managing inventory. Refer to ["Ad inventory and placements" collection overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/12002181-ad-inventory-and-placements-collection-overview) for a full list of comprehensive, text-based documentation covering these topics.

text:
## AQ Insights report overview

When healthcare advertisers evaluate how effectively their campaigns reached the right patient audiences, they’re able to bridge the gap between clinical targeting and digital media performance.

Audience Quality (AQ) Insights reports help you validate patient reach. These insights leverage third-party healthcare data from PurpleLab to confirm audience exposure based on patient-level targeting criteria including prescriptions, diagnoses, and procedures.

The IQM platform pairs these insights with an AQ Score ranging from 0% to 100%, so you’ll know exactly how well each campaign and audience is connecting with the qualified patient segments you intend to reach. Each report also includes detailed data across dimensions such as publisher, geography, and device type for more in-depth campaign-level and audience-level AQ insights.

context_header: Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report overview › AQ Insights report eligibility requirements
text:
## AQ Insights report eligibility requirements

If you’re a Healthcare advertiser, you may be eligible to generate AQ Insights reports.

The following conditions must also be met before a given campaign or audience becomes eligible for AQ Insights reporting.

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| **Campaign vertical** | Healthcare* |
| **Audience type** | [Matched (Patient)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11535636-matched-audience-overview) [Segmented (Patient)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5651486-segmented-audience-overview) [Campaign (Patient)](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/7033794-campaign-audience-overview) |
| **Audience status** | Ready |
| **Campaign type** | Advanced, and targeting at least one patient audience |
| **Campaign status** | Running Expired (within the past two years) Paused |
| **Campaign impressions** | 1K or more impression |
| **Campaign duration** | 14 or more days |

***Healthcare:** Any campaign created under a healthcare advertiser account is a “Healthcare” campaign.

text:
## AQ Insights report metrics

> **More on healthcare campaign insights:** AQ Insights reports provide in-depth data of your patient-based strategies. For NPI-based audiences, gain deeper insights with two additional healthcare measurement solutions: Provider Level Data (PLD) Insights reports and Script Lift Study (SLS) Insights reports. PLD Insights reports help you uncover ad-exposure and engagement data, demographic data, and physician-specialty data for your NPI-based healthcare audiences; while SLS Insights reports help you evaluate the effectiveness of your healthcare campaigns based on pre- and post-campaign prescription (Rx, TRx) volumes and your competitors’ prescription patterns. Refer to [PLD Insights report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10774817-provider-level-data-pld-insights-report-overview) and [SLS Insights overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/10858871-script-lift-study-sls-insights-report-overview) for more information.

The AQ Insights report includes impression, reach, and audience-matching analyses broken out by a particular dimension, including geographic location, device type, audiences, and publishers. These metrics inform an overall AQ Score to help you evaluate how effectively a given campaign reached the intended patient audience.

Review the AQ Insights report metrics below, and refer to [Generate or manage an Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13132289-generate-or-manage-an-audience-quality-aq-insights-report) when you’re ready to create one. ## AQ Insights report pricing

There is a cost associated with generating an AQ Insights report. You can reference its price after you enter key details–like the campaign’s total number of chargeable impressions and date range–and before you generate the report. We calculate these impressions on a CPM basis.

Refer to [Generate or manage an Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13132289-generate-or-manage-an-audience-quality-aq-insights-report) for more information on where to reference the report-price preview.

text:
### Price deduction - Sufficient funds

The workflow to generate an AQ Insights report ends with a **Generate** button that you’ll use to create the report. We’ll deduct the **AQ Cost** from your account’s available balance once the report successfully generates. In most cases, this will take place immediately after you select **Generate**.

Refer to [Generate or manage an Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13132289-generate-or-manage-an-audience-quality-aq-insights-report) for step-by-step report creation instructions.

### Price deduction - Insufficient funds

The workflow to create an AQ Insights report typically ends with a **Generate** button that you can use to create the report. If your account’s available balance is less than the report’s **AQ Cost**, then this button will prompt you to add funds to your account instead. We’ll redirect you to enter a fund amount and select a payment method when you click **Add Funds**.

Note that you’ll need to refresh the **Audience Insights** creation widget to reflect your account’s updated balance and continue with report generation.

context_header: Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report overview › AQ Insights report pricing › Pricing for AQ Insights reports with overlapping datasets
text:
### Pricing for AQ Insights reports with overlapping datasets

There may be instances when you generate multiple AQ Insights reports with partially overlapping date ranges for the same campaign. This means that the insight data also overlaps.

You’ll pay only once for AQ Insights data for each date.

**Example:** An advertiser generates two reports for the same campaign–one with a date range of August 1st-14th, and another with a date range of August 5th-20th. Since they already paid for the insights from August 1st-14th, they’ll only be charged for a portion of the second report: the new data generated for the August 15th-20th date range. However, we’ll still aggregate data from the full August 5th-20th date range in the second report.

context_header: Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report overview › Key terms and concepts › Audience Quality (AQ) Score
text:
### Audience Quality (AQ) Score

An Audience Quality score is determined by two metrics: The audience’s **Exposed** users and **Matched** details.

The audience’s **Exposed** metric is the total number of identified patients who were exposed to your ad. Its **Matched** metric represents the number of these users who were confirmed to be part of the qualified patient segments you intended to reach.

When you divide the Patient audience’s total number of **Matched** users by the **Exposed** users, then multiply the result by 100, you’re left with the audience’s AQ Score.

A campaign’s overall AQ Score considers each of the individual AQ Scores of its target audiences.

**Example:** A campaign served 3.3M **Impressions**, and earned an **Exposure** of 274K identified patients. Approximately 250K of these users were confirmed to be **Matched**. This campaign’s AQ Score is 91.2%. ([250K / 274K] * 100 = 91.2%).

### Generate an AQ Insights report from the Insights app

Follow these steps to create new report from the Insights app:

1. Open the Insights app.
2. Click **Audience Quality**.
3. Select **+ Generate New**. This will open the **Generate Audience Quality** pop-up window.
4. Enter a name for the report.
   1. Choose a unique one to differentiate this report from others that you may create.
5. Select whether the desired campaign is **Running**, **Paused**, or **Expired**.
   1. Your selection will determine which campaigns are available in the **Campaign** menu.
6. Search and select the campaign for which you want to generate insights.
7. The **Date Range** field will automatically populate once you select a campaign.
   1. The selected range reflects the campaign’s start date through one day ago or the campaign’s end date–whichever took place first.
8. Choose campaign-level or audience-level Concept Group ID assignment.
9. Enter the applicable Concept Group ID(s).
   1. If you chose audience-level Concept Group ID assignment, note that individual Concept Group IDs are required for each audience.
10. Select **Next**.
11. Review the report’s settings, and a summary of the AQ Insights report’s chargeable impressions and the associated cost.
    1. We calculate **AQ Cost** based on the number of impressions that your campaign delivered during the specified date range at a CPM rate.
12. Select **Previous** to change any report settings, if desired.
13. Click **Generate** to create the AQ Insights report.

The **AQ Cost** will be held as soon as you select **Generate**, and deducted from your account’s available balance as soon as the report’s status changes from **Processing** to **Ready**. In some cases, this may occur immediately.

You can locate generated reports on the **Audience Quality** page. Review Manage an AQ Insights report for more details.

text:
## AQ Insights report troubleshooting overview

Advertisers can create Audience Quality (AQ) Insights reports if their account and audiences meet certain eligibility criteria. They must also follow specific steps to successfully generate a report.

If you encounter an error or are blocked from creating or managing an AQ Insights report, refer to these resources first:

- [Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13132023-audience-quality-aq-insights-report-overview)
- [Generate or manage an Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13132289-generate-or-manage-an-audience-quality-aq-insights-report)

Return to this article to address and resolve other factors that may block your ability to create or manage an AQ Insights report.

article_title: Troubleshoot an Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report
context_header: Troubleshoot an Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report › AQ Insights report creation troubleshooting
text:
### Insufficient funds

The workflow to generate an AQ Insights report ends with a **Generate** button that you’ll use to create your report. If your account’s available balance is less than the **AQ Cost**, this button will change to **Add Funds** to prompt you to add funds to your account instead.

You can also add funds from the Organization app. Refer to [Add and manage funds](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/5734663-add-and-manage-funds) for step-by-step instructions.

### Campaign missing from list

A campaign is excluded from your report’s **Campaigns** list due to its [eligibility](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13132023-audience-quality-aq-insights-report-overview#h_74980b9de1) or [status](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13132023-audience-quality-aq-insights-report-overview#h_f52e8b13c3).

Follow these steps to troubleshoot why a given campaign is missing from the list:

1. Refer to [Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13132023-audience-quality-aq-insights-report-overview) to confirm that the campaign meets all eligibility criteria.
2. Check the campaign’s current status and duration. You can generate AQ Insights reports for eligible campaigns that feature a **Pending**, **Running**, or **Expired** status; and have a duration of 14 or more days.
3. Make sure that your **Campaign Status** selection is correct. It narrows the items included in the **Campaigns** menu to only include the campaigns that feature the status you choose. For example, if you choose **Expired**, we’ll only list eligible campaigns with an **Expired** status in the **Campaigns** field.
4. Confirm whether another AQ Insights report is still processing for the same campaign. While you can generate insights for an unlimited number of campaigns, you can generate only one AQ Insights report at a time for each campaign.

article_title: Troubleshoot an Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report
context_header: Troubleshoot an Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report › AQ Insights report creation troubleshooting
text:
### Cannot change date range

The AQ Insights report’s **Date Range** field will auto-populate once you select a campaign. The first date reflects the campaign’s Start Date, and the second date reflects either the campaign’s End Date or today’s date minus one day–whichever took place first. These dates are not editable.

### Select Campaign is disabled - Insights app

The campaign selector becomes disabled when none of your campaigns’ statuses match the ones you selected in the **Campaign Status** menu. Refer to the number in parentheses next to each status, which indicates how many of those campaigns are eligible for AQ Insights reporting. For example, **Running (0)** indicates that zero eligible campaigns currently feature a **Running** status.

**Expired** campaigns work slightly differently. The selected campaigns must have expired within the past two years to be eligible for AQ Insights reporting.

article_title: Troubleshoot an Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report
context_header: Troubleshoot an Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report › AQ Insights report creation troubleshooting
text:
### Generate AQ Insights is disabled - Campaigns app, Dashboard app

There may be instances where the option to **Generate AQ Insights** is disabled in the Campaign or Dashboard apps. This occurs when the selected campaign doesn’t meet the eligibility criteria, or when you’ve selected multiple campaigns.

If the selected campaign meets all eligibility criteria but the button remains disabled, note that, while you can generate insights for an unlimited number of campaigns, you can generate only one AQ Insights report at a time for each campaign.

### Cannot generate a report - Insights app

You may encounter a warning message or another issue that blocks you from generating AQ insights for a particular campaign. We build in certain blocks to help avoid charging you for highly similar datasets more than once, or generating reports inaccurately.

These blocks typically occur for one of the following reasons:

1. You can generate one AQ Insights report at a time for each campaign. Another AQ Insights report can be generated once the in-progress report displays a **Ready** status on the **Audience Quality** page. Refer to [Generate or manage an Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13132289-generate-or-manage-an-audience-quality-aq-insights-report) to learn how to access this page and review report statuses.
2. You can generate only one AQ Insights report when you choose the same campaign and date range. The **Generate** option won’t be available in this circumstance since the report’s data would be identical to the initial report. Instead, you can review the AQ Insights report that you already generated for the campaign.
3. You no longer have access to AQ Insights reporting.
   There may be certain cases where you’ve previously generated AQ Insights reports, but your access is now revoked due to permission changes applied by a system administrator. You won’t be able to generate new insights, but you can continue to access reports you’ve already generated for one year after their creation date.

article_title: Troubleshoot an Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report
context_header: Troubleshoot an Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report › AQ Insights report results troubleshooting
text:
### Cannot delete a report

We limit the ability to delete AQ Insights reports to help avoid accidental deletions of paid insights.

The **Audience Quality** page of the Insights app displays each of your AQ Insights and their statuses: **Ready**, **Processing**, and **Failed**. You can delete any **Failed** AQ Insights reports either individually or in bulk.

### Cannot email a report

The email feature may be disabled for one of the following reasons:

1. The report’s status is **Processing** or **Failed**. You can email any **Ready** AQ Insights reports.
2. The **Send Email** button is disabled. If you can access the **Email Audience Quality** pop-up window, but the **Send Email** button is disabled, note that you must enter valid email aliases to send the report to the recipients you specified. If you completed the field but the button is still disabled, you likely only added one email alias. You’ll need to click anywhere within the **Email Audience Quality** window, and outside of the **Email ID** field, for it to register. This will enable the **Send Email** button automatically.

article_title: Troubleshoot an Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report
context_header: Troubleshoot an Audience Quality (AQ) Insights report › AQ Insights report results troubleshooting
text:
### Cannot download a report

The **Audience Quality** page of the Insights app displays each of your AQ Insights reports and their statuses: **Ready**, **Processing**, and **Failed**. You can download any **Ready** reports by following the steps outlined in [Download an AQ Insights report](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13132289-generate-or-manage-an-audience-quality-aq-insights-report#h_8051e9e5c1).

### Cannot edit or duplicate a report

Editing and duplication are not currently supported for AQ Insights reports.

### AQ Insights report generation failed

You encountered a technical error during report generation. Try again in a few minutes.

Note that, if an AQ Insights report features a **Failed** status, no **AQ Cost** will be deducted from the advertiser’s account balance until it successfully generates.

context_header: Custom Voter audience overview › Custom Voter audience overview
text:
## Custom Voter audience overview

Custom Voter audiences help ensure your political campaigns reach the right users. These audiences are built using voter segments, and are customized based on locations, districts, demographics, party registration, early and absentee voting status, and more.

When you create a Custom Voter audience, you’ll manually select data segments to customize your audience across a number of voter dimensions. You can also take advantage of AI-powered audience generation. Regardless of your approach, you’ll have an opportunity to reviewinsights into the audience’s reach and demographic details, and apply any changes before generating it.

Refer to [Create or manage a Custom Voter audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336749-create-or-manage-a-custom-voter-audience) to get started.

context_header: Custom Voter audience overview › Custom Voter Audience eligibility requirements
text:
## Custom Voter Audience eligibility requirements

Political advertisers are eligible to create a Custom Voter audience. A campaign must also meet each of these conditions before it becomes eligible for Custom Voter audience targeting.

| **Requirement type** | **Requirement details** |
| --- | --- |
| **Campaign vertical** | Political |
| **Campaign type** | Advanced |
| **Campaign status** | Draft Running Expired Paused |
| **Audience status** | Processing Ready |
| **Audience type*** | Matched Segmented Retargeted Geofarmed Contextual Lookalike Campaign Pre-bid |
| **Audience Potential Reach** | 100 or greater |

***Audience type:** A single campaign can target any combination of the listed audiences. Up to 20 audiences per campaign are supported.

context_header: Custom Voter audience overview › Custom Voter audience statuses
text:
## Custom Voter audience statuses

You can review a Custom Voter audience’s status on the **Custom Voter Audience** page of the Audiences app. Refer to [Review a Custom Voter audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336749-create-or-manage-a-custom-voter-audience#h_34cdd0ed35) for more information on how to access this page.

| **Status** | **Definition** |
| --- | --- |
| **Ready** | Your audience is generated. You can review or manage the audience and [assign it to a campaign](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/11497815-assign-an-audience-to-a-campaign). |
| **Processing** | We’re working on generating your audience. Depending on the audience’s size, this process may take up to 48 hours. |
| **Failed** | You encountered a technical error during audience creation. Attempt to generate it again, or [duplicate](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336749-create-or-manage-a-custom-voter-audience#h_2ab985186c) the audience to create a new one with different settings. |
| **Deleted** | Deleted audiences are automatically removed from the Audiences app as soon as you complete this action. For this reason, none of your Custom Voter audiences will feature a **Deleted** status at any time. |

context_header: Custom Voter audience overview › Custom Voter audience pricing
text:
## Custom Voter audience pricing

Custom Voter audiences each display a CPM price. Note that there’s no cost associated with generating a Custom Voter audience. Instead, the listed CPM price will apply once you run a campaign that’s targeting the Custom Voter audience.

You can review the CPM cost of targeting a given Custom Voter audience once it finishes generating and features a **Ready** status. Refer to [Review a Custom Voter audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336749-create-or-manage-a-custom-voter-audience#h_34cdd0ed35) to learn how to locate an audience’s cost details.

context_header: Custom Voter audience overview › Key terms and concepts › AI-powered audience generation
text:
### AI-powered audience generation

When you create a Custom Voter audience, you’ll manually add your desired audience segments. These segments allow you to customize your audience across a number of voter dimensions such as locations, districts, demographics, party registration, and more.

To save time and simplify the process, you have the option to enter a description of your audience via an **AI Assist** chat box instead. You can also select a pre-loaded description for inspiration. Either option will begin building a Custom Voter audience for you that’s powered by AI, after which you can apply your requirements and create the audience.

You’ll have an opportunity to review the AI-generated segment selections and add or remove any selections to further customize your audience. Refer to [Create or manage a Custom Voter audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336749-create-or-manage-a-custom-voter-audience) to get started with AI-powered audience generation.

context_header: Custom Voter audience overview › Key terms and concepts › Map view
text:
### Map view

Your Custom Voter audience includes a **Map** view providing graphic insights into the audience’s voter density. Along with surfacing **Potential Reach** details, it compares the targetable audience size to the total addressable audience to determine whether it’s **Broad**, **Moderate**, or **Specific**.

| **Audience size** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| **Broad** | The targetable audience is greater than or equal to 70% of the total addressable audience. |
| **Moderate** | The targetable audience is greater than 30%, but less than 70%, of the total addressable audience. |
| **Specific** | The targetable audience is less than or equal to 30% of the total addressable audience. |

The **Map** view also includes the distribution of **Republicans**, **Democrats**, and **Others** for the selected audience segments.

context_header: Custom Voter audience overview › Key terms and concepts › Insights view
text:
### Insights view

Your Custom Voter audience’s **Insights** tab includes graphic insights into the audience’s voter pool.

| **Insight** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| **Party Registration** | An interactive graph illustrating the audience’s political-affiliation distribution based on party registration across **Republican**, **Democrat**, **Unaffiliated**, and **Others** categories. |
| **Gender** | An interactive graph illustrating the audience’s gender distribution across **Female**, **Male**, **Unknown**, and **Gender Expansive** categories. |
| **Urbanity** | An interactive graph illustrating the audience’s geographic classification across **Urban**, **Rural**, and **Suburban** categories. |
| **Age** | An interactive graph illustrating the audience’s age distribution across the **18-29, 30-39**, **40-49**, **50-64**, **65+**, and **Unknown** age ranges. |
| **Ethnicity** | An interactive graph illustrating the audience’s ethnicity distribution across its top-five ethnicities. |
| **Reach** | A metric representing the estimated number of unique voters and constituents that are available for targeting. |

context_header: Custom Voter audience overview › Key terms and concepts › Segment Groups and relationships
text:
### Segment Groups and relationships

You can customize the targeting logic for your Custom Voter audience. This includes deciding between an “AND” or an “OR” relationship among each **Segment Group**, and between the individual audience segments included in those **Segment Groups**.

| **Item** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| **Segment Group (parent group)** | A bucket containing one or more audience segments that share a relationship type (“AND” or “OR”). |
| **Segment Sub-group** **(child group)** | A child bucket containing one or more audience segments that share a relationship type (“AND” or “OR”), which is nested within a parent Segment Group. This nested approach allows for more possibilities when logically grouping segments, and typically applies when using AI-powered audience generation. |
| **Segment** | A specific subgroup of users based on their shared characteristics. |
| **“AND” relationship** | The user must meet all conditions to be eligible for targeting. |
| **“OR” relationship** | A user must meet at least one condition to be eligible for targeting. |

Note that “AND” relationships can impact an audience’s scale because they’re more restrictive than “OR” relationships. To help avoid interruptions to your campaign’s ability to spend, review the audience’s estimated **Potential Reach** details prior to targeting it.

context_header: Custom Voter audience overview › Key terms and concepts › Segment Groups and relationships › Examples: Segment Groups and relationships
text:
#### Examples: Segment Groups and relationships

Refer to the scenarios below for more information on which users would be reachable based on a Custom Voter audience’s Segment Groups and relationship settings.

| **Segment Groups and relationships** | **Targetable users** |
| --- | --- |
|  | A user is eligible for targeting when any of these conditions are met: Female in New Mexico **and** voted in the 11/05/2025 New Mexico general election; Female in New Mexico **and** returned a ballot early by mail; Male in Wyoming **and** voted in the 11/05/2025 New Mexico general election; Male in Wyoming **and** returned a ballot early by mail in New Mexico |
|  | A user is eligible for targeting when any of these conditions are met: Female in New Mexico; Male in Wyoming; Voted in the 11/05/2025 New Mexico general election **and** returned a ballot early by mail |
|  | A user is eligible for targeting when any of these conditions are met: Female in New Mexico; Male in Wyoming; Voted in the 11/05/2025 New Mexico general election; Returned a ballot early by mail in New Mexico Since the relationship is the same between each Segment Group and segment (“OR”), the advertiser could have created a single Segment Group instead of two. |

section_path: Early voter and absentee ballot (AB-EV) segments
context_header: Custom Voter audience overview › Key terms and concepts › Early voter and absentee ballot (AB-EV) segments
text:
### Early voter and absentee ballot (AB-EV) segments

Early voter and absentee ballot (AB-EV) segments separate voters who’ve already cast a ballot, either by voting early or by returning an absentee ballot, from those who haven’t. This data comes from L2, and it’s available for states that publicly release individual-level early voting and absentee ballot records.

Combine AB-EV segments with your audience’s location, partisan lean, and demographic segments to build ballot-chasing audiences. For example, target likely supporters in a district, and exclude voters who’ve already voted early or returned an absentee ballot, so your campaign focuses on the voters who still need to act. The audience’s **Potential Reach** reflects any AB-EV segments you exclude.

To locate AB-EV segments, expand the desired state when you add segments, then open its **Early Voters/Absentee Ballot** subsection. Refer to [Create with voter segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336749-create-or-manage-a-custom-voter-audience#h_7f8710f69d) for step-by-step instructions.

article_title: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience
context_header: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience › Custom Voter audience overview
text:
## Custom Voter audience overview

Generate Custom Voter audiences to reach the right users with your political campaigns. These audiences are built using voter segments, and are customized based on locations, districts, demographics, party registration, and more. You can also utilize AI-powered audience generation tools, and review insights into the audience’s reach before finalizing any requirements.

Refer to [Custom Voter Audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336712-custom-voter-audience-overview) for more information and eligibility requirements, or continue reading to create and manage a Custom Voter audience in the IQM platform.

article_title: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience
context_header: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience › Create a Custom Voter audience
text:
## Create a Custom Voter audience

You can use the Audiences app to create one Custom Voter audience at a time, and in the following ways:

- Using voter segments
- Using AI assist

You can also use a combination of these options; for example, you might prompt AI to create an initial set of segment selections for your audience, then manually choose additional ones.

Follow these steps to access the **+ Create Audience** workflow:

1. Open the Audiences app.
2. Select **Custom Voter Audience**.
3. Click **+ Create New**. This will open the **Create Custom Voter Audience** pop-up window.

article_title: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience
context_header: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience › Create a Custom Voter audience › Create with voter segments
text:
### Create with voter segments

Follow these steps to create a Custom Voter audience from individual voter segment selections:

1. Enter a name for the audience.
2. Search or browse and select the state(s) where your target audience is located.
   1. If needed, click the trashcan icon in the **Actions** column of a state to deselect it.
3. Select **Continue**.
4. Select the **Voter Segments** tab.
5. Click **+ Segments** to search or browse and select voter segments.
   1. Choose whether the segments in the Segment Group are assigned an [“OR” or “AND” relationship](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336712-custom-voter-audience-overview#h_4d221fa72d).
   2. To add early voter and absentee ballot (AB-EV) segments, expand the desired state, then browse and select segments in its **Early Voters/Absentee Ballot** subsection. Refer to [Early voter and absentee ballot (AB-EV) segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336712-custom-voter-audience-overview#h_51bae67c51) for more information.
6. If desired, select **+ Group** within the Segment Group to add more granular conditions with a nested logic applied.
   1. Choose whether the segments in the Segment Sub-group are assigned an [“OR” or “AND” relationship](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336712-custom-voter-audience-overview#h_4d221fa72d).

article_title: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience
context_header: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience › Create a Custom Voter audience › Create with voter segments
text:
### Create with voter segments

Follow these steps to create a Custom Voter audience from individual voter segment selections:

7. If desired, select **+ Group** outside of the first Segment Sub-group to create a new group.
   1. Repeat steps 5 and 6 to select the segments you’d like to add to the second Segment Group and any applicable sub-groups.
8. If the audience includes more than one Segment Group, choose the relationship between them.
9. For each Segment Group and any sub-groups, choose whether a user should be included or excluded based on whether they meet the selected criteria.
   1. Leave a toggle switch as is (green and to the right) to include users that meet the selected criteria.
   2. Select a toggle switch once (red and to the left) to exclude users that meet the selected criteria.
   3. For example, to build a ballot-chasing audience, exclude a Segment Group containing the AB-EV segments for voters who’ve already voted early or returned an absentee ballot, so your campaign focuses on the voters who still need to act.
10. Select **Apply**.
11. In the **Map** tab, compare the audience’s **Potential Reach**, **Audience Size**, and distribution of party affiliations.
    1. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Map view](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336712-custom-voter-audience-overview#h_a6276b09bd) for more details.
12. In the **Insights** tab, review graphic insights into the audience’s voter pool.
    1. Refer to [Key terms and concepts: Insights view](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336712-custom-voter-audience-overview#h_f37ff0697e) for more details.
13. Select **Create Audience** to generate the Custom Voter audience.

Your Custom Voter audience will immediately begin processing. You can monitor its current status by following the steps outlined in Review a Custom Voter audience.

article_title: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience
context_header: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience › Create a Custom Voter audience › Create with AI assist
text:
### Create with AI assist

Follow these steps to use AI to select the appropriate voter audience segments based on your criteria:

1. Enter a name for the audience.
   1. Choose a unique one to differentiate this audience from others that you may create.
2. Search or browse and select the state(s) where your target audience is located.
3. Click **Continue**.
4. Select the **AI Assist** tab.
5. Specify your audience requirements.
   1. If desired, select a chat preset.
   2. Describe your audience’s characteristics and select the arrow icon.
   3. Repeat this process to add additional requirements, as needed.
   4. Select **Apply**. This will automatically select the voter segments that match your audience requirements.
6. Select the **Voter Segments** tab.
7. Follow steps 5 through 13 of the Create with voter segments workflow to review the auto-selected segments and their potential reach; make any adjustments, if desired; and create the Custom Voter audience.

Your Custom Voter audience will immediately begin processing. You can monitor its current status by following the steps outlined in Review a Custom Voter audience.

article_title: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience
context_header: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience › Manage a Custom Voter audience
text:
## Manage a Custom Voter audience

Use the **Custom Voter Audience** page of the Audiences app to review, search, sort, or filter your existing audiences. You can also use this page to duplicate or delete them, and assign them to campaigns.

article_title: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience
context_header: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience › Manage a Custom Voter audience › Review a Custom Voter audience
text:
### Review a Custom Voter audience

Follow these steps to locate and review an existing Custom Voter audience.

1. Locate the audience you’d like to review.
   1. Search by **ID** or **Audience Name**.
   2. Filter by **Status**.
   3. Open the column selector to add or remove a table column.
2. Select the desired audience ID in the **ID** column. This will open the audience.
3. Review the settings you specified when you created the audience and related insights.
   1. Review the audience’s Segment Groups and segments, and the relationships between them, in the **Voter Segments** panel.
   2. Review the audience’s **Potential Reach**, **Audience Size**, and distribution of party affiliations in the **Map** tab.
   3. Review graphic insights into the audience’s voter pool in the **Insights** tab.
4. Close the audience pop-up window to return to the **Custom Voter Audience** page.

article_title: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience
context_header: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience › Manage a Custom Voter audience
text:
### Edit a Custom Voter audience

Editing is not currently supported for Custom Voter audiences. We recommend duplicating an existing audience to start from an existing audience’s settings.

### Duplicate a Custom Voter audience

You can duplicate one **Ready**, **Processing**, or **Failed** audience at a time, and in the following ways:

- From the table
- From the audience preview

article_title: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience
context_header: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience › Manage a Custom Voter audience › Duplicate a Custom Voter audience › Duplicate from the table
text:
#### Duplicate from the table

Follow these steps to duplicate an existing Custom Voter audience from the **Custom Voter Audience** table.

1. Select the page icon from the desired audience’s **Actions** column.
2. The new audience will include the same state and segment selections as the original audience.
   1. Click **Edit States** to modify the audience’s state selection.
   2. Select the trashcan icon next to a Segment Group to remove it from the audience.
   3. Select the trashcan icon next to a segment to remove it from a Segment Group.
   4. Follow the steps outlined in Create with voter segments or Create with AI assist to create new Segment Groups, add segments to them, and choose the relationships between them.
3. Click **Apply** to update the data included in the audience’s **Map** and **Insights** tabs.
4. Select **Create** to generate the Custom Voter audience.

The duplicated audience will appear in the **Custom Voter Audience** table of the Audiences app. The original audience will remain unchanged.

article_title: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience
context_header: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience › Manage a Custom Voter audience › Duplicate a Custom Voter audience › Duplicate from the audience preview
text:
#### Duplicate from the audience preview

Follow these steps to duplicate an existing Custom Voter audience while reviewing that existing audience:

1. Select the desired audience’s ID in the **ID** column. This will open the audience.
2. Select the vertical ellipses.
3. Click **Duplicate**. This will open the **Duplicate Custom Voter Audience** pop-up window.
4. Enter a name for the audience.
5. Select **Duplicate**.
6. Follow steps 2 through 4 of the Duplicate from the table workflow.

The duplicated audience will appear in the **Custom Voter Audience** table of the Audiences app. The original audience will remain unchanged.

article_title: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience
context_header: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience › Manage a Custom Voter audience › Delete a Custom Voter audience
text:
### Delete a Custom Voter audience

> **Audience deletion notice:** Note that deleted audiences are unrecoverable, and this action is permanent. As a safeguard, consider duplicating and updating the audience to reflect any desired changes.

You can delete Custom Voter audiences individually or in bulk. They must feature a **Ready**, **Processing**, or **Failed** status; and their **Allowlist/Blocklist** count must be **0**.

Delete a Custom Voter audience in the following ways:

- From the table
- From the audience

article_title: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience
context_header: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience › Manage a Custom Voter audience › Delete a Custom Voter audience
text:
#### Delete from the table

Follow these steps to delete an existing Custom Voter audience from the **Custom Voter Audience** table.

1. To delete audiences individually, use the **Actions** column to select the trash can icon next to the individual audience that you’d like to delete.
2. To delete audiences in bulk:
   1. Select the checkbox(es) next to the desired audience(s).
   2. Click **Delete**.

The deleted audience(s) will no longer appear in the Audiences app.

#### Delete from the audience

Follow these steps to delete an existing Custom Voter audience while reviewing that existing audience:

1. Select the desired audience’s ID in the **ID** column. This will open the audience.
2. Select the vertical ellipses.
3. Click **Delete**.

The deleted audience will no longer appear in the Audiences app.

You can review a campaigns’ data costs in the following ways:

- From the Dashboard app

article_title: Create or manage a Custom Voter audience

context_header: Troubleshoot a Custom Voter audience › Custom Voter audience troubleshooting overview
text:
## Custom Voter audience troubleshooting overview

Certain advertisers can create and target Custom Voter audiences if their account and campaign meet certain eligibility criteria. They must also follow specific steps to successfully create an audience and assign it to a campaign.

If you encounter an error or are blocked from creating, managing, or targeting a Custom Voter audience, refer to these resources first:

- [Custom Voter audience overview](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336712-custom-voter-audience-overview)
- [Create or manage a Custom Voter audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336749-create-or-manage-a-custom-voter-audience)

Return to this article to address and resolve other issues that you may encounter related to Custom Voter audiences.

section_path: Troubleshoot Custom Voter audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Custom Voter audience › Troubleshoot Custom Voter audience creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to duplicate an audience

**Ready**, **Processing**, or **Failed** Custom Voter audiences can be duplicated by following the steps outlined in [Duplicate a Custom Voter audience](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336749-create-or-manage-a-custom-voter-audience#h_2ab985186c).

### Unable to edit an audience

Editing isn’t currently supported for Custom Voter audiences. Consider duplicating the audience instead. You’ll have an opportunity to rename the audience, add or remove selected states and audience segments, and save those changes to a new audience.

### Unable to delete an audience

You can delete audiences individually or in bulk. Every selected audience must be unassigned from all campaigns before you can delete them.

You can easily reference whether an audience is assigned to any campaigns in the **Allowlist/Blocklist** column. Audiences with an **Allowlist/Blocklist** value of **0** can be deleted.

section_path: Troubleshoot Custom Voter audience creation or management issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Custom Voter audience › Troubleshoot Custom Voter audience creation or management issues
text:
### Unable to locate a deleted audience

Deleted audiences are automatically removed from the Audiences app as soon as you complete this action. For this reason, none of the Custom Voter audiences listed in the Audiences app will feature a **Deleted** status.

### Custom Voter audience option is missing in Campaigns app

Custom Voter audience creation is enabled for Political advertisers. Confirm that your account and campaign meet Custom Voter audience [eligibility requirements](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336712-custom-voter-audience-overview#h_311c647cdf), and contact IQM’s support personnel if you believe that you should have access.

Unable to locate early voter or absentee ballot segments
context_header: Troubleshoot a Custom Voter audience › Troubleshoot Custom Voter audience creation or management issues › Unable to locate early voter or absentee ballot segments
text:
### Unable to locate early voter or absentee ballot segments

Early voter and absentee ballot (AB-EV) segments are organized by state. When you add segments, expand the desired state, then open its **Early Voters/Absentee Ballot** subsection. If you’ve selected all states for the audience, then the **Early Voters/Absentee Ballot** option is available as its own menu. Refer to [Create with voter segments](https://help.iqm.com/en/articles/13336749-create-or-manage-a-custom-voter-audience#h_7f8710f69d) for step-by-step instructions.

If a state doesn’t include an **Early Voters/Absentee Ballot** subsection, AB-EV data isn’t available for that state. AB-EV segments are only available for states that publicly release individual-level early voting and absentee ballot records.

section_path: Troubleshoot Custom Voter audience targeting issues
context_header: Troubleshoot a Custom Voter audience › Troubleshoot Custom Voter audience targeting issues
text:
### New campaign - Unable to select a PG campaign type

PG campaigns aren’t eligible for Custom Voter audience targeting. When you create a new campaign targeting a Custom Voter audience, the **Advanced** option is selected by default, and the **PG** option is disabled.

### Existing campaign - Unable to add to a PG campaign

Only Advanced campaigns are eligible for targeting Custom Voter audiences.

### Existing campaign - Campaign is missing from list
